designs.name: Keel: one slow-trend rule inside a heavy protection shell (Python/ccxt on Binance XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT perpetuals)
designs.thesis:
What the open-source field is worth is plumbing, not signals. In the 264 EAs audited, 100% carry red flags, 18% of trading EAs are grid or martingale (27% of the gold/silver-titled ones), only 106 of 206 always send a hard stop, and 10 of 264 reach quality 5. The research says the same from the other side: single-instrument trend following is not a statistically established edge (very_likely), session breakouts on gold have no peer-reviewed cost-inclusive support (very_likely, fact-check partially supported), volatility sizing is risk control and not alpha (confirmed), and 74-89% of retail leveraged accounts lose (confirmed).

So this proposal reads 'gather the features of all the open-source bots' as: take every catalog feature marked core that protects the account or makes a test honest, re-implement it from a written spec (ideas only, no Code Base code copied or translated, provenance log kept), and attach the smallest possible strategy surface: one slow, symmetric, three-parameter trend rule with no optimiser, plus one challenger that runs in shadow only. The default assumption is zero edge minus costs. The bot's job is to bound losses and to produce records that can show whether that assumption is wrong.

The shell is not a theoretical need. I read the requester's current bot (/home/user/Basel-Almubarak/pro-scalping-bot.zip) and it has the catalog's listed mistakes:
- src/risk.py position_size() computes the stop distance and then ignores it: qty = balance x risk_pct x leverage / entry. Notional is a fixed 10% of free balance, so '1% risk per trade' is not what is traded.
- RiskManager.record_trade() is never called from src/bot.py, so the 5% daily loss stop and the loss-streak throttle can never fire.
- src/strategy.py reads the forming bar (df.iloc[-1] of fetch_ohlcv), so signals repaint inside the bar.
- src/broker.py only logs a failed stop-loss order, leaving the position naked; stops are computed from the signal price, not the fill.
- Open-position state, daily counters and the halt flag live in memory while railway.json restarts the process on failure; nothing is rebuilt from the exchange.
- close_all() closes every position on the account in one pass with no retry.

Every one of these is fixed by a named core feature below, and the same shell can later be back-ported to the crypto bot.
designs.platform:
Python 3.11 + ccxt (pinned, >= 4.5.92) trading Binance USD-M perpetuals XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT, run as a second Railway worker beside the existing bot, in a dedicated Binance sub-account, with a small persistent store (SQLite on a Railway volume, or Postgres). One venue adapter, one code base, no MQL5 in v1. The catalog is MQL5-specific in vocabulary only; each core feature is re-implemented in venue terms: exchange filters instead of symbol properties, sub-account plus clientOrderId prefix instead of magic number, income history instead of deal history, funding instead of swap.

Why not an MT5 EA, the home of all 264 sources:
1. Capital arithmetic. The only strategy family with long evidence is slow trend, whose volatility stop today is about $270-290 per ounce of gold (3 x a daily ATR of about $90-95, confirmed). At a 0.01-lot minimum of 1 oz that needs roughly $54,000 of equity to keep risk at 0.50%, so on a small CFD account 'Never-round-up lot normalisation' would skip every trade. Binance's reported 0.001 oz increment makes the same rule tradable from a few hundred USDT. Capital is unknown, so the venue where the risk rule can be satisfied at any size is the robust choice.
2. Costs fit the holding period. Binance is fee-dominated: about 10 bps per taker round trip against a one-tick spread (likely; the account's own rate is unverified). That is about 1.5% of R on a 7% stop and irrelevant at roughly ten trades a year. It would be fatal for intraday work, which v1 therefore does not trade.
3. Honest testing is simpler here for a daily rule. No tick model is needed; Python's zoneinfo gives correct New York sessions in replay and live (the MT5 tester makes TimeGMT equal server time, has no calendar, and appears to apply today's swap to all history); the venue publishes its own trade, funding and depth history.
4. The requester can read every line, and the deployment (Procfile, railway.json, ccxt) already exists.

What this choice costs: the contracts are 11 months old and their off-hours pricing rules changed twice in 2026; access is jurisdiction-gated and geo-blocked; profit and loss are in USDT; funding has cost longs roughly 6-11% a year recently and far more in January 2026; the MT5 Strategy Tester is given up.

Assumptions, each checked in Phase 0. If one fails, stop and re-decide the venue instead of coding against a guess:
A1. The account is eligible for TradFi perps and the agreement can be signed (country list not verified).
A2. The sub-account holds at least 500 USDT; capital is otherwise unknown.
A3. Taker fee is about 0.05% per side.
A4. Tick 0.01, step 0.001 oz, min notional 5 USDT and leverage brackets are read live; all are unverified because exchangeInfo returned HTTP 451 to the researchers.
A5. The Railway region is one Binance serves, and persistent storage is attached.
A6. Spot daily history is an acceptable proxy for the perp for a daily-bar rule (tested by the overlap gate).

Fallbacks if A1 fails: the same spec on OKX XAU-USDT-SWAP / XAG-USDT-SWAP through ccxt (about a tenth of Binance's gold volume, every venue fact re-measured), or an MT5 EA at a regulated broker if equity is near $54,000 or the broker offers sub-ounce lots.

strategies.name: TREND-D1 (the only live candidate)
strategies.logic: Fixed inputs, not optimised: N = 63 NY-day bars, ATR period 20 (Wilder, true range), k = 3.0. Index 1 is the last closed NY-day bar. Channel: HH(i) = highest high of bars i+1..i+N; LL(i) = lowest low of the same bars. Long trigger: close[1] > HH(1) and close[2] <= HH(2). Short trigger: close[1] < LL(1) and close[2] >= LL(2). The condition must be new on bar 1. Preconditions: no own position and no live intent on the symbol; a trigger while a position is open is logged SKIP(position_open) and never reverses. Delivery: the intent is created at the 17:00 New York close and sent as one market order in the 20:00-22:00 New York window that evening (Sunday 20:00-22:00 for Friday's bar), with up to 3 attempts on transient errors at least 60 s apart; it expires at 22:00. It is skipped if |mid - close[1]| > 1.0 x ATR20 (late or gapped) or if any gate vetoes. Initial stop: fill price minus (long) or plus (short) k x ATR20[1], rounded to tick, as a server-side reduce-only stop-market order confirmed by read-back within 5 s; otherwise the position is closed. Exit: chandelier only. After each NY-day close, candidate = highest close since entry - k x ATR20[1] (mirrored for shorts); the stop becomes max(current, candidate) for longs and moves only if the improvement is at least 0.1 x ATR20; it is never widened. No take-profit, breakeven, partials or time stop; positions are held over weekends and releases by design, and are sized for that. Pre-registered sensitivity grid, all 24 cells reported and counted as trials: N in {21, 63, 126, 252} x k in {2, 3, 4} x 12-month-sign filter {off, on} (filter: longs only if close[1] > close[253], shorts only if below). Primary cell: 63 / 3 / off.
strategies.timeframe: D1, defined as the New York trading day (18:00 to 17:00 America/New_York, Monday to Friday), built from 1h klines. Evaluated once per closed bar.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT perpetuals with identical parameters. Silver runs at half the risk of gold, and same-direction positions in both count as one bet. Each metal gets its own go/no-go in validation.
strategies.rationale: Slow trend following is the only family in the research with long, multi-source evidence (confirmed), and the research implication is a 1-12 month signal with volatility-based sizing; 63 days sits in the middle of that band and the grid spans 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. The entry is the catalog's 'Fresh closed-bar trend trigger' in the channel form used by the best-coded gold EA in the sample (77691, quality 5), minus its long-only default, which its own header admits was chosen because shorts lost in 2020-2026. The exit is 'Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop', the best-supported trail in the catalog. Three parameters, no optimiser, closed bars only, so backtest and live cannot disagree about signals. Limits stated up front: per-instrument trend is not statistically established (very_likely), static trend had a Sharpe near zero in 2009-2022 (confirmed, diversified portfolios), and the ATR stop adds no edge of its own (confirmed for volatility scaling in commodities). The wide stop means small notional (about 7% of equity in gold, 2% in silver), which is what makes fees, weekend gaps and a 30 January 2026 type session survivable.

strategies.name: RANGE-NY (challenger, shadow only, not evidence-backed)
strategies.logic: In v1 this is computed and journalled in MONITOR mode with simulated fills and sends no orders. Times are America/New_York. Range: high and low of 1-minute bars from 02:00 to 08:00, frozen at 08:00; the day is void if fewer than 90% of bars are present. Width W = high - low. Day filters: 0.20 <= W / ATR14(NY-day) <= 0.80; W >= 20 x current spread; no NFP, CPI, PCE or FOMC on that date (UTC-stamped CSV, also used in replay). Trigger: the first closed M15 bar between 08:00 and 11:00 whose close is above high + 0.10 W (long) or below low - 0.10 W (short). One attempt per symbol per day; the day key is consumed even when a gate vetoes. Simulated entry: next bar open plus the recorded half-spread plus a 5 bps fee per side. Stop: opposite range edge. Target: 1.5R. Net-RR gate: (target - costs) / (stop + costs) >= 1.2. Time exit: flat at 15:45. All constants are fixed in advance; changing one is a new trial.
strategies.timeframe: Range from M1 bars, signal on closed M15 bars, intraday only, flat before the thin 16:00-19:00 New York hours.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT first. XAGUSDT is journalled separately; its 0.01 tick is about 2 bps of price, so costs are worse.
strategies.rationale: Session-range breakout is what the better-coded gold EAs in the sample actually do (75586, 76153, 78688, 78293, 17465), and the catalog's core entry features ('Session/opening range builder from M1 bars', 'Closed-bar range breakout with buffer and entry window', 'Range-width and compression gate') are built around it, so it deserves an honest test and not faith or dismissal. The window follows the measured session structure: activity peaks 08:00-11:00 New York and no London-open surge is visible in 2026 (very_likely; the fact-check confirms the ordering of hours). The prior is that it fails: there is no peer-reviewed cost-inclusive gold result, an index-CFD replication found the edge consumed by costs, and on this venue 10 bps of fees is 5-20% of R against a 50-200 bps stop. It ships disabled, is built last, and is deleted after 6 months unless it clears the promotion gate in the validation plan.

features_excluded.feature: Grid, martingale, averaging down, recovery baskets and their exits (Basket / aggregate exits; Basket money / equity-ratio take-profit close-all; Grid-basket rescue devices; lot multiplication after losses)
features_excluded.why: No edge of their own and a documented path to ruin (very_likely). They are 18% of trading EAs and 27% of gold/silver-titled ones, mostly without a broker-side stop. A single session on 30 January 2026 moved gold about 9-12% and silver 26-31%, which no grid spacing survives. The code will contain no path that adds to a losing position.

features_excluded.feature: Weighted additive confluence score gate; Weighted-score voting; Composite 0-100 risk score; the current bot's five-confirmation EMA/RSI/MACD/volume stack with its 'score'
features_excluded.why: Arbitrary weights and correlated conditions that cannot be ablated (overfit 5). Independent boolean gates with reason codes replace them. The existing entry logic is not ported: it stacks filters, reads the forming bar, and belongs to a 5-minute horizon that this venue's fees do not support.

features_excluded.feature: Any parameter optimiser: genetic or best-of-grid search, walk-forward re-optimisation, Staged optimisation switch, Count-based or drawdown-rescaled fitness formulas
features_excluded.why: With about 5 years of data roughly 45 independent trials are enough to produce a zero-skill in-sample Sharpe of 1 (confirmed). Parameters are fixed in advance; the 24-cell grid is a sensitivity report read by its median, not a search for the best cell.

features_excluded.feature: Self-optimising and learned signal generators; Veto-only model confirmation layer (ML or LLM)
features_excluded.why: In-sample fitting running continuously, hidden state, unreproducible tests (overfit 4-5). Nothing in the research shows a model-based edge on metals that survives costs.

features_excluded.feature: Live intraday or scalping strategies on this venue, including tick-driven triggers and the Tick-velocity fast-market detector
features_excluded.why: About 10 bps per taker round trip is roughly an order of magnitude above a raw-spread CFD (likely), while documented intraday gold edges are a few bps gross per trade. Tick logic also depends on the feed and cannot be tested honestly. RANGE-NY is allowed only in shadow.

features_excluded.feature: Oscillator zone-exit / band re-entry reversal trigger and other short-horizon mean reversion
features_excluded.why: No cost-surviving evidence on gold or silver; the limited evidence points to continuation after large moves (likely). In the sample these triggers mostly ride on averaging baskets.

features_excluded.feature: Pending-order entries: Two-sided pending stop bracket with OCO, news straddles and other price-chasing or stacked pendings, Pending-to-market fallback
features_excluded.why: Stop-order fills at the worst moments cannot be modelled, and OCO and expiry add failure paths. v1 enters at market on a closed bar only, so the cost is visible in the test instead of hidden.

features_excluded.feature: Liquidity sweep-and-reclaim, Fair value gap / order-block zone retest, Scale-free candle-quality metrics as confirmation
features_excluded.why: Second and third strategies with many definitional choices and thresholds (overfit 3-4). A minimal design carries one live entry engine; these can be proposed later as pre-registered shadow challengers.

features_excluded.feature: Cross-symbol directional proxy and gold/silver ratio pairs trading
features_excluded.why: The cointegration link is unstable and the reversion trade has failed for years at a time (very_likely, fact-check partially supported). It would also couple the two symbols' risk accounting.

features_excluded.feature: Virtual / stealth SL-TP
features_excluded.why: A stop that exists only in the process disappears when Railway restarts it. The invariant is a confirmed server-side stop on every position.

features_excluded.feature: Breakeven with net-of-cost lock offset, Scale-out ladder in R-multiples, Pyramiding into profit, Secondary profit-lock ratchets, and any take-profit on the trend rule
features_excluded.why: Each adds fitted thresholds and mostly improves win rate, not net R. The trend rule has one exit; plain chandelier is the baseline any later exit must beat out of sample.

features_excluded.feature: Duplex long/short parameter sets, per-metal tuned presets, long-only default
features_excluded.why: Long/short asymmetry fitted on 2015-2026 memorises the gold bull market (likely). One symmetric parameter set serves both metals; silver differs only in risk. The long/short switches exist for operations and diagnostics, not tuning.

features_excluded.feature: Scaling size up by signal confidence, Kelly or win streaks; Loss-streak risk throttle; Guarded minimum-lot fallback
features_excluded.why: Flat risk keeps every trade equally weighted in the test. With about ten trades a year there is no sample to estimate a streak effect. Below minimum size the trade is skipped, never rounded up.

features_excluded.feature: Daily profit stop, Equity / basket profit giveback ratchet
features_excluded.why: Fitted exits presented as protection; they cut the few large trend days that carry a trend system.

features_excluded.feature: Extra regime filters: Compression/expansion day filters, Over-extension filter, more than one trend filter, tick-volume conditions
features_excluded.why: The catalog's own rule is one filter with a switch and a no-filter control. The only filter here is the 12-month sign, and it is off in the primary cell.

features_excluded.feature: Runtime strategy overrides, manual trade buttons, User-drawn chart objects as triggers, Remote command queue, chart UI
features_excluded.why: They make the live system differ from the tested one and add an attack surface on a live account. Control is a host-side CLI limited to risk-reducing actions.

features_excluded.feature: MT5/MQL5 EA, CFD broker account, the MetaTrader5 Python package, MT4/MT5 macro layer, Generic indicator-to-signal adapter in v1
features_excluded.why: A slow-trend stop needs about $54,000 at a 1 oz minimum; the Python package is Windows-only and cannot run on Railway (confirmed); a second code base doubles the test surface. Kept as a documented fallback, not built.

features_excluded.feature: News blackout from the native MT5 economic calendar, WebRequest calendar fetch, Adaptive spread cap
features_excluded.why: The trend rule only enters at 20:00-22:00 New York, when no scheduled US release occurs, so it needs no news filter. RANGE-NY uses a hand-checkable UTC CSV that also works in replay. Adaptive caps can normalise bad conditions; thresholds stay fixed and the recorder only measures.

features_excluded.feature: Weekend entries, PAXG as a gold proxy, a second venue
features_excluded.why: Weekend volume is 6-16% of weekday volume and the index mechanics differ; PAXG's basis wandered about -0.4% to +0.2%; a second venue means a second set of unverified contract rules.

features_excluded.feature: Copying, translating or bulk-downloading MQL5 Code Base source
features_excluded.why: Unlicensed Code Base files are best treated as all rights reserved, translation is a restricted act, and the site terms forbid automated access (confirmed for the clause texts; research, not legal advice). Features are re-implemented from a written spec with a provenance log.

designs.risk_model:
All numbers are policy defaults fixed in advance. None is optimised.

Isolation
- Dedicated Binance sub-account holding only this bot's USDT; symbol whitelist XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT; one-way mode; cross margin inside the sub-account; exchange leverage set to 2x as a hard order-size ceiling.
- If sub-accounts are unavailable: clientOrderId prefix plus an equity-allocation input, and the crypto bot's close_all() must be fixed first because it closes every position on the account.
- Capital floor: the bot refuses to arm below 500 USDT (below that, step rounding distorts risk by more than about 10%).

Per trade
- Risk base = min(wallet balance, equity) of the sub-account; never free margin.
- Loss at the stop, including fees and a 10 bps slippage allowance: XAU 0.50%, XAG 0.25% (standard stage L2). Probe stage L1 is half: 0.25% and 0.125%. Compiled ceiling 1.0%; the bot will not start above it, and anything above L2 requires the SUPPORTED verdict.
- Stop = 3.0 x ATR20 (NY-day) from the actual fill, about 7% of price for gold and 13-14% for silver today. Server-side, never widened. A position without a confirmed stop for more than 5 s is closed after 3 failed attach attempts.
- Size is floored to step and skipped below min quantity or min notional, never rounded up; the rounded size is re-verified. Absolute max-risk-money and max-quantity inputs apply on top.

Portfolio
- One position per symbol, two in total.
- Combined open risk at the stops for gold plus silver <= 0.75% at L2 (0.375% at L1). They count as one bet: correlation 0.83-0.88, silver beta about 2 (confirmed).
- Notional caps: 15% of equity per symbol, 25% combined. Expected use is about 7% (gold) and 2% (silver).

Account limits (day boundary 17:00 New York; equity-based, including floating P/L, fees and funding; deposits and withdrawals excluded)
- Daily soft lock at -1.0% of day-start equity: no new entries until the next boundary.
- Daily hard lock at -2.0%: latched flatten of own positions and orders, lock until the next boundary, operator alert.
- Warning at 80% of each limit. The next trade's planned loss must fit inside 80% of the remaining daily allowance.
- Trailing equity high-water mark: warning at -6%, permanent halt at -10% (flatten, persisted lock, manual re-arm only, no automatic release).
- Frequency: at most 1 entry per symbol per NY-day, 2 per day in total, 6 per symbol per rolling 30 days.

Entry gates (never applied to exits or stop changes)
- Entries only in the 20:00-22:00 New York window, Sunday to Thursday. This excludes weekends, the thin 16:00-19:00 hours and every scheduled US release.
- Spread <= 3 bps of price (XAU) or 10 bps (XAG), and <= 2% of the stop distance. Quote age <= 5 s. Order notional <= 1% of resting depth within 0.2% of mid.
- Late-entry guard: skip if price is more than 1.0 x ATR20 from the signal close.
- Funding gate: skip if the trailing-30-day funding for that side, projected over 30 days, exceeds 0.25R (about 21% a year at a 7% stop). January 2026 levels would have vetoed new longs.
- Volatility shock: no new entries while ATR5 / ATR60 (NY-day) > 2.0.

Stress arithmetic at L2 (mine, from the research figures)
- A 30 January 2026 type session against longs in both metals with the stops not filling until the end: gold 7.1% notional x 12% = about 0.85% of equity; silver 1.9% x 31% = about 0.6%; about 1.5% in total.
- A 2% gold and 4% silver weekend move: about 0.14% + 0.08%.
- Liquidation is not a practical risk at under 0.25x effective leverage in a cross-margined sub-account.
designs.validation_plan:
Ground rules
- No optimiser is used anywhere. Parameters are fixed in a pre-registration file committed before the first full backtest.
- The only search is the 24-cell sensitivity grid. Every cell is reported and counted as a trial. Lifetime trial budget: 45 (MinBTL logic, confirmed), kept in a trial ledger with code hash, parameters and result.
- Thresholds from the cited papers are labelled 'sourced'; everything else is a convention chosen in advance and labelled as such in the report.

V0. Data gate (hard)
- Two independent spot XAU and XAG daily histories with New York-close bars, at least 2010-2026 (target 2005+) so the 2011-2015 bear market is inside. Candidates: Dukascopy export, OANDA v20 candles; coverage to be confirmed. Median absolute close difference between sources <= 0.05%, no missing weeks.
- Proxy-versus-venue overlap on Binance NY-day bars from 2026-02-01 (the thin launch weeks excluded): correlation of daily returns >= 0.98 and identical channel and ATR signals on >= 95% of days. If a metal fails, the long backtest is not accepted as evidence for it.

V1. Correctness gate (hard)
- Known-answer self-tests pass: ATR, channel, step flooring, min-notional skip, New York session maths on the US/EU clock-change weeks, state save and reload.
- The backtest is bit-reproducible.
- Invariant scan over every simulated trade: 0 positions without a stop, 0 widened stops, realised loss never above planned plus the modelled gap.

V2. Evidence gate for TREND-D1
- Cost model: fee 5 bps per side; slippage 5 bps on entries and 10 bps on stop exits; a stop that is gapped through fills at the bar open; funding of 10% a year charged to longs and nothing credited to shorts; a second run at 25% a year.
- Reported per metal and pooled, long and short separately, in R and in bps, by era (start-2008, 2009-2022, 2023-2026), with the trade count beside every average and the breakeven win rate beside the achieved one.
- REFUTED if any of: pooled net expectancy of the primary cell <= 0; the grid's median cell <= 0 or fewer than 18 of 24 cells positive; the pooled result is below the median of 1,000 seeded random-entry runs with the same exits, frequency and long/short mix; the result with 2019-01 to 2026-01 removed is negative; fewer than 150 pooled trades. Outcome: no live trading.
- INCONCLUSIVE if not refuted but the primary cell is below the 90th percentile of the random-entry distribution. Outcome: shadow only.
- NOT REFUTED if none of the above. Outcome: live at probe risk only. A metal with at least 60 trades and expectancy <= 0 on its own is dropped.
- SUPPORTED if in addition DSR >= 0.95 with the honest trial count (sourced) and pooled t = Sharpe x sqrt(years) >= 3.0 (sourced). Required for any risk above 0.50% / 0.25%.
- Also reported, flagged as noisy at 24 trials: PBO by CSCV on the complete grid with S = 16. <= 0.05 is the sourced strict level; 0.05-0.2 is an informal band.
- Stated prior: NOT REFUTED or INCONCLUSIVE is the best realistic outcome.

V3. Survival gate (hard)
- Block bootstrap of the trade list in R (blocks of 5 consecutive trades, 5,000 resamples): the 95th-percentile maximum drawdown at L2 risk must be <= 8% of equity, otherwise risk is lowered until it fits. Independent resampling is not used because it removes loss clustering.
- Stress replays: the 30 January 2026 session, the worst silver weekend (about 5%), and funding at January 2026 levels. Loss per event <= 2% of equity.

V4. Shell gate (hard, on testnet if the symbols exist there, otherwise at minimum order size)
Ten fault injections, all passing twice:
1. Process killed between fill and stop placement: on restart the stop is attached within 5 s or the position is closed.
2. Stop placement rejected three times: fail-safe close.
3. Restart mid-position: no duplicate entry, initial R and trail state restored.
4. Daily lock survives a restart.
5. Flatten latch persists through failed closes until flat.
6. The same intent delivered twice: one order.
7. HTTP 451/403/5xx and timeouts: classified, backed off, no retry storm.
8. Failed or partial kline fetch: the bar is retried, not skipped.
9. A deposit or withdrawal does not move the day's P/L.
10. Size below minimum: skipped with a reason.

V5. Shadow gate
- At least 4 weeks in MONITOR on live data.
- 0 unexplained differences between live decisions and next-day replay.
- Veto counts by reason reviewed against the recorder's spread and funding tables.

V6. Live probe (L1 risk, at least 6 months and at least 8 closed trades)
- Pre-written stop rules, any one halts trading for review: an invariant violation (naked position over 5 s, widened stop, duplicate entry); median entry slippage > 10 bps; realised/planned loss > 2.0 on any trade or median > 1.25; drawdown beyond the bootstrap 95th percentile for the stage; an unexplained live-versus-replay mismatch.
- Step-up to L2 only if none fired.
- Live trading tests implementation and cost parity, not edge. Minimum track record length (likely) puts confirmation of a Sharpe of 1 at about 2.7 years of daily returns and far longer for lower values.

RANGE-NY promotion gate (shadow only)
- At least 150 shadow signals.
- Net expectancy after 10 bps of fees and measured slippage >= +0.10R, with a bootstrap 95% lower bound above 0.
- At or above the 95th percentile of random-direction entries at the same times with the same exits.
- Gross edge at least 3 times all-in cost.
- Otherwise the module is deleted after 6 months.

build_phases.acceptance: Every contract and fee value is read live and stored, none assumed. No HTTP 451 or 403 from the worker for 14 days. The recorder covers two weekends and the 16:00-19:00 New York hours. Sub-account equity is at or above the floor. If any assumption A1-A6 fails, a written venue re-decision is produced and no strategy code is written.

build_phases.phase: 1. Data layer, evaluator, cost model, pre-registration
build_phases.deliverable: NY-day bar builder; two-source spot history loader; the single TREND-D1 evaluator; explicit cost model; random-entry benchmark; trial ledger; self-tests; the pre-registration file with frozen parameters, grid and gates.

build_phases.phase: 2. Evidence run and verdict
build_phases.deliverable: One validation report: all 24 cells, per-metal and pooled results, long/short and era splits, random-entry distribution, DSR and PBO, block-bootstrap drawdown, stress replays, and a verdict of REFUTED, INCONCLUSIVE, NOT REFUTED or SUPPORTED.

REFUTED ends the trading project here; the shell is then built only if the requester wants it for the existing crypto bot. No parameter is changed after seeing results without logging a new trial.

build_phases.phase: 3. Protection and execution shell

The sizing audit line shows planned loss within 5% of the budget on every test order. A code grep confirms a single order-send function and no path that adds to an open position.

build_phases.phase: 4. Shadow run

build_phases.acceptance: V5 passes: zero unexplained decision differences; every veto has a reason and a measured value; alerts fire once per state change and report recovery; the operator has exercised EXIT_ONLY and a confirmed flatten.

build_phases.phase: 5. Live probe at 0.25% / 0.125% risk
build_phases.deliverable: Live trading at L1 for at least 6 months and 8 closed trades, with a monthly reconciliation report: live versus replay trade by trade, slippage, funding in R, planned versus realised loss, limit usage.
build_phases.acceptance: No V6 stop rule fired. Median entry slippage <= 10 bps. Drawdown inside the bootstrap 95th percentile. Only then may risk move to 0.50% / 0.25%; anything above that requires the SUPPORTED verdict.

build_phases.phase: 6. Optional, after phase 4: RANGE-NY in shadow, and back-port of the shell

For the back-port: sizing uses the stop distance, record_trade is wired or replaced by the equity-based guard, signals read the closed bar, and a failed stop closes the position.

main_risks: No edge. The most likely long-run outcome is roughly zero expectancy minus costs: per-instrument trend is not statistically established, static trend was near zero in 2009-2022, and two correlated metals give almost none of the diversification the published results rely on.

Venue risk. Binance's metals perps are 11 months old, their off-hours index and mark rules changed twice in 2026, access is jurisdiction-gated, the futures API geo-blocks by server location (HTTP 451), and equity sits in USDT at one exchange. A rule change, delisting or region change at Railway can stop the bot or change stop behaviour.

Unverified inputs. Max leverage, min notional, step sizes, the account's real fee rate, the excluded-country list, how the pinned ccxt version names the markets and routes conditional orders, and whether sub-accounts and a testnet listing are available were not confirmed. Phase 0 exists to read them; the design may need to change afterwards.

Funding regime. Longs paid about 4.35% of notional in January 2026 alone and roughly 6-11% a year from May to October 2026; single prints reached 0.5% per 4 hours on a weekend. A multi-week long can lose a meaningful fraction of R to funding; the gate limits new entries only.

Proxy-history mismatch. The evidence run uses decades of spot daily bars while the bot trades a perp with a basis, weekend prints and funding, and the overlap is under a year. The overlap gate checks signals, not costs in past regimes.

Fast markets and gaps. Stops are stop-market orders and fill at the next available price. Silver fell 26-31% and gold about 9-12% in one session on 30 January 2026; weekend books are thin (silver weekend ranges up to about 5%). Losses above 1R will happen; sizing bounds them, it does not prevent them.

Low trade count. About ten trades a year means live results stay statistically uninformative for years, which invites tinkering. Every tweak is a trial; breaching the 45-trial budget voids the validation.
Regime dependence. Gold is in a high-volatility drawdown after a record bull run. Backtests over 2015-2026 flatter anything long-biased, and breakout rules lose in runs when the market ranges.

Operational failure. Railway restarts, redeploy overlap, ephemeral storage if no volume is attached, exchange API changes and clock or session errors are the realistic ways to lose money without any market move. The shell reduces these and cannot remove them.
Silver specifics. Thinner depth, a coarse tick, squeeze and air-pocket history, and broker- and venue-specific contract terms. Silver may fail its own validation and be dropped.
Legal and regulatory. The licensing findings are research, not legal advice; the status of leveraged metals perps and of this exchange for the requester's country of residence was not checked.
designs.honest_expectation:
No profitability is promised or implied. The base rate is that 74-89% of retail leveraged accounts lose money (confirmed), and backtest Sharpe had almost no power to predict live results in the one large cohort studied (very_likely).

What Phase 2 will most likely say: NOT REFUTED or INCONCLUSIVE, not proof. Published per-market trend Sharpe is about 0.4 gross over 136 years and static trend was near zero in 2009-2022 (confirmed for diversified portfolios). If the verdict is REFUTED, the correct outcome is that the bot does not trade and the product of the project is the shell and the report.

If it does trade:
- Expect roughly 8-14 trades a year across both metals (to be measured), most of them small losses, and flat or losing stretches of one to three years.
- At 0.50% / 0.25% risk the yearly sum of risk is only about 4% of equity. With per-trade expectancy anywhere between -0.1R and +0.3R, that is about -1% to +1% a year after fees and funding, and single years of perhaps -5% to +8%. This is my arithmetic from an assumed expectancy range, not a measurement.
- That is small on purpose. Position notional is about 7% of equity in gold and 2% in silver, which is what keeps a 30 January 2026 type session to about 1.5% of equity. A higher return would need either an edge the evidence does not show or more risk on an unproven one; the design allows the second only after the SUPPORTED gate.

What the requester gets with high confidence, whatever the strategy does:
- Position size that really is tied to the stop, which the current bot's is not.
- Loss limits that are wired, equity-based and survive a restart.
- A server-side stop on every position, or the position is closed.
- A journal that lets live and replay be compared trade by trade.

Statistical confirmation of any edge from live trading will take years. Until then the honest status is 'not refuted, risk bounded'.

designs.name: MetalSleeves: an evidence-gated multi-strategy portfolio for gold and silver (one risk allocator, sleeves that must earn their capital)
designs.thesis:
Build one risk allocator and let strategy modules ("sleeves") compete for a small, fixed risk budget under pre-registered gates, instead of merging every open-source feature into one signal.

Three facts from the brief set the shape.
1. Of 206 trading EAs, 18% are grid or martingale, only 106 always carry a hard stop, and 100% have red flags. What is worth gathering is the plumbing (closed-bar evaluation, loss-at-stop sizing, persisted locks, reason-coded gates), not the signals.
2. The evidence review supports only slow trend following. Even that is "very likely" not established on a single instrument, and it decayed after 2009. Session breakouts on gold are folklore, short-horizon mean reversion has no cost-surviving evidence, and gold/silver ratio reversion failed violently in 2020 and 2025-26.
3. XAU and XAG are 0.83-0.88 correlated with silver beta about 2. Diversification cannot come from the two symbols; it can only come from different horizons and payoff shapes, and that has to be measured, not assumed.

So the portfolio is tiered.
- Tier A: one prior-justified sleeve that may go live (slow multi-horizon trend).
- Tier B: two catalog-derived intraday candidates (session range breakout, sweep-and-reclaim) that run in shadow mode with zero capital until they pass statistical gates.
- Tier C: gold/silver ratio diagnostics that are logged but never sized.

Risk shares follow evidence quality, not backtest performance. Every added module or filter is charged to a trial ledger capped at 30 runs, shares one parameter set across both metals and both directions, and must show low correlation to what is already live. The allocator is regime-aware only towards less risk (volatility, shock, event, off-hours, drawdown, carry). It never routes between strategies and never scales size up.

The design offers bounded, auditable risk and an honest test of whether any edge exists. It does not promise profit, and a null result (risk engine built, no sleeve cleared for capital) is an accepted outcome.
designs.platform:
Decision: a venue-neutral Python 3.12 core (sleeves, allocator, risk, journal and backtester share one code path) on the requester's existing Linux PaaS, with Binance USD-M TradFi perpetuals XAUUSDT / XAGUSDT through ccxt as the first live venue.

Why, from the brief:
(a) Stack reuse. The requester already runs Python + ccxt on Binance futures. The official MetaTrader5 Python package is Windows-only, has no tester access and cannot run on a Linux PaaS or MetaQuotes VPS (fact-check: supported); an MQL5 EA is a rewrite in a new language plus a Windows VPS.
(b) Size granularity with capital unknown. The gold perp trades in 0.001 oz steps. CFD minimums are 1 oz of gold and 10-50 oz of silver per 0.01 lot. A daily trend stop of 3 x ATR(D1) is about $270/oz today, so one CFD minimum lot risks about $270: 1% risk needs roughly $27k equity and 0.25% needs about $108k (own arithmetic). Only the perp lets "never round up" and fixed-fractional risk both hold for a small account.
(c) Cost fit for the one evidence-backed sleeve. Slow trend turns over a few times a year, so Binance's fee-dominated cost (about 10 bps per taker round trip at the standard 0.02%/0.05% tier; the real rate is read from the API) is immaterial for it.
(d) Validation tooling. Trial ledger, Deflated Sharpe, PBO and block bootstrap are native in Python; MT5 has none built in.

Costs of this choice, stated up front:
- The same 10 bps makes most intraday setups fail the cost gate. That is the intended outcome; intraday sleeves stay in shadow and are also scored under a raw-spread CFD cost model (about 0.5-1.5 bps round trip).
- Funding is a 4-hourly cash flow. It cost longs roughly 6-11% a year from May 2026 (fact-check figure), with single prints up to +0.5% per 4 hours.
- The contract has about 11 months of history spanning two changes to off-hours pricing (2026-05-08, 2026-09-15), so long tests use spot XAU/XAG proxies validated on the 2026 overlap.
- Access needs a signed TradFi-Perps agreement, an eligible jurisdiction and a server region that is not geo-blocked (HTTP 451 was seen from a US host). P&L settles in USDT.

Settings: one-way (netting) mode, cross margin, exchange leverage 3x or lower, market entries, server-side reduce-only STOP_MARKET stops and limit take-profits, clientOrderId prefixes as the ownership key (the magic-number equivalent).

Assumptions to verify in Phase 0: the account is eligible; equity is at least about $2,000 (below that, one-third-size silver positions fall under the reported, unverified 5 USDT minimum notional and are skipped, not rounded up); tick, step, leverage and funding caps are read from exchangeInfo, never assumed; no prop-firm or swap-free account is involved.

Phase 0 decision rule: if eligibility fails, the first adapter becomes OKX XAU-USDT-SWAP / XAG-USDT-SWAP via ccxt (0.001 XAU contract, different tick, 8-hour funding; parameters are re-read, not copied).

A raw-spread CFD adapter through a Python-native API (OANDA v20 or cTrader Open API) is built only in Phase 6, and only if an intraday sleeve passes every gate under measured CFD costs and equity covers minimum lots without rounding up.

Not used: MT5/MQL5 as the trading platform, PAXG as a gold proxy (its basis wandered about -0.4% to +0.2%), and the weekend session for new entries.

strategies.name: TREND-D1: slow multi-horizon trend (Tier A, the only sleeve allowed capital at launch, about 85% of the risk budget)
strategies.logic:
Inputs: D1 bars built from H1 with a 17:00 America/New_York boundary; bars between Friday 17:00 and Sunday 18:00 New York are excluded from signals.

Signal: at each D1 close t, for L in {21, 63, 252} trading days, m_L = sign(C_t - C_(t-L)). Composite S = (m_21 + m_63 + m_252) / 3, which takes the values -1, -1/3, +1/3, +1. Direction = sign(S); exposure fraction = |S|.

Sizing: a campaign starts when sign(S) flips or after a flat period. q_unit = floor_to_step(E x u x g x v / (D + c)), where E = min(balance, equity), u = 1.00% (XAU) or 0.50% (XAG), g = stage multiplier, v = regime multiplier, D = 3.0 x ATR(D1,20) from closed bars, c = per-unit fees plus assumed stop slippage. Held quantity = |S| x q_unit. When |S| changes without a sign flip the position is resized: 1 -> 1/3 closes two thirds; 1/3 -> 1 adds back only as much as keeps the loss at the current stop within E x u x g x v. A sign flip is a verified close, then a new campaign the other way.

Stop: one server-side reduce-only stop at entry -/+ D. Then a closed-bar chandelier: candidate = best close since campaign start -/+ 3.0 x ATR(D1,20), applied through the tighten-only gateway when it improves by at least 0.25 x ATR(D1,20). No take-profit, breakeven or partials other than the |S| resize.

Re-entry latch: after a protective stop-out the symbol stays flat in that direction until m_21 has pointed the other way at some close, or the composite sign flips.

Execution: decisions at the D1 close; orders at the first H1 open at or after 11:00 New York on the next trading day that is outside an event blackout (roll to the next day after 15:00). Market orders.

Carry veto: no new campaign on a side whose trailing-30-day funding annualises above 15% against it; existing positions are kept.

Fitted parameters: none. 21/63/252, 3.0 and 20 are fixed a priori and perturbed only for a sensitivity report.
strategies.timeframe: Signals on D1 (17:00 New York close); holding period weeks to months; at most one execution per symbol per day.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT perps, with signals validated on spot XAU/USD and XAG/USD proxies. Silver at half the unit risk. Both metals count as one directional bucket.
strategies.rationale:
This is the only family with long, multi-source evidence: about 0.4 gross Sharpe per market over 1880-2016 (Hurst, Ooi, Pedersen) and the Goulding-Harvey-Mazzoleni tables (fact-check: supported).

Limits respected: the same sources show decay after 2009 (12-month trend Sharpe 1.07 then 0.06 on a 43-market book), and single-instrument trend is "very likely" not a statistically established edge. The sleeve is therefore prior-justified, not proven on gold or silver.

Design choices: the three lookbacks are the standard 1/3/12-month blend, so nothing is chosen from metal data. |S| scaling cuts exposure to one third when horizons disagree, which is where turning points do their damage. ATR-stop sizing is risk control, not edge (Harvey et al., supported). A few round trips a year make the 10 bps fee irrelevant; funding is the cost to watch.

Catalog support: "Higher-timeframe trend-side filter on closed bars" (18 EAs, including q5 77691), "Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop", "Volatility-unit stop distance (ATR or gap-free mean range)".

strategies.name: SRB: pre-New-York session range breakout (Tier B candidate; shadow first, zero capital until gates pass)
strategies.logic:
Range: high and low of M1 bars in [03:00, 08:00) New York. The day is no-trade if fewer than 90% of those M1 bars exist.

Width gate: W = R_hi - R_lo must satisfy 0.15 <= W / ATR(D1,20) <= 0.70 and W >= 10 x current spread.

Trigger: the first M15 bar that closes in [08:00, 11:00) New York with close > R_hi + 0.10 x W (long) or close < R_lo - 0.10 x W (short). Never a forming-bar pierce. One trigger per day.

Direction lock: only in the direction of sign(S) from TREND-D1 (one shared trend state; switchable for ablation).

Entry: market at the next M15 open after all gates pass (event, shock, cost, net reward-to-risk, direction, daily budget).

Stop: range midpoint (R_hi - 0.5 x W for longs). D = entry - stop. If D < 0.75 x ATR(H1,20) the stop is widened to that distance before sizing; if D > 2.0 x ATR(H1,20) the setup is skipped.

Target: entry + 2.0 x D as a resting reduce-only limit.

Feasibility: all-in round-trip cost <= 10% of D, and (target distance - cost) / (D + cost) >= 1.5; otherwise skip with a reason code.

Management: stop and target only; flatten at 15:30 New York. No breakeven, partials or trailing in v1.

Size: 0.25% x g x v of equity at the stop, also capped by the intraday notional cap.

Pre-registered grid (6 runs): target R in {1.5, 2.0, 3.0} x window in {pre-NY as above; Asian range [19:00, 02:00) New York with entries [03:00, 06:00)}. The live configuration is the pre-registered default (2.0R, pre-NY); the grid is robustness evidence only.
strategies.timeframe: Range from M1, trigger on M15 closed bars, ATR context from H1 and D1. Intraday, always flat by 15:30 New York.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT only as a capital candidate. XAGUSDT runs the same parameters in shadow as a robustness check (silver's spread eats about three times more of its hourly range).
strategies.rationale:
Included because the best-engineered gold EAs in the sample are of this family (75586, 76153, 78688, 78293, 17465) and the catalog rates its parts core: "Session/opening range builder from M1 bars", "Closed-bar range breakout with buffer and entry window", "Range-width and compression gate". Its intraday, flat-by-close payoff is also structurally different from a multi-week trend position.

Not included on evidence of edge, because there is none. The research found no peer-reviewed, cost-inclusive test on gold (fact-check: partially supported), and an index-CFD replication saw a gross +0.13R vanish after costs. What is confirmed is time-of-day structure in range: New York 08:00-11:00 is the peak block in 2026, which is why that window is primary. Sessions predict how much gold moves, not which way.

On Binance the 10 bps fee is roughly 15-25% of a typical 40-70 bps stop, so most setups will fail the 10% cost gate. The shadow journal therefore scores every setup under both the Binance and a raw-spread CFD cost model. Prior: zero edge minus costs.

strategies.name: SWEEP: failed-breakout sweep-and-reclaim (Tier B candidate, built after SRB, shadow first)
strategies.logic:
Level registry per symbol and day: prior-day high and low (17:00 New York boundary) and the pre-NY range high and low. Each level is single-use. A level is deleted when an M15 bar closes beyond it by 0.10 x W; that event belongs to SRB.

Sweep bar: an M15 bar closing in [08:00, 13:00) New York whose high >= L + 0.25 x ATR(M15,20) and whose close < L (mirror for lows).

Confirmation: within the next 3 M15 bars, a bar closes below the sweep bar's body low with range >= 0.30 x ATR(M15,20). Otherwise the setup expires.

Entry: market at the next open, short for a swept high and long for a swept low, and only when that direction equals sign(S) of TREND-D1 (fade failed breakouts against the slow trend only).

Stop: sweep extreme +/- 0.10 x ATR(M15,20). Skip unless 0.5 <= D / ATR(H1,20) <= 2.0.

Target: 2.0 x D. Same cost and net reward-to-risk gates as SRB.

Shock ceiling: no entry when ATR(M15,5) / ATR(M15,20) >= 1.5.

Management: flatten at 15:30 New York. One SWEEP trade per symbol per day, and never while an SRB position is open.

Size: 0.25% x g x v.

Pre-registered grid (6 runs): wick multiple in {0.15, 0.25, 0.40} x target R in {1.5, 2.0}. Live configuration is the default (0.25, 2.0R).
strategies.timeframe: M15 closed bars with H1 and D1 context. Intraday, flat by 15:30 New York.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT as a capital candidate; XAGUSDT in shadow with identical parameters.
strategies.rationale:
This is the portfolio's stand-in for mean reversion. It is the only counter-move entry in the catalog that is fully specified on closed bars with ATR-qualified wicks, a confirmation window and single-use levels ("Liquidity sweep-and-reclaim (failed breakout) entry"; 77639 q5, 77094 q4; verdict optional, overfit 3). It is chosen over the "Oscillator zone-exit / band re-entry reversal trigger" (verdict avoid; hosts are mostly grid or recovery EAs) because it has a structural invalidation point and no averaging.

Evidence status: none beyond code quality. The research found no cost-surviving evidence for short-horizon reversal on metals and mild evidence for continuation after large moves, so the prior is zero to negative.

Its value to the portfolio, if any, is that it trades range days when breakout and trend sleeves lose. That is tested by the correlation gate, not assumed. Level ownership and the direction lock stop it from ever holding against SRB or TREND.

strategies.name: RV-DIAG: gold/silver relative value (Tier C; logged diagnostics, never sized in v1)
strategies.logic:
Once per D1 close, compute and journal: ratio = C_XAU / C_XAG; z = (ratio - mean_250) / sd_250; sign of the 63-day ratio change; rolling 60-day correlation and beta of XAG to XAU.

No orders, no veto, no input to any sleeve.

A paper record of two hypothetical rules is kept for information only, each volatility-balanced (XAG notional = XAU notional / beta): (a) fade |z| >= 2 and exit at |z| <= 1, the form that failed in the literature; (b) follow the 63-day ratio trend.

Promotion to a tradable sleeve would need a new pre-registration, its own ledger entries, every candidate gate, and a market-neutral execution design that does not exist in v1.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT as a pair; not traded.
strategies.rationale:
The portfolio angle calls for considering relative value, and the evidence says no. Gold/silver cointegration is unstable and regime-dependent, and z-score reversion worked in windows then failed violently (fact-check: partially supported; direction confirmed, magnitudes unreliable). The ratio ranged 57-105 in 2025 and 46-80 in 2026. Ratio momentum was not found in any credible study.

The catalog rates the "Cross-symbol directional proxy" optional with overfit 4 and says to log it first as a diagnostic. This does exactly that, and it gives the allocator's static rule (XAU and XAG are one bucket, silver beta 2) a monitored basis.

strategies.name: BENCH: null and reference sleeves (research only, never traded)
strategies.logic:
Four comparators run through the same backtester, cost model and journal:
1. Random entry: the sleeve's own exits, hours, frequency and long/short mix with a seeded coin-flip direction, 1,000 seeds.
2. Exposure-matched buy-and-hold for each metal.
3. Donchian-20 closed-bar breakout on H4 with EMA200 side filter and ATR stop (the q5 EA 77691), long and short.
4. A straight port of the requester's existing entry (EMA9/21/50 alignment, fresh cross, RSI zone, rising MACD histogram, volume spike; SL 1.5 x ATR, TP 3 x ATR on 5m).

Each is one ledger entry, run once, with no tuning.
strategies.timeframe: Matches the sleeve being benchmarked (D1, H4, M15, 5m).
strategies.symbols: Spot XAU/USD and XAG/USD proxies and the 2026 Binance perp history.
strategies.rationale:
A backtest alone cannot say how much of a result is signal and how much is exit geometry or gold's drift. The catalog's "Random-entry benchmark mode (null hypothesis)" answers that.

Buy-and-hold is needed because 2015-2026 gold backtests are contaminated by a record bull market.

Donchian-20 H4 is the transparent benchmark the catalog recommends for the session engine; its own author admits long-only was chosen because shorts lost.

The port of the existing 5m stack shows the requester why it is not carried over. Standard moving-average rules had no predictive power on 5-minute gold and none on silver (Batten et al.). A 1.5 x ATR(5m) stop is on the order of 10-15 bps (own estimate), so a 10 bps fee would consume most of 1R before any edge.
