designs.risk_model:
All numbers are policy defaults fixed before testing. None is optimised; each gate has a switch so its effect can be reported.

1. Risk unit
- Risk = loss at the server-side stop, including fees and assumed stop slippage, as a fraction of E = min(wallet balance, equity).
- Flat risk per trade. No Kelly, no score scaling, no increase after wins.

2. Stage multiplier g (per sleeve)
- SHADOW 0, PILOT 0.25, LIVE-1 0.5, LIVE-2 1.0.
- Promotion needs gate evidence plus a recorded operator sign-off. Demotion is automatic.

3. Unit risk at g = 1
- TREND-D1: 1.00% XAU and 0.50% XAG at |S| = 1 (one third of that at |S| = 1/3).
- SRB and SWEEP: 0.25% per trade, XAU only, one intraday position at a time.
- Share of budget: TREND about 85%, intraday candidates about 15%, reflecting evidence quality.
- Scale check (own arithmetic on 2026 volatility): 1% at a 3 x ATR(D1) stop is about 14.5% of equity in gold notional; 0.5% in silver is about 3.8%. Portfolio volatility at full stage is roughly 5-7% a year.

4. Portfolio caps (the smallest binds; the binding limit is logged)
- Total open risk at stops: 2.0% of equity.
- Carried notional (held outside liquid hours): XAU <= 20% of equity, XAG <= 8%. Derivation: with every stop failing in a repeat of 30 Jan 2026 (gold -12%, silver -31%), loss = 2.4% + 2.5% = 4.9%. At the default trend sizes the same scenario costs about 2.9%.
- Intraday notional (flat by 15:30 New York, stop resting): XAU <= 30% of equity.
- Gross notional <= 60% of equity; exchange leverage setting <= 3x; no entries if used initial margin exceeds 25% of equity.
- XAU and XAG are one bucket: |N_XAU + 2 x N_XAG| <= 40% of equity.
- One net direction per symbol. Intraday sleeves trade only in the direction of sign(S) from TREND.
- A new order may use at most 80% of the remaining daily loss allowance.
- Below-minimum sizes are skipped and counted, never rounded up.

5. Regime rules (reduce only)
- HIGH_VOL: ATR(D1,20) / ATR(D1,250) >= 1.5 halves new-entry risk on that symbol.
- SHOCK: last D1 true range >= 3 x ATR(D1,20) blocks all new entries on that symbol for one trading day. Intraday ATR(5)/ATR(20) ceilings: 2.5 on H1 for SRB, 1.5 on M15 for SWEEP.
- EVENT: no intraday entries from 30 minutes before to 30 minutes after NFP, CPI and PCE (08:30 New York), and from 13:30 to 15:00 on FOMC days. TREND executions are shifted out of these windows. Flagged dates: 9-10 December 2026 (FOMC then CPI).
- OFF_HOURS: no new entries 16:00-19:00 New York daily, or from Friday 16:00 to Sunday 19:00.
- COST: skip when all-in round-trip cost exceeds 10% of the stop distance, or when spread exceeds 3 x its recorded same-hour median.
- CARRY: no new TREND campaign on a side paying more than 15% annualised funding over the trailing 30 days.

6. Account limits by stage (PILOT / LIVE-1 / LIVE-2)
- Daily loss on equity, day boundary 17:00 New York: 1.0% / 1.5% / 2.0%.
  - At 80% of the limit: block entries and flatten intraday positions.
  - At the limit: latched flatten of everything and a lock until the next boundary.
- Weekly loss: 2% / 3% / 4%. No new entries until the next week.
- Trailing drawdown kill from the persisted equity high-water mark: 4% / 8% / 15%, or 1.25 x the block-bootstrap 95th-percentile drawdown if that is lower. Permanent lock, human review.
- At 60% of the kill level the stage is halved; restoring it needs operator action.

7. Invariants
- No position without a confirmed server-side stop for more than 5 seconds; otherwise close.
- Stops are never widened.
- Exits are never blocked by entry gates.
- Locks survive restarts.
- Three invariant violations put the bot in EXIT_ONLY.

8. Not covered
- A stop is not a guarantee. Gaps, thin off-hours books and venue rule changes can produce losses beyond these limits; the notional caps are the only defence that does not depend on a fill.
designs.validation_plan:
The plan has two purposes: limit the overfitting cost of extra modules, and decide pass/fail before results are seen. Gates marked [P] have a primary source in the brief; [C] are conventions and are labelled as such in every report.

A. Degrees-of-freedom budget
- A pre-registration file (parameters, grids, gates, data windows) is hashed and committed before any metal data is pulled.
- Trial ledger capped at 30 runs: TREND 1 + 6 neighbours, SRB 6, SWEEP 6, ablations 10, reserve 1. This is under the roughly 45 independent configurations that 5 years of data allow before a zero-skill in-sample Sharpe of 1 appears [P]. The bound is tighter for lower Sharpe targets, so anything below Sharpe 1 is treated as unproven.
- Searched parameters: TREND 0; SRB 2; SWEEP 2; allocator 0. The live configuration is always the pre-registered default; grids are robustness evidence, not a menu.
- Ablations may only remove a component.
- Any new module or filter needs a new pre-registration and raises the trial count used in the Deflated Sharpe. With about 30 trials and a cross-trial Sharpe dispersion of 0.5, the zero-skill expected maximum is already about 1.0 annualised (own calculation).

B. Data gates (fail = stop)
- Daily and H1 spot XAU/XAG from two independent feeds, 2005-2026; closes within 0.3% on at least 99% of days.
- M1 bid/ask with at least 99% coverage inside session windows. Assumed available from about 2016; audited in Phase 1.
- Binance archive (trades, 1m klines, funding, premium index, depth) for 2026, with December 2025 excluded and the two off-hours regime changes tagged.
- Proxy check on the 2026 overlap: TREND sign agreement between spot and perp on at least 98% of days.
- Backtests charge fees, spread and slippage both ways, apply stop-first when a bar contains stop and target, use actual funding for 2026 and a carry model before that (longs pay T-bill + 3%, shorts receive T-bill - 3%, floored at zero), and are re-run with costs doubled.

C. TREND-D1 gates (non-contradiction, not proof)
Expected t is about 0.3 x sqrt(21 years) = 1.4, so the sleeve cannot be significant on its own data. It rests on the multi-market literature prior.
- T1: net Sharpe >= 0.20 over 2005-2026 at fixed-money risk.
- T2: net P&L >= 0 in the 2011-2015 gold bear market and in at least 3 of 4 five-year blocks.
- T3: long and short sides reported separately. If shorts lose more than half of what longs earn, the sleeve is classed as long beta and capped at PILOT.
- T4: median net Sharpe of the 7 neighbour configurations >= 0.15, and at least 5 of 7 positive [C].
- T5: at or above the 90th percentile of 1,000 random-direction runs with matched long share and holding periods.
- T6: lower maximum drawdown than exposure-matched buy-and-hold.
- Any failure: TREND does not trade.

D. Candidate gates for SRB and SWEEP
Every gate applies under the target venue's cost model.
- C1: at least 300 trades and at least 30 per year [C].
- C2: net expectancy >= +0.10R and >= 2x all-in cost per trade.
- C3: t-statistic of mean R >= 3.0 [P]. Between 2 and 3 the sleeve stays in shadow.
- C4: Deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 using the full ledger count [P].
- C5: PBO by CSCV (S = 16) on the complete pre-registered config matrix <= 0.05 [P]. 0.05-0.20 is an informal band that blocks promotion beyond PILOT. The matrix barely meets the "many more than 10 trials" requirement, so PBO is supporting evidence only.
- C6: at or above the 95th percentile of 1,000 random-entry seeds with the same exits, hours and long/short mix.
- C7: positive in both high-volatility (2020, 2025-26) and low-volatility (2017-19, 2024) samples, and on both sides.
- C8: at least 4 of 6 grid runs net positive; same sign on XAG with identical parameters; second feed within +/-30%; still positive at 2x costs.
- C9: anchored yearly walk-forward with at least 60% of out-of-sample years positive [C].
- C10: a final 12-month holdout opened once; mean R >= -0.05 and trade frequency within +/-30% of expectation.

E. Portfolio gates
- P1: a candidate gets its own risk budget only if the correlation of its daily returns with the live portfolio is within +/-0.30.
- P2: weekly block bootstrap, 5,000 paths: probability of reaching the drawdown kill within 3 years <= 10% at the requested stage, otherwise a lower stage.
- P3: stress replay of 30 Jan 2026, the October 2025 silver squeeze, a 5% silver weekend and a +0.5% funding print: loss <= 5% of equity with total stop failure.

F. Execution gates
- E1 paper, at least 6 weeks: 100% decision-by-decision parity between live decisions and a replay on the same data; every skip has a reason code.
- E2 pilot, at least 12 weeks at g = 0.25: zero invariant violations, a passed forced-restart test with a lock active, fees and funding within 2% of the model, median entry slippage at or below the assumption.

G. Live falsification
- A sleeve is suspended if its drawdown exceeds the bootstrap 95th percentile, if realised costs exceed 1.5x the model over 20 trades, or if rolling 24-month net R falls below the bootstrap 5th percentile.
- Live trading cannot confirm a low-Sharpe edge: the minimum track record is about 2.7 years at Sharpe 1 and decades at Sharpe 0.3. It can only bound and falsify.

build_phases.phase: Phase 0 - Venue fact audit and pre-registration (about 1 week)
build_phases.deliverable: Venue fact sheet read from the bot's own server: eligibility and TradFi-Perps agreement status, exchangeInfo for XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT (tick, step, minimum notional, leverage, funding caps), real commission rate, ccxt symbol names, stop trigger types, trading-schedule endpoint, region check for HTTP 451. Spread, depth and funding recorder started. Pre-registration file (all parameters, grids, gates, trial budget) and licensing provenance log committed.
build_phases.acceptance: Every assumed value in this proposal is replaced by a read value, or the venue decision rule is applied (switch to the OKX adapter, or stop). Recorder runs 7 days without gaps. Pre-registration hash is in the repository before any historical metal data is downloaded. Minimum-equity figure recomputed from the real minimum notional and step.

build_phases.phase: Phase 1 - Core library, data layer and backtester (3-4 weeks)
build_phases.deliverable: instrument_profile, market_clock_data, position_sizer, cost and funding model, journal, event-driven bar backtester, self-test suite. Two-feed data audit report.
build_phases.acceptance: All known-answer self-tests pass. Reruns are deterministic (identical journal hash). DST tests pass for the US and EU changeover weeks in March and October/November. A 10,000-case property test shows sizing never rounds up and the verified loss never exceeds budget. The backtester reproduces a hand-computed 20-trade ledger to the cent, including fees and funding. Data gates in section B pass or the affected sleeve is blocked.

build_phases.phase: Phase 2 - Allocator, account guard and execution engine in paper mode (3-4 weeks)
build_phases.deliverable: risk_allocator, gate_pipeline, account_guard, execution_engine, exit_manager and state_ops running against live data with simulated fills and real order validation; operator status page and exit-only / flatten controls.
build_phases.acceptance: Fault-injection suite passes: process kill mid-order, network drop, rejected stop, partial fill, duplicate signal, day rollover while locked, expired calendar file. In every case no position is unprotected for more than 5 seconds, no duplicate order is created, locks persist, and panic flatten reaches flat within 30 seconds in simulation. State round-trip test passes.

build_phases.phase: Phase 3 - TREND-D1 validation (about 2 weeks)
build_phases.deliverable: One pre-registered run plus six neighbours on 2005-2026 proxies and the 2026 perp overlap; report with long/short split, five-year blocks, carry sensitivity, random-direction benchmark, buy-and-hold comparison, bootstrap drawdown; trial ledger entries.
build_phases.acceptance: Gates T1-T6 and the proxy check pass, with the report stating plainly that the result is not statistically significant by itself. If any gate fails, the trend sleeve is not traded and the project continues only as research; that outcome is accepted in advance.

build_phases.phase: Phase 4 - TREND paper then pilot (6 weeks paper, then at least 12 weeks at g = 0.25)
build_phases.deliverable: TREND live on Binance at pilot size with full journals; weekly reconciliation of decisions, fills, fees and funding against a replay; monthly sleeve scorecard.
build_phases.acceptance: E1: 100% decision parity over the paper period. E2: zero invariant violations, forced-restart test passed with a lock active, costs within tolerance. Gate P2 confirms the drawdown-kill probability at the requested stage. Only then LIVE-1 (g = 0.5).

build_phases.phase: Phase 5 - Candidate sleeves: research and shadow mode (4-6 weeks build, runs in parallel with Phase 4)
build_phases.deliverable: SRB then SWEEP implemented behind the sleeve interface; six-run grids and benchmarks executed once each; shadow mode live with hypothetical trades journaled under both cost models; RV-DIAG logging; decision memo on whether a CFD adapter is justified.
build_phases.acceptance: Gates C1-C10 and P1-P3 evaluated exactly as pre-registered, ledger at or below 30 runs. A sleeve that fails stays in shadow or is retired; no gate is relaxed after results are seen. Shadow decisions match replay 100% over at least 8 weeks.

build_phases.phase: Phase 6 - Conditional promotion or second venue (only if Phase 5 produces a pass)
build_phases.deliverable: If a candidate passes on Binance costs: PILOT at 0.25 x 0.25% risk. If it passes only under CFD costs: a raw-spread CFD adapter (OANDA v20 or cTrader Open API) with run-time contract checks (silver 1,000 vs 5,000 oz, digits, stops level, swap, sessions) and 8 weeks of recorded spreads on the actual account.
build_phases.acceptance: The adapter passes the full Phase 2 fault-injection suite and the symbol-profile abort tests. Candidate gates are re-run with the measured spread table and still pass. Equity covers minimum lots without rounding up. Then E1 and E2 are repeated for the new sleeve or venue.

build_phases.phase: Phase 7 - Operate, review, scale (ongoing)
build_phases.deliverable: Monthly scorecard per sleeve (net R, costs versus model, veto counts by reason, drawdown versus bootstrap bands), quarterly re-validation with new data, annual review of policy constants.
build_phases.acceptance: LIVE-2 (g = 1.0) only after at least 12 months live with no invariant violation, drawdown inside the bootstrap 75th percentile and operator sign-off. Any change to logic or parameters restarts at SHADOW with a new pre-registration and ledger entries. Suspension rules in section G are applied without discretion.

main_risks: There may be no edge at all. Single-instrument trend following is 'very likely' not statistically established, static trend rules earned almost nothing in 2009-2022, and the two intraday candidates have no cost-inclusive evidence. Multi-year flat or losing stretches are the expected case, not the tail.

Live results cannot confirm the trend sleeve. At a Sharpe of 0.2-0.4 the minimum track record is decades, so capital is committed on a literature prior plus non-contradiction tests, and the only live information is falsification.

Diversification is weaker than a multi-strategy label suggests. Gold and silver are 0.83-0.88 correlated, and the direction lock makes all sleeves long or short together. A turning point or gap hits every sleeve at once.

Gap and fast-market risk. Gold moved about 11-12% and silver 26-31% in one session on 30 Jan 2026. Stops fill at the next available price, off-hours books are thin, and the notional caps are the only protection that does not depend on a fill.

Venue risk on Binance metals perps: jurisdiction eligibility, a geo-block seen from a US host, off-hours index mechanics changed twice in 2026, only about 11 months of contract history, USDT settlement, and fee or margin changes without notice.

Funding drag. Longs paid roughly 6-11% a year from May 2026, with prints up to +0.5% per 4 hours, which is comparable to the whole gross edge the literature suggests for a long trend position. The carry veto and cost model reduce but do not remove this.

Proxy risk. Long backtests run on spot XAU/XAG from specific feeds, not on the traded perp. Spot metals are over-the-counter and feed-specific, and intraday M1 coverage and the carry model are assumptions until audited.

Overfitting through module growth. Each sleeve, filter and ablation is a trial. The ledger, small grids and Deflated Sharpe limit the damage, but any selection procedure still selects noise, and pressure to relax a gate after a near miss is the usual way these controls fail.

Implementation complexity. Several sleeves on a netting account with per-sleeve stops, resizes and locks is far more code than the requester's current bot. Bugs in sizing, duplicate entries or lost state are the realistic way to lose money quickly.

Silver-specific risk: squeeze and air-pocket behaviour, a 0.01 tick worth about 2 bps, weekend ranges of about 5%, thinner depth, and margin that brokers and exchanges have raised several-fold within days.

Capital and minimum size are unknown. Below roughly $2,000 the smaller silver positions are skipped, so the live portfolio differs from the tested one. On CFD venues minimum lots make the trend sleeve infeasible for small accounts.

Operator and legal risk: manual overrides or promoting a failing sleeve break the link between test and live. Reusing MQL5 Code Base source without a licence, or scraping it, breaches copyright and site terms.

Base rate: 74-89% of retail CFD accounts lose money, and backtest Sharpe had almost no power to predict live results in a large cohort (R-squared below 0.025). Passing this pipeline lowers the chance of a false positive; it does not show the bot is profitable.
designs.honest_expectation:
Most likely outcome: a sound risk engine, one trend sleeve that passes non-contradiction tests, and intraday candidates that stay in shadow.

The trend sleeve. If its long-run Sharpe is in the 0.2-0.4 range the literature gives per market before the post-2009 decay, then at full stage (about 5-7% annual volatility) it would earn low single-digit percent a year before funding drag, with multi-year flat or negative stretches. At pilot size the figures are a quarter of that. It could equally earn nothing; 2009-2022 shows what that looks like. Live trading will not settle the question within any practical horizon, because the minimum track record at that Sharpe is decades. What live trading can show is whether losses stay inside the bootstrap bands.

The intraday candidates. I expect both to fail on Binance, where a 10 bps round trip is 15-25% of a typical stop. My judgment, not a measured probability, is that the chance of either clearing every gate even under raw-spread CFD costs is well under one in four. The t >= 3 and Deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 hurdles are meant to be hard. The gold/silver ratio will not be traded.

What a multi-strategy structure buys here. Not much diversification: two metals at 0.85 correlation and a shared direction lock limit that. It buys a way to test catalog ideas with zero capital, per-module attribution, and one place where total risk is bounded.

What is and is not bounded. Loss limits are concrete: per-trade risk, daily and weekly limits, a drawdown kill at 4%, 8% or 15% by stage, and notional caps sized so a repeat of 30 January 2026 with every stop failing costs about 5% of equity. They are still not guarantees against gaps, venue failure or a bug.

Cost and base rate. Reaching first pilot capital takes about five to six months of build, validation and paper trading. The base rate for retail leveraged trading is that 70-90% of accounts lose. This design should lose slowly and visibly if there is no edge. I do not promise that it makes money.

designs.name: Sabika: modular all-in-one XAUUSD/XAGUSD Expert Advisor for MetaTrader 5
designs.thesis:
Taken literally, 'gather the features of all the open-source bots' fails. In the 264 MQL5 Code Base EAs that were read, 100% carry red flags, only 10 reach code quality 5, 18% of the 206 trading EAs are grid/martingale (27% of the gold/silver-titled ones), and only 106 of 206 always send a hard stop. The defensible version keeps the literal shape (one configurable all-in-one EA with many signal and management modules) but changes what is gathered.

1) The catalog's 108 'core'-verdict features are always on. Only 7 of them concern entry signals; the rest are risk sizing, account protection, execution safety, state recovery and telemetry. That plumbing is the real 'best of all the bots'.

2) A library of four pluggable signal modules sits on top. Each is re-implemented from a written spec (no Code Base code is copied, since it carries no licence), has its own magic number, and is treated as an unproven hypothesis. The research finds no peer-reviewed, cost-inclusive intraday breakout evidence on gold, no statistically established single-instrument trend edge, and classic MA rules failing once data snooping is controlled.

3) A Configuration Governor stops the all-in-one from becoming a curve-fitting machine: one active signal module per symbol by default (hard maximum two), at most two tuned parameters per module, a project-wide trial ledger capped at 45 configurations (the MinBTL bound for about 5 years of data), and real-account trading only with a preset hash that passed the validation gates.

The 27 'avoid'-verdict features (grids, martingale, confluence scores, self-optimisers, virtual stops, news straddles and others) are not compiled in. The product is a verifiable risk-and-execution framework that can host a strategy if one survives testing. It is not a claim that one will.
designs.platform:
MetaTrader 5, one MQL5 Expert Advisor (MQL5 only, no MT4 compatibility layer), attached to one chart and trading XAUUSD and XAGUSD through per-symbol context objects. Reasons: the literal request is about open-source EAs, which are MQL5; and the MT5 Strategy Tester in 'Every tick based on real ticks' mode with multi-symbol support is the strongest ready-made test tool in the research.

Constraints and their costs:
- The requester's Python/ccxt/Linux PaaS stack does not carry over. The official MetaTrader5 Python package is Windows-only and cannot use the tester, so the EA needs a Windows VPS or the MetaQuotes VPS. The design uses no DLL and no WebRequest, so it is compatible with the MetaQuotes VPS.
- Python is kept for offline analysis only (Deflated Sharpe, PBO, bootstrap, walk-forward driver) on the EA's CSV journal.
- The tester has no economic calendar, TimeGMT() equals server time in it, swaps appear to use today's specification, and market-order slippage is not modelled. The design carries its own DST rule engine, a CSV news replay and cost-stress runs for those gaps.

Assumptions (broker, account type and capital are unknown):
- Every contract property is read at runtime: digits, tick size, contract size (silver 5,000 oz vs a possibly 1,000 oz lot), filling mode, stops and freeze levels, swap table, sessions.
- Netting and hedging accounts are both supported, with one position per symbol.
- Server time is assumed to be the New-York-close convention (GMT+2/+3 on US DST) and is verified live; if it differs, a broker-offset profile input is required.

Not in scope for v1: running on Binance XAUUSDT/XAGUSDT perps. Their cost structure is the opposite (about 10 bps taker round trip against roughly 0.5 bps on a raw CFD account) and their history is only 10-11 months.

modules.responsibility: Owns OnInit/OnTick/OnTimer, wires the modules in a fixed order, and enforces the complexity budget that makes an all-in-one EA defensible.
features: 'Unified tick-plus-timer cycle: re-entrancy guard, throttle, snapshot, idempotent actions': OnTick and a 1-second OnTimer call one Cycle(); one position snapshot per cycle; XAGUSD is serviced from the timer when the EA sits on an XAUUSD chart
'Ordered pipeline: exits before entries, one entry gate that never blocks management': refresh data, then protection, then exits, then stop changes, then entries
'One context object per symbol inside a single EA, with shared account-level risk': properties always read for the position's own symbol, never _Symbol
'Signal/execution separation via narrow module interfaces': a signal returns direction, entry, SL, TP and expiry on closed bars; no signal code can call OrderSend

'Magic-number namespace per sub-strategy and direction, with permission switches and per-magic statistics': magic = base + 100 x symbol slot + module id; mutual lock of one position per symbol, forced on netting accounts
'Fail-fast input validation in OnInit': INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT for any invalid or over-budget configuration, so the optimiser discards the pass

Governor (own design, not from the catalog): Tier A safety features cannot be switched off on a live account; Tier B switches follow the approved preset; Tier C optional features are compiled but locked off until a validation report unlocks them

Governor limits: 1 signal module per symbol by default, hard maximum 2; at most 2 Tier C flags on; at most 2 tuned parameters per module; about 60-80 inputs in total, of which at most 8 are eligible for tuning

Config hash of all inputs plus build number stamped on every journal row; real-account trading needs AllowLive=true and the hash listed in approved_presets.csv, otherwise the EA stays in MONITOR mode ('Account precondition gates: live-arming guard')

modules.responsibility: Turns whatever the broker calls gold and silver into a verified instrument profile and refuses to trade on anything it cannot verify.
features: 'Metal symbol profile with suffix-tolerant detection': resolved by properties (base XAU/XAG, profit currency USD, full trade mode) with a manual override input; unrecognised symbol fails init

'Broker capability probe at init (filling mode, expiration type, account mode, input validation)': filling type derived from SYMBOL_FILLING_MODE and SYMBOL_TRADE_EXEMODE, never hard-coded (hard-coded FOK is a red flag in most of the SilverTrend family)
'Tick-size price rounding and instrument-scaled distance units': every input is an ATR multiple, an R multiple, a spread multiple or a percent of price; no pips or points anywhere
'Composite minimum stop-distance engine (stops level, freeze level, spread fallback, correct quote side)': minimum = max(stops level, freeze level, 3 x live spread) + 1 tick, re-read at every use
'Trade-validator class for broker constraints, with strict retcode handling'

Contract-size confirmation: gold expected 100 oz; silver must be confirmed by input as 5,000 or 1,000 oz (one broker sheet shows 1,000, unverified); mismatch aborts init; profile re-read each trading day because digits can change

Capital feasibility table at init ('Account precondition gates: minimum capital'): minimum-lot loss at each module's median stop over the last 60 sessions versus the risk budget; a module that would be skipped in more than half its setups is flagged INFEASIBLE_CAPITAL and disabled

modules.responsibility: Supplies closed-bar data, session ranges and a tester-safe clock to every other module.
features: 'Closed-bar-only signal evaluation with new-bar gate' (seen in 52 EAs) with per-symbol, per-timeframe bar timestamps
'Closed-bar gate that re-arms on data failure': the bar is marked consumed only after all buffers and filters were read successfully
'Closed-bar data layer: cached indicator handles and per-timeframe new-bar gates': handles created once in OnInit, shift 1 and 2 only
'Market/indicator data sanity and history-readiness guards': ATR must be finite, above zero and below 10% of price; failure aborts the cycle with a logged reason
'Session/opening range builder from M1 bars': range built from M1, frozen at window end, rebuilt from history on restart; a window with under 90% of expected M1 bars marks the day NO_TRADE

'DST-aware session anchoring and rule-based server offset': all windows defined in America/New_York and converted by US/EU DST rules; live cross-check against TimeTradeServer() minus TimeGMT(); unit tests on the March and October-November changeovers
'Trading-day rollover: baseline rebuild and daily state reset': day boundary 17:00 New York by default, with an input for a prop-firm clock

modules.responsibility: Hosts the pluggable entry modules (S1-S4 plus the S0 null control) behind one interface and one setup state machine.
features: S1 session range breakout: 'Closed-bar range breakout with buffer and entry window' plus 'Range-width and compression gate'
S2 'Liquidity sweep-and-reclaim (failed breakout) entry', modelled on the specs of 77639 (quality 5) and 77094 (quality 4), with the trend filter moved to closed bars
S3 and S4: 'Fresh closed-bar trend trigger: N-bar channel breakout or MA cross' (channel form after 77691, quality 5; MA form as a benchmark)
'Higher-timeframe trend-side filter on closed bars': one state source per module, read at shift 1, with an on/off switch for ablation
'Setup lifecycle state machine with single-use latches': armed, awaiting confirmation, consumed, expired; 'already traded' derived from deal history by magic and symbol
'Single evaluator for live and replay, with a filter-result bitmask as reason code' (the in-sample filter-combination rescoring is not built)
Level ownership rule: S1 owns the session range, S2 owns prior-day extremes and H1 pivots; never opposite positions on one symbol
'Independent long/short enable switches' as a diagnostic only; both sides are reported separately and the switch is never a tuned parameter

modules.responsibility: One CanOpen(reason) function that vetoes new risk only, never exits, and logs every veto with the measured value.
features: 'Gate pipeline with reason codes, veto logging and per-filter switches' and 'Single pre-trade gate with logged reasons and per-day entry limits'
'Cost-relative spread gate with hard cap, entry-only': Ask minus Bid plus round-trip commission must be at most 12% of the stop distance; backstop cap 4 bp of price for gold and 15 bp for silver
'Pre-trade feasibility and net-RR gate with logged reject reasons': infeasible setups are skipped, never reshaped

'Tradability gate: broker session table, pre-close margin, rollover blackout, stale-quote check': no entries 16:00-19:00 New York, none within 15 minutes of a session end, none on a quote older than 10 s (neutral in the tester)
'Entry time window with midnight wrap (minute resolution, per weekday)': windows fixed a priori from the session research, never optimised

'News blackout from the native MT5 economic calendar': USD high-impact events mapped explicitly to both metals; 30 minutes before to 30 minutes after NFP, CPI and PCE; 13:30-15:30 New York on FOMC days
'Tester-compatible news source: calendar CSV replay and date blacklist': UTC CSV loaded in the tester; a loud 'news filter inactive' log line when no source is present

'Closed-bar volatility shock pause (ATR ratio / bar range versus ATR)': block entries for 4 H1 bars when the last H1 true range exceeds 3 x ATR(20,H1) or ATR(5)/ATR(20) exceeds 2.0; fixed, compared against a no-filter control
'Setup-geometry sanity band normalised by ATR' and 'Attempt limiter: one attempt per day/window plus entry cooldown, persisted'
'Scheduled flatten and week-edge guards (Friday cutoff, weekly-open wait, daily flat time)': no entries in the first 60 minutes after the weekly open

modules.responsibility: Defines 1R in money for every trade and guarantees that rounding, margin and caps can only reduce size.
features: 'Loss-at-stop sizing via OrderCalcProfit' with a second pass on the rounded lot; the tick-value formula is not used (the report of wrong XAUUSD tick values is anecdotal, so this is a precaution)
'Never-round-up lot normalisation (skip below minimum)': the most common risk red flag in the gold EAs (78968, 75586, 79234) is raising to minimum lot
'Volatility-unit stop distance (ATR or gap-free mean range)' and 'Broker stops-level and freeze-level floor applied before sizing'
'Margin affordability pre-check with free-margin buffer': post-trade margin level at least 400%, so a 4x margin hike does not reach stop-out
'Aggregate exposure caps (total lots, positions, volume limit, pending reserve)': gold and silver counted as one correlated budget
'Hard ceilings: max lot, max risk money, bounded risk percent': compiled-in 1.0% per-trade ceiling; notional cap 2x equity per position
'Lot cap from remaining daily loss budget': planned loss at most 80% of what is left of the day's allowance
'Selectable risk base: fixed money, balance or equity': fixed money for backtests, min(balance, equity) live
'Init-time validation of the sizing configuration'
Tier C, locked off: 'Guarded minimum-lot fallback with a second risk cap' (1.5x base, every use counted) and 'Loss-streak risk throttle (reduction only)'

modules.responsibility: The single choke point for every order, modify and close; turns broker rejections into classified, logged outcomes.
features: 'Pre-trade permission and broker-limit gate with distinct reason codes' and 'OrderCheck preflight inside the send path' (closing and reducing orders are always exempt)

'Protected entry: stops anchored to the real fill, fail-safe close, slippage tolerance': SL/TP sent with the order where accepted, otherwise attached at once; 3 attempts in 2 s, then immediate close; trade closed if realised risk exceeds 1.3x planned

'Decide once, deliver with a bounded retry window and failure circuit breaker': at most 2 entry attempts within 20 s of the signal bar open, only if price drift is under 0.1 x ATR; entries paused after 3 consecutive failures
'Retcode-classified retry and backoff with attempt budgets': transient, re-compute, wait-state and fatal classes; timestamps, never Sleep in the tick handler
'Transaction-confirmed order state machine (in-flight guard + deferred deal queue)' with a 10 s timeout that falls back to polling
'Read-back confirmation of fills, modifies and closes' and 'Duplicate-entry prevention and restart-safe ownership'
'Safe modify/close wrapper: freeze-level guard, no-change skip, minimum step, throttle': minimum stop improvement 0.1 x ATR, at most one modify per position per 5 s
'Market-availability gate: broker session table, quote freshness, data readiness' and 'Volume normalisation and margin affordability check'
'Emergency flatten routine (snapshot, pendings first, retry until flat)'

modules.responsibility: Keeps every position inside its planned risk and applies exits in a fixed precedence that can only tighten.
features: 'Initial protective stop from structure or ATR, clamped and broker-valid' and 'Take-profit as an R-multiple of the stop distance': both broker-side on every position
'Single SL modification gateway: tighten-only, broker-valid, step-gated, throttled' (seen in 43 EAs)
'Staged exit pipeline with fixed precedence and profit-only trail activation': newSL = max(currentSL, candidates) for longs, mirrored for shorts
'Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop': default exit of S3; off for S1, S2 and S4 so plain SL/TP is the baseline
'Time stop in traded bars' and 'Session-end / end-of-day flatten and stale-position cleanup': intraday modules flat at 15:45 New York, retried until flat
'Auto-attach missing protective stop (naked-position safety net)' and 'Idempotent SL/TP reconciliation and missing-stop repair'
'Restart-safe per-position exit state and strict ownership': initial 1R stored at entry, keyed by login, symbol, magic and position identifier
'Signal-driven exits and verified close-then-reverse': only the opposite-channel exit of S3, with the close verified before any new entry
Tier C, locked off: 'Breakeven with net-of-cost lock offset' and 'Structure-based trail (Donchian or swing) behind a pluggable candidate-SL interface'

modules.responsibility: Account-level limits shared by both metals, enforced until flat and remembered across restarts.
features: 'Daily loss limit on equity (closed + floating) with configurable day boundary' on one account-level number for both symbols
'Day reference rebuilt from deal history (deposit-aware, scoped)': a restart cannot grant a fresh loss budget
'Total drawdown limit: static floor or trailing equity high-water mark': permanent lock, cleared only by an explicit operator input
'Act-before-limit buffer on credit-free equity': limits trigger at 80-90% of their value
'Crash-proof persisted lock state machine': until-timestamp locks, escalate-only, tester keys isolated, mirrored to a file because terminal globals expire after about four weeks
'Latched flatten with enforcement until flat' (survives the daily break and the weekend)
'Stop-loss watchdog for naked positions': re-attach, then forced close after 5 failures
'Trade-frequency caps: daily/session quota, entry cooldown, one-setup-per-day key' and 'Exposure caps: positions, per-direction levels, single direction, entry spacing'
'Account precondition gates: live-arming guard, minimum capital, margin level'
'Early-warning alerts and visible block reasons' at 80% of each limit
Tier C, locked off: prop-firm profile (firm reset clock, static or trailing maximum loss, news execution window, 'Profit-target lock' in its challenge form only)

modules.responsibility: Makes a restart, reconnect or VPS reboot a non-event by treating the broker as the database.
features: 'Ownership by symbol + magic + position identifier': magic 0 and foreign magics are never touched
'Stateless restart recovery from broker state': positions, orders and deal history are re-read at init and each cycle
'Minimal durable store for non-derivable state': initial risk, day baseline, equity high-water mark, lock and flatten latches, operator mode; written on change with GlobalVariablesFlush
'Startup preflight: connection, permissions and account identity': nothing is loaded, saved or traded while disconnected or before history sync
'Timer plus tick processing with throttle': guards run from the timer; signal decisions stay on the closed-bar gate
OnDeinit saves state for every reason code and never flattens
Tier C, locked off: 'Single-instance lock with heartbeat'

modules.responsibility: Produces the same evidence in the tester and live, so every decision and every cost can be reconciled.
features: 'Position-level trade journal rebuilt from deals (net of all costs)': one CSV row per closed position, identical code in tester and live
'R-multiple against the initial stop, plus MFE/MAE per trade' and P/L in basis points of price
'Session, weekday, hour and exit-reason tags with bucket tables' (tags only; no filter may be built from them without out-of-sample evidence)
'Decision journal with reason codes and a single order-send choke point': one line per evaluated signal, cannot be disabled
'Execution-cost telemetry: signed slippage, fill latency and spread' including stop-loss exits
'Risk audit: sizing line, planned-versus-realised loss, never-widen-stop check': violations count as test failures
'Logging plumbing: levels, change-based throttling, durable append-only CSV', one file per symbol and magic
'OnTester criterion with hard gates and early/late consistency' with long and short reported separately
'Cost-aware expectancy checks: breakeven win rate and pessimistic bar resolution'

strategies.name: S1 Session range breakout (closed-bar)
strategies.logic:
Range: high/low of M1 bars in [03:00, 08:00) New York, frozen at 08:00 (preset PreNY). One alternative preset is declared in advance: range [19:00, 02:00), entries [02:00, 05:00).
Width gate: 0.15 <= range width / ATR(14, D1, shift 1) <= 0.70, and width >= 8 x live spread; otherwise no trade that day.
Trigger: the first closed M15 bar inside [08:00, 11:30) New York whose close is above rangeHigh + B (long) or below rangeLow - B (short), where B = max(0.10 x ATR(14, M15)[1], 2 x spread), and whose previous bar had not already closed beyond that level.
Filter (switch, default on, ablated): long only if H4 close[1] > EMA200(H4)[1]; mirrored for shorts.
Entry: market at the next bar open; one attempt per side per day; one position per symbol.
Stop: range midpoint. D = |entry - midpoint|. If D < 0.6 x ATR(14, H1)[1], widen to that floor. If D > 1.5 x ATR(14, H1)[1], skip (STOP_TOO_WIDE).
Target: 2.0 x D, recomputed from the actual fill.
Exits: SL, TP, flat at 15:45 New York. No breakeven and no trail in the baseline.
Tunable (maximum 2, 3 values each): buffer factor {0.05, 0.10, 0.20} and R multiple {1.5, 2.0, 3.0}. Everything else is fixed.
strategies.timeframe: Range from M1; signal on M15; filter on H4; stop band from H1 ATR; width gate from D1 ATR
strategies.symbols: XAUUSD first. XAGUSD runs the same inputs as a robustness check and stays disabled unless it passes on its own.
strategies.rationale: This is the best-engineered family in the code reading (75586, 76153, 78688, 78293, 17465) and uses four core catalog features. The hours follow the measured 2026 session shape: range is highest relative to spread at 08:00-11:00 New York, and no London-open surge is visible. The edge itself is unproven. The research found no peer-reviewed, cost-inclusive breakout test on gold, and an index-CFD replication saw the gross edge consumed by costs. It is a hypothesis that must beat the random-entry control.

strategies.name: S2 Liquidity sweep-and-reclaim (failed breakout)
strategies.logic:
Levels: prior-day high and low (17:00 New York day) plus confirmed H1 5/5 swing pivots from the last 5 days, at most 10 levels, each single-use.
Sweep (short side; long is mirrored): a closed M15 bar with high >= level + 0.10 x ATR(14, M15) and close < level.
Confirmation: within the next 3 closed bars, one bar closes below the sweep bar's body low with range >= 0.30 x ATR(14, M15); otherwise the setup expires.
Filter: H1 close[1] < EMA50(H1)[1] for shorts, read on closed bars.
Entry: market at the next bar open, inside [03:00, 11:30) New York.
Stop: sweep extreme + 0.10 x ATR(14, M15). Required: 0.5 x ATR(14, M15) <= D <= 1.5 x ATR(14, H1), else skip.
Target: 2.0 x D. Exits: SL, TP, flat at 15:45 New York.
A level is deleted when a bar closes through it and price does not reclaim it within the 3-bar window.
Tunable: wick multiple {0.05, 0.10, 0.20} and R multiple {1.5, 2.0, 3.0}.
strategies.timeframe: M15 signal; H1 pivots and trend filter; D1 for prior-day levels
strategies.symbols: XAUUSD only in v1. Silver's spread puts wick-edge stops proportionally closer to noise.
strategies.rationale: It is the best-specified reversal entry in the sample (77639 quality 5, 77094 quality 4), with ATR-qualified wicks, a confirmation window and single-use levels. The catalog rates it optional with overfit risk 3, and it trades against S1 at shared levels, hence the ownership rule and the one-module-per-symbol default. No published evidence supports it; it is built last and tested standalone.

strategies.name: S3 Channel trend (Donchian) with two pre-declared presets
strategies.logic:
Preset T-fast: H4, entry channel N = 20, exit channel 10. Preset T-slow: D1, N = 55, exit channel 20.
Long: close[1] > highest high of bars 2..N+1, and close[2] was not above its own channel (fresh break), and close[1] > EMA200[1] (switch, ablated). Short is mirrored. Both sides are always enabled; long-only is prohibited as a setting.
Stop: 2.0 x ATR(14)[1] of the signal timeframe; the lot is sized from it.
Exit: chandelier stop = best close since entry - 3.0 x ATR(14)[1], applied only once it is beyond entry; or a close through the opposite exit channel. No fixed target.
Delivery: an H4 bar that closes inside the 16:00-19:00 New York blackout drops its signal. A D1 signal is delivered at the first tick after 19:00 New York only if the spread gate passes and price is within 0.25 x ATR(14, D1) of the signal close.
No new entries after Friday 12:00 New York.
Weekend rule at Friday 15:30 New York: compute the loss from a 2% (gold) or 4% (silver) adverse gap with OrderCalcProfit; if it exceeds 2 x the planned 1R, close; otherwise hold.
Tunable: nothing. The two presets are the only trials.
strategies.timeframe: H4 (T-fast) or D1 (T-slow); positions held overnight
strategies.symbols: XAUUSD and XAGUSD with identical inputs; silver at half the risk percent; same-direction positions in both count against one combined risk cap.
strategies.rationale: The channel form comes from 77691, the highest-quality gold EA in the sample, without its admitted long-only regime fit. Slow trend is the only family with long, multi-source evidence, but that evidence is for 43-67 diversified markets, decayed after 2009 (12-month trend Sharpe 1.07 before, 0.06 in 2009-2022), and is not statistically established on a single instrument. Long gold also costs roughly 5-8% a year in swap. Expect a per-instrument Sharpe of about 0.2-0.4 at best and multi-year flat periods. Stops of 2 x ATR are roughly $75 (H4) to $180 (D1) per ounce at 2026 volatility, so at 0.5% risk and a 0.01 lot this module needs an account of roughly $15,000-36,000 (my estimate from the research ATR figures).

strategies.name: S4 EMA alignment benchmark (the requester's own entry, on closed bars)
strategies.logic:
M30 closed bars. Long: EMA9[1] > EMA21[1] > EMA50[1], EMA9[2] <= EMA21[2] (fresh cross between bars 2 and 1), and close[1] > EMA50[1]. Short is mirrored.
Two optional confirmations, default off, each counted as a trial if switched on: RSI(14)[1] between 50 and 70 for longs (30 to 50 for shorts); MACD histogram rising, hist[1] > hist[2].
The volume-spike condition is removed.
Entry window [03:00, 11:30) New York; market at the next bar open; one position per symbol.
Stop: 1.5 x ATR(14, M30)[1]. Target: 3.0 x ATR (2R). Flat at 15:45 New York.
Tunable: nothing in v1.
strategies.rationale: This is a transparent benchmark, not a candidate edge. It ports the logic of the requester's crypto bot so they can see it measured on metals, after costs, against the random-entry control. The closed-bar MA form follows 78968 (quality 4). The evidence is against it: on 5-minute spot gold and silver, standard moving-average parameters showed no predictive power before costs, and 7,846 technical rules on commodity futures failed once data snooping was controlled. Volume is dropped because tick volume on metal CFDs is the broker's quote count, not traded volume. It is built first because it exercises the whole pipeline with the simplest signal.

strategies.name: S0 Random-entry control (Strategy Tester only)
strategies.logic: Replaces the entry decision of the module under test with a seeded coin flip (MathSrand(seed), MathRand) at the same entry frequency, the same long/short mix and the same trading hours. Stops, targets, sizing, filters and the cost model are untouched. 200 seeds per comparison. OnInit refuses this mode outside the tester.
strategies.timeframe: Same as the module under test
strategies.symbols: Same as the module under test
strategies.rationale: It implements 'Random-entry benchmark mode (null hypothesis)'. Gold's long drift and a 2R exit geometry can make random long entries look profitable, so every module must exceed the 95th percentile of this distribution before its result is credited to the signal. It has nothing to tune, so it cannot be overfitted.

features_excluded.feature: Grid, martingale, averaging-down and recovery baskets (26 EAs; e.g. GoldWarrior02b, the XANDER family, Sniper Gold Hybrid Recovery, Daily Zone Recovery)
features_excluded.why: They have no edge of their own and a documented path to ruin: a high win rate traded for a rare account-sized loss. Silver fell 26-31% and gold about 11-12% in one session on 30 January 2026, which overwhelms any grid spacing. Adding to a loser and multiplying lots after a loss are impossible in this code: one position per symbol, risk is never increased.

features_excluded.feature: 'Lot sizing not tied to the stop' and 'Scaling size up by signal confidence, Kelly or win streaks'
features_excluded.why: Money at risk per trade becomes undefined, and size becomes another fitted dimension. Gold setups produce too few trades to estimate a Kelly fraction. Risk per trade is flat.

features_excluded.feature: 'Weighted additive confluence score gate' and 'Weighted-score voting with open/close thresholds, or supervisor override by specialist models'
features_excluded.why: Weights and thresholds are arbitrary correlated parameters that cannot be ablated (catalog overfit 5). This is the usual way an all-in-one EA combines signals and the most direct route to a fitted backtest. Here modules are independent, never blended, and every filter is a separate boolean with its own switch.

features_excluded.feature: 'Self-optimising and learned signal generators', perceptron/ML votes and the MathRand 'quantum' term (Gold Dust, Quantum Gold Silver Trader)
features_excluded.why: In-EA adaptivity is continuous in-sample optimisation with hidden state, and results cannot be reproduced. Randomness in a signal makes a backtest meaningless.

features_excluded.feature: 'Oscillator zone-exit / band re-entry reversal trigger' and other short-horizon mean reversion
features_excluded.why: Popular (22 EAs) mainly as the trigger of averaging systems. No cost-surviving evidence was found on gold or silver; the limited evidence points to continuation after large moves.

features_excluded.feature: 'Tick-driven triggers: z-score bursts, renko bricks, intrabar displacement' and 'Tick-velocity fast-market detector'
features_excluded.why: They depend on the broker's tick feed and the tester's tick model, so they are not honestly testable. Short-horizon gross edges are the same order as metals costs.

features_excluded.feature: 'Price-chasing and stacked pending orders' and 'News straddle / event breakout trading'
features_excluded.why: The tester cannot reproduce release-second spread and stop slippage, so the backtest measures the fill model. The news calendar is used only to stand aside.

features_excluded.feature: 'Two-sided pending stop bracket with broker-side expiry and OCO' (deferred, not rejected)
features_excluded.why: v1 enters at market on closed bars, which the tester reproduces faithfully. Stop orders at the range edge fill where slippage is worst and need the whole pending-order hygiene set. The slot exists; it is not built.

features_excluded.feature: 'Virtual / stealth SL-TP levels hidden from the broker'
features_excluded.why: It contradicts the invariant that no position exists without a confirmed broker-side stop, and it disappears when the terminal or VPS is down.

features_excluded.feature: 'Basket / aggregate exits', 'Basket money / equity-ratio take-profit close-all', 'Equity / basket profit giveback ratchet', 'Grid-basket rescue devices' and the daily profit stop
features_excluded.why: These are exit rules for averaging baskets presented as protection. Money targets do not scale with volatility, and a daily profit cap removes the few strong days a trend system lives on.

features_excluded.feature: 'Duplex: fully separate long-side and short-side parameter sets' and long-only as a tuned choice
features_excluded.why: It doubles the parameters and memorises the drift of the test window. 77691's own header admits its long-only default was chosen because shorts lost in 2020-2026.

features_excluded.feature: 'Generic indicator-to-signal adapter table' and any iCustom dependency
features_excluded.why: It makes indicator shopping cheap and hides repainting inputs. Every signal here is compiled in and reads only built-in indicators on closed bars.

features_excluded.feature: 'Fair value gap / order-block zone retest', 'Scale-out ladder in R-multiples', 'Pyramiding into profit with capped adds', 'Secondary profit-lock ratchets', 'Compression/expansion day filters', 'Over-extension filter', 'Scale-free candle-quality metrics'
features_excluded.why: All are optional in the catalog with overfit risk 3-4, and each adds two or more thresholds. They are held back by the trial budget: the parameters they would add cost more evidence than about 5 years of data can supply. Partial closes are also impossible at minimum lot on small accounts.

features_excluded.feature: 'Cross-symbol directional proxy' and gold/silver ratio trading
features_excluded.why: The gold-silver cointegration is unstable; a published z-score reversion trade lost heavily after 2020 (magnitudes unreliable, direction clear). It would also couple the two symbols' tests.

features_excluded.feature: 'Runtime strategy overrides, per-ticket toggles and manual trade buttons' and 'User-drawn chart objects as trigger levels'
features_excluded.why: Every runtime override makes the live system different from the tested one, and none of it can be backtested.

features_excluded.feature: 'Remote command queue with acknowledgement', WebRequest bridges, licence gates and the 'Veto-only model confirmation layer'
features_excluded.why: A network dependency and remote-control surface on a live account (the red flag in 75652). None of it runs in the tester, and WebRequest-based control is not allowed in Market products.

features_excluded.feature: 'Count-based or drawdown-rescaled fitness formulas', 'Composite 0-100 risk score as a control input' and 'Staged optimisation switch'
features_excluded.why: They reward high-win-rate shapes, dilute a breached limit, or hide the real number of fitted parameters. Limits are independent hard gates.

features_excluded.feature: 'Pending-to-market fallback', 'Close-by netting and double-lot reversal' and 'Macro abstraction layer for MT4/MT5 trade calls'
features_excluded.why: They silently change the strategy's semantics, add failure paths, or double the test surface for no benefit.

features_excluded.feature: Copying or bundling any MQL5 Code Base source
features_excluded.why: The Code Base has no published licence, so unlicensed files are all rights reserved, and the one staff statement on record forbids re-publishing outside mql5.com. Ideas are re-implemented from written specs with a provenance log.

features_excluded.feature: Tick volume as a required entry condition (the requester's volume-spike rule)
features_excluded.why: On metal CFDs it is a broker-specific quote count that differs between history and live.

features_excluded.feature: Binance XAUUSDT/XAGUSDT perps as an execution venue in v1
features_excluded.why: Fees dominate there (about 10 bps taker round trip), history is 10-11 months across two changes in off-hours pricing, and the contract trades weekends. It would be a separate Python project reusing the risk rules, not this EA.

designs.risk_model:
All values are policy defaults fixed before testing and never optimised. Capital is unknown, so everything is in percent, R, ATR or spread units.

Per trade
1. Risk 0.50% of min(balance, equity) on XAUUSD and 0.25% on XAGUSD (silver beta to gold is about 2, its relative spread is about 3x worse). Compiled-in ceiling 1.0%. Backtests use fixed-money risk so years are comparable.
2. Lot from OrderCalcProfit at the stop actually placed, floored to the volume step. If the result is below minimum lot the trade is skipped and logged, never rounded up.
3. Stop distance at least max(stops level, freeze level, 3 x live spread) and at least 0.5 x ATR of the signal timeframe. Sanity bounds: ATR below 10% of price; stop below 2% of price (gold) or 4% (silver) for intraday modules, 6% and 12% for S3.
4. Spread plus round-trip commission at most 12% of the stop distance at send time. Backstop caps: 4 bp of price on gold, 15 bp on silver.
5. Notional at most 2x equity per position; post-trade margin level at least 400%, so a 4x broker margin hike does not reach a 50% stop-out.
6. If the realised risk after the fill exceeds 1.3x planned, the trade is closed at once.

Portfolio
7. One position per symbol, two in total. Combined open risk across both metals at most 1.0% of equity; they are one correlated bet (correlation 0.83-0.88).
8. At most 2 entries per symbol and 3 in total per day; one attempt per side per module per day; no re-entry on the bar a trade closed.

Account locks (equity-based, net of swap and commission, credit excluded, persisted)
9. Daily loss limit 2.0% of the day reference (higher of balance and equity at 17:00 New York). It triggers at 80% of the limit (1.6%): flatten, lock until rollover. Each new trade must fit inside 80% of the remaining allowance.
10. Weekly loss limit 4.0%: EXIT_ONLY until the next weekly open.
11. Total drawdown 10% from the persisted equity high-water mark, triggering at 9%: flatten and permanent lock, cleared only by the operator. A static mode exists for prop rules.
12. Capital floor: a module whose minimum-lot loss exceeds its budget in more than half of recent setups is disabled at init.

Time-based
13. No new entries 16:00-19:00 New York, in the first 60 minutes after the weekly open, or inside the news windows. Intraday modules are flat by 15:45 New York. S3 applies the Friday gap-stress rule.

Rough capital implications (my estimates from the research range figures, to be replaced by the init table): gold intraday stops are about $10-35 per ounce, so a 0.01 lot at 0.5% risk needs roughly $3,000-7,000; a 5,000-oz silver lot at 0.25% needs roughly $5,000-12,000; S3 needs about $15,000-36,000. Below those sizes most signals are skipped by design.

What the model does not cover: a gap through the stop (2026 weekend gaps exceeded 1% in gold about one weekend in eight) fills at the next price, and whether the account has negative-balance protection is unknown.
designs.validation_plan:
Each module ends with one of three statuses: REJECTED, UNPROVEN (may trade only at minimum size) or SUPPORTED. Gates marked (convention) have no primary statistical source.

G1 Data. Final tests only in 'Every tick based on real ticks' on the broker and account type to be traded. Pass: real-tick share at least 99% and History Quality at least 95% over the window (my thresholds). Periods before the first real-tick date are labelled generated-tick and count toward no gate. The Recorder runs at least 4 weeks to compare live spread by hour with tester spread.

G2 Invariants, zero tolerance in every run. Positions without a broker stop after the attach window: 0. Stop-widening events: 0. Trades whose planned loss exceeds budget: 0. Minimum-lot round-ups: 0. Journal net P/L equals the tester report to 0.01. Daily-lock overshoot no larger than the buffer plus logged gap slippage. All built-in self-tests OK.

G3 Standalone test per module, pre-declared defaults, no optimisation. Commission as at the broker, fixed delay equal to measured ping, plus one Random Delay run.
- Trades: at least 200 for S1, S2, S4 and 100 for S3 T-fast (convention). T-slow is reported as not testable on broker history unless imported long history yields at least 60 trades.
- Bootstrap 5th percentile of mean R above 0 at base cost, and mean R above 0 with spread x1.5 and one extra tick of slippage each side.
- Long-only and short-only mean R each at least -0.05R.
- Mean R positive in at least 3 of 4 calendar sub-periods and never below -0.10R, with low-volatility 2024 and high-volatility 2026 both covered.
- Module mean R at or above the 95th percentile of 200 random-entry seeds (S0).
Any failure: REJECTED.

G4 Trial budget and tuning. Complete grid search only, no genetic runs. At most 9 configurations per module and 45 across the whole project, counted from the trial ledger (the published bound for about 5 years of data at a target Sharpe of 1, assuming independent trials). Pass: at least 7 of 9 cells positive and the chosen cell is the centre of the plateau, not an isolated peak (convention).

G5 Statistical evidence, computed in Python from exported daily returns. Deflated Sharpe Ratio at least 0.95 with the ledger's trial count, and t = annualised Sharpe x sqrt(years) at least 3.0. PBO by CSCV (S = 16) is reported; at most 0.05 is the strict level but it is noisy for 9 configurations, so it is informational. Pass: SUPPORTED. Fail with G3 and G4 passed: UNPROVEN. At a Sharpe of 1, t of 3 needs about 9 years, so most modules will end UNPROVEN at best.

G6 Walk-forward (convention). Scripted anchored walk-forward, 6 windows: efficiency at least 50% and at least 4 of 6 out-of-sample windows profitable. A final 6-month holdout is opened once. Fail: REJECTED.

G7 Ablation. Each Tier B filter is run on and off against a no-filter control. A non-safety filter stays on only if out-of-sample mean R improves and trade count falls by less than half.

G8 Combination, only if two modules pass. Correlation of daily R below 0.5, and bootstrap 95th-percentile maximum drawdown (1,000 resamples in R, read as a lower bound) at most 8%. Otherwise run one module.

G9 Cross-feed. Repeat on a second broker's real ticks or imported ticks as a custom symbol: same sign and mean R within 50% of the first feed. Run the same inputs on XAGUSD; failure keeps silver disabled.

G10 Stress. Replay 30 January 2026, the NFP, CPI and FOMC hours, and an injected weekend gap of 2% (gold) and 4% (silver). Pass: no stop-out, and locks hold across a forced restart mid-position and mid-flatten on demo.

G11 Demo parity. At least 8 weeks and 30 trades. Re-run the tester over the same period. Pass: at least 90% of trades match on the bar, median entry slippage and spread inside the tester assumptions, veto counts by hour within 20%. This tests implementation, not edge: a track record needs about 0.7 years at Sharpe 2 and 2.7 years at Sharpe 1.

G12 Live at minimum size (0.25% risk). Pre-written disable rules: live drawdown beyond the bootstrap 95th percentile; median realised/planned loss ratio above 1.3; or mean R after 50 trades below the 5th percentile of the backtest bootstrap.

If no module passes G3, the EA ships as a framework in MONITOR mode with all signals disabled on real accounts. That is a valid result of this plan.
