build_phases.phase: P8 Demo, parity check and minimum-size live (at least 8 weeks of demo, then open-ended)
build_phases.deliverable: MONITOR mode, then demo trading with the approved presets, a parity report, then live at 0.25% risk with the G12 disable rules written down in advance.
build_phases.acceptance: G11 passes: at least 30 demo trades, at least 90% matched to the tester, slippage and spread inside assumptions. Live starts only for presets whose hash is approved. Any G12 rule that fires disables the module without discussion.

main_risks: No signal module passes. The research supports this as the base case: no cost-inclusive breakout evidence on gold, no established single-instrument trend edge, MA rules failing after data-snooping control. The result would be a well-built framework with nothing proven to run on it.

Combinatorial overfitting is the specific danger of an all-in-one design. Four modules, a few presets and a handful of switches reach the 45-configuration bound quickly; beyond it a zero-skill strategy is expected to show an in-sample Sharpe of 1. The Governor and ledger only help if every run is logged honestly.

Complexity risk. About 108 core features is a large code base, and all 264 EAs read, including the quality-5 ones, carried red flags. More code means more failure paths and a test matrix of module x account mode x broker.

Regime risk. Gold is about 31% and silver about 60% below their January 2026 records, daily ranges are roughly three times 2024 in dollars, and the macro backdrop has flipped. Recent gold-only backtests are contaminated by a strong bull market.

Tail and gap risk. On 30 January 2026 silver fell 26-31% and gold about 11-12% in one session; in 2026 about one weekend in eight gapped more than 1% in gold. Stops fill at the next price, and negative-balance protection is unknown.

Broker dependence. Contract size (silver 5,000 or 1,000 oz), digits, filling mode, margin windows, swap and real-tick depth all differ by broker and can change. Margin was raised from 5% to 20% on silver at one broker with a few days' notice, applied to open positions.

Tester optimism. Market-order slippage and liquidity are not modelled, swaps appear to use today's values, the calendar is unavailable, and generated-tick spread is unreliable. Live results will be worse than the backtest by an amount only live trading can measure.

Small-account infeasibility. With a 0.01 minimum lot, intraday gold needs roughly $3,000-7,000 at 0.5% risk and the trend module far more; silver is largely untradeable on small accounts. On a small account the EA will mostly log skipped trades.

Platform switch. The requester's stack is Python on a Linux PaaS. This design needs MQL5, a Windows host or the MetaQuotes VPS, and a new broker relationship, and little of the existing bot's code carries over.
Correlation. Gold and silver are one bet with different leverage; running both adds cost and tail risk more than diversification.

Licensing and distribution. Unlicensed Code Base code is all rights reserved. This design is for private use from re-implemented ideas; selling it or publishing the source raises separate questions, and separate gold and silver versions that differ only in settings would fall under the Market's duplicate-product rule.
Operator risk. An EA with 60-80 inputs invites tinkering. The approved-preset hash is the only barrier between the tested system and an untested one.
designs.honest_expectation:
I do not expect this bot to be profitable, and nothing in the evidence lets me say it will be. Roughly 74-89% of retail CFD accounts lose money. The realistic claim is narrower: losses are bounded per trade (0.5%), per day (2%) and in total (10%), every decision is logged with a reason, and the tester and the live account can be reconciled trade by trade.

What the all-in-one approach costs:
- Most of the work buys no edge. About 100 of the 108 core features are plumbing. They stop the avoidable losses seen in the open-source EAs (no stop, minimum-lot round-ups, lost state after a restart); they do not make money.
- Gathering signals subtracts rather than adds. Each extra module, preset or switch spends part of a budget of about 45 honest trials for 5 years of data. That is why the design allows one module per symbol and two tuned parameters, which is far less 'all-in-one' than the request implies.
- The likely outcome is that none or one of the four signal modules clears the gates, and that the survivor is labelled UNPROVEN, because a t-statistic of 3 at a Sharpe of 1 needs about 9 years of data.
- If the trend module survives, the research suggests a per-instrument Sharpe of about 0.2-0.4 before costs at best, near zero for static rules in 2009-2022, with multi-year flat or losing stretches and a swap drag of roughly 5-8% a year on long gold. The intraday modules have documented gross edges of only a few basis points, the same order as costs.
- Time: about 4-5 months of build and testing plus at least 8 weeks of demo before the first minimum-size live trade (my estimate). Statistical confirmation of a live edge then takes roughly 0.7 to 2.7 years.
- Money: accounts under about $3,000 will see most signals skipped; silver and the trend module need considerably more.
- Maintenance: a larger code base, broker-specific behaviour, and a platform change away from the requester's Python/Linux setup.

A single-strategy bot on the same safety core would be cheaper to build and easier to validate. The all-in-one form is defensible only because its switches are locked behind validation. If the Governor is bypassed to turn on more modules or filters until the backtest looks good, the result will be a fitted backtest.

designs.name: Metals Core v1 - Python on Binance USD-M XAU/XAG perpetuals, venue-portable, survival-first (platform-pragmatic proposal)
designs.thesis:
Do not build the union of all open-source bots. Of the 264 EAs read, 206 trade and every one carries red flags; 18% are grid or martingale (27% of the gold/silver-titled ones), only 106 of 206 always send a hard stop (43% of the gold-titled), and 141 of 264 score quality 1-2 out of 5. What the few quality 4-5 EAs share is not a signal but plumbing: closed-bar decisions, loss-at-stop sizing, a server-side stop on every position, restart-safe state, account-level locks, and a logged reason for every skipped trade. The proposal takes that plumbing in full, takes exactly one entry engine, and refuses the rest.

Platform answer: stay in Python and trade the gold and silver perpetuals that already exist on the requester's own venue (Binance USD-M XAUUSDT / XAGUSDT, confirmed trading on 2026-11-13) through ccxt on the existing Railway worker. This gives the fastest verifiable result (same API, wallet, deployment), 0.001 oz order increments that let even a small account size a wide volatility stop correctly, and one code path for backtest and live. It is not free: the venue is fee-dominated (about 10 bps per taker round trip, roughly 20x a raw-spread CFD account), has only about 11 months of its own history, charges 4-hourly funding and trades through weekends on thin liquidity. Those costs remove scalping and intraday breakouts here, which is acceptable because the published evidence for them on gold is folklore. The one family that is both affordable on this venue and has long published evidence is slow trend following, so v1 has one live candidate: a closed-session channel breakout with an ATR chandelier exit on New-York-close daily bars, symmetric long/short, identical parameters for both metals, silver at half risk.

MQL5 is deferred, not dismissed. It is opened only if the venue probe fails, if a regulated or prop account is required, or if the requester deliberately chooses an intraday family that needs about 1 bp costs; a venue adapter keeps that door open without rewriting strategy, risk or journal code. The MetaTrader5 Python package is rejected outright.

Honest stance: single-instrument trend following is not a statistically established edge, and the most likely validation outcome is weak evidence or a fail. The design treats zero edge minus costs as the default, pre-registers pass/fail gates, and makes the verifiable execution and risk engine plus an honest test report the deliverable that has value whatever the strategy verdict is. One finding from reading the requester's current bot matters for that goal: its '1% risk' sizing ignores the stop distance and its 5% daily-loss stop can never fire (details under platform), so 'stay in Python' means keep the runtime, not the trading core.
designs.platform:
DECISION: Stay in Python. Venue: Binance USD-M XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT perpetuals via ccxt, on the existing Railway Linux worker. Not MQL5 now. Never the MetaTrader5 Python package. Conditional on a read-only Phase 0 go/no-go probe.

WHY THIS IS FASTEST TO A VERIFIABLE RESULT (research label: confirmed unless stated)
- Same API, margin wallet and deployment as the bot the requester already runs. New work is a one-time TradFi-Perps agreement and an eligibility check.
- Contracts are real and liquid: gold about $2.26B per weekday in Oct 2026, quoted spread one tick (0.01 USDT, about 0.025 bps; estimate from trades), price step 0.01, quantity step 0.001 oz. Silver thinner: about $876M per weekday, one tick is about 1.9 bps.
- Binance publishes free trades, 1m klines, funding, mark/index/premium and book-depth files for both symbols, so execution-realistic replay needs no vendor.
- ccxt 4.5.92 already maps the tradingSchedule and TradFi-agreement endpoints.

WHY IT SIZES CORRECTLY FOR UNKNOWN CAPITAL (own arithmetic from the research figures)
- A 3 x ATR daily stop on gold is about $270 per oz. On a 100-oz CFD contract the minimum 0.01 lot is 1 oz, so the smallest possible trade risks about $270: that needs about $54,000 of equity at 0.5% risk. Silver on a 5,000-oz contract: 50 oz x about $6.5 = about $324, i.e. about $130,000 at 0.25% risk.
- On the perp, 0.001 oz steps make the same stop cost about $0.27 per step. With the reported (unverified) 5 USDT minimum notional, gold is tradable at 0.5% risk from about $70 of equity and at the 0.10% staging risk from about $350; silver from about $265 and $1,320.
- So the catalog rule 'Never-round-up lot normalisation (skip below minimum)' leaves a small CFD account with no trades at all on a slow-trend stop, while here it almost never binds.

WHY IT IS EASIER TO MAINTAIN
- One language, one repo, pytest and CI instead of a second toolchain.
- Time zones: Python zoneinfo gives exact America/New_York and Europe/London rules. In the MT5 tester TimeGMT() equals server time, so offset logic silently breaks there.
- News: one UTC CSV serves backtest and live. The MT5 calendar does not work in the Strategy Tester (confirmed through build 6230).
- Statistics: Deflated Sharpe, random-entry benchmarks and bootstrap are native in Python; MT5 needs per-pass exports.
- Contract facts (size, tick, step, fees, funding) are read from one exchange API instead of varying per broker (silver 1,000 vs 5,000 oz, gold 2 vs 3 digits).

WHAT THIS VENUE COSTS (stated plainly)
- Fees dominate: standard 0.05% taker per side, about 10 bps or $3.90 per oz per round trip, versus about $0.19 per oz on a raw-spread CFD account. The account's real rate is unverified and must be read from the API.
- Consequence, own estimate with square-root-of-time scaling from the 2.3% daily ATR: 5m ATR is about 13-14 bps, so the requester's template (stop 1.5 x ATR, target 3 x ATR) pays about half of 1R in fees; break-even win rate rises from 33% to about 50%. Intraday families are not viable here at taker fees.
- History: gold since 2025-12-11 (illiquid first month), silver since 2026-01-07, with two changes to off-hours pricing (2026-05-08, 2026-09-15). Long history must come from a spot proxy and be validated on the 2026 overlap.
- Funding every 4 hours, mostly paid by longs: budget 6-11% a year, single prints up to +0.5% per 4 hours.
- 24/7 trading with weekend volume roughly 6-16% of weekday; silver weekend ranges reached about 5% in January 2026.
- USDT settlement and exchange counterparty risk; jurisdiction-gated; the futures API returned HTTP 451 from a US-located host, so the Railway region matters.

ALTERNATIVES JUDGED
- MetaTrader5 Python package: rejected. Windows-only wheels, no Strategy Tester access, no event callbacks, cannot run on MetaQuotes VPS. It breaks the Linux deployment and still gives no tester.
- MQL5 EA: strongest ready-made tester (real ticks, forward split) and access to regulated CFD brokers. Costs: full rewrite in a second language, a Windows VPS, per-broker symbol quirks, no calendar in the tester, swaps not historical, 0.01-lot granularity. Deferred behind explicit triggers: (a) Phase 0 NO-GO; (b) a regulated account with negative-balance protection or a prop-firm account is required; (c) a deliberate choice of an intraday family that needs about 1 bp costs.
- If a trigger fires, order of preference: OANDA v20 REST (Linux, Python; division availability unverified), then cTrader Open API (Linux, Python SDK), then an MQL5 EA. The first two reuse strategy, risk, journal and research code through the venue adapter. An MQL5 port would be written from this project's own specification, never from Code Base files (unlicensed entries are all rights reserved; no scraping, no Code Base files in the repo).
- CME micro futures via Interactive Brokers: one MGC is about $39,000 notional and the gateway needs a GUI session; not for a PaaS or a small account.
- A general framework (for example NautilusTrader): considered, not adopted for v1. A daily-bar engine with about 10 trades a year per metal is small enough to own outright; revisit if an intraday module is ever added.

WHAT IS KEPT FROM THE EXISTING BOT, AND WHAT IS NOT (verified by reading /home/user/Basel-Almubarak/pro-scalping-bot.zip)
Kept: Python 3.11, ccxt async, Railway worker with env-var config, the EMA/ATR helpers in src/indicators.py.
Not kept, because each is a catalog 'common mistake':
1. src/risk.py lines 61-78: size = free balance x risk_pct x leverage / entry. The stop distance is computed and never used, so '1% risk per trade' is really a fixed 10% notional at leverage 10 whatever the stop ('Lot sizing not tied to the stop', same defect as KA-Gold Bot 48251).
2. src/bot.py lines 163-179: RiskManager.record_trade is never called, so the 5% daily-loss halt and the 3-loss size cut can never trigger.
3. src/broker.py lines 77-84: a failed stop-loss order is only logged; the position stays open with no stop.
4. src/strategy.py line 56: signals read df.iloc[-1], the still-forming candle.
5. src/bot.py line 97: positions live only in an in-memory dict; after a restart (railway.json policy ON_FAILURE) the bot can enter again on a symbol it already holds.
6. No fees in the reward:risk check, no trade journal, no backtest, ccxt unpinned (>=4.4.0).
These affect the crypto bot that is live today and are worth fixing independently of this project.

DEPLOYMENT SHAPE
- Separate Railway service and a separate Binance sub-account with its own trade-only API key, so account-level limits are not mixed with the 30-pair crypto bot.
- One-way position mode, isolated margin, ccxt pinned to an exact version.
- Non-derivable state in SQLite on a Railway volume (Railway Postgres as alternative); everything else rebuilt from the exchange.
- Default run mode MONITOR; live orders require an explicit LIVE_ARMED flag plus the expected account id.

ASSUMPTIONS TO BE RESOLVED IN PHASE 0 (none is relied on before then)
- The account's jurisdiction is eligible and the agreement can be signed for the key or sub-account in use.
- Fee tier is the standard 0.02% / 0.05%; minimum notional is 5 USDT; leverage brackets allow 2-3x isolated.
- The ccxt unified symbols (expected XAU/USDT:USDT and XAG/USDT:USDT) resolve; markets are always resolved by exchange id, never by a hard-coded name.
- How conditional stop orders are created and listed for these symbols on the pinned ccxt version (I recall Binance moving USD-M conditional orders to a separate algo-order endpoint around December 2025; not verified here).
- Whether the futures testnet lists these symbols.
- Capital, tax and legal position of the requester are unknown and not assessed.

modules.module: 1. venue - venue adapter and capability probe
modules.responsibility: The only code that talks to the exchange. Wraps ccxt behind a narrow interface (specs, quotes, bars, positions, orders, income) so strategy, risk and journal code never see venue details and a second adapter (OANDA v20, cTrader) can be added later. Reads every contract fact at start and once per session day; refuses to start on anything unexpected.
features: Broker capability probe at init (filling mode, expiration type, account mode, input validation) - here: load_markets, position mode must be one-way, margin mode isolated and read back, leverage set and read back, multi-asset mode off, agreement status, real maker/taker rate, funding interval, tradingSchedule

Metal symbol profile with suffix-tolerant detection - resolve by exchange market id and base asset XAU/XAG with a manual override; fail init if not found; profile carries only structural differences (risk fraction, leverage, slippage allowance)
Tick-size price rounding and instrument-scaled distance units - all distances in ATR or percent of price, prices rounded to tick with stops rounded away from price
Trade-validator class for broker constraints, with strict retcode handling - min amount, step, min notional, price filters refreshed before each order

Retcode-classified retry and backoff with attempt budgets - ccxt exception classes mapped to transient (timeout, rate limit, network), no-retry (invalid order, insufficient funds) and fatal (auth, permission, HTTP 451/403: halt and alert)
Pre-trade permission and broker-limit gate with distinct reason codes
Signal/execution separation via narrow module interfaces

modules.module: 2. data - bars, indicators and data sanity
modules.responsibility: Builds New-York-close session bars (Mon-Fri; Monday's bar starts Sunday 18:00 New York; weekend prints from Friday 17:00 to Sunday 18:00 excluded from indicators) from 1h or 1m klines, for both the perp and the proxy history, with one builder. Serves closed bars only.
features: Closed-bar-only signal evaluation with new-bar gate - the forming candle returned by fetch_ohlcv is always dropped; bar identity is its open time per symbol and timeframe
Closed-bar gate that re-arms on data failure - the processed-bar latch advances only after all data checks pass
Market/indicator data sanity and history-readiness guards - exact bar counts, finite positive values, ATR below 10% of price, a session with fewer than 12 hourly bars is a no-signal day
Closed-bar data layer: cached indicator handles and per-timeframe new-bar gates
Volatility-unit stop distance (ATR or gap-free mean range) - ATR20 on session bars, so the reopening gap never inflates the unit
Session/opening range builder from M1 bars - built and tested, used only by the research strategy
Empirical execution-cost baseline (spread and slippage recorder) and adaptive cap - recorder only: hourly spread and depth samples in MONITOR mode; no adaptive cap

modules.responsibility: All time logic in one place, defined in America/New_York and UTC with zoneinfo. Answers: which session day is it, is the underlying market open, is a new entry allowed now, is a scheduled US release near.
features: DST-aware session anchoring and rule-based server offset - solved by zoneinfo instead of broker-offset tables; unit-tested on the 2026 US and EU changeover dates

Tradability gate: broker session table, pre-close margin, rollover blackout, stale-quote check - uses the exchange tradingSchedule, quote age under 5 s, no entries from Friday 16:00 to Sunday 19:00 New York

Entry time window with midnight wrap (minute resolution, per weekday) - one fixed execution slot, 20:00-21:00 New York, chosen a priori as the liquid Asian-open hour after the thin 16:00-19:00 stretch

Tester-compatible news source: calendar CSV replay and date blacklist - one hand-checkable UTC CSV (payrolls, CPI, PCE, FOMC) used identically in backtest and live; start-up logs loudly if it is missing or stale

News blackout from the native MT5 economic calendar - replaced by the CSV gate (30 min before and after high-impact USD events, entries only). For the daily engine it rarely binds because execution is at 20:00 New York; it ships because the journal tags and any later intraday module need it

Scheduled flatten and week-edge guards (Friday cutoff, weekly-open wait, daily flat time) - Friday cutoff and weekly-open wait on; daily flatten off for the trend engine as a declared strategy property

Closed-bar volatility shock pause (ATR ratio / bar range versus ATR) - one extreme ceiling only: no new entries for 2 sessions after a session whose true range exceeds 3 x ATR20; switchable for ablation

modules.responsibility: Pure functions from closed bars to an intent: direction, proposed stop, expiry, and a bitmask of every gate result. No order code, no account access. The same class is imported by the backtester and the live loop.
features: Fresh closed-bar trend trigger: N-bar channel breakout or MA cross - channel form with freshness test, as in the quality-5 gold EA 77691 but symmetric long/short
Higher-timeframe trend-side filter on closed bars - close versus EMA200 on session bars, shipped with a switch, default OFF (decided before testing), reported both ways
Setup lifecycle state machine with single-use latches - one intent per symbol per session day, expiry at the end of the execution slot, 'already traded' derived from exchange fills
Single evaluator for live and replay, with a filter-result bitmask as reason code - used for attribution and ablation only, never to pick a best filter subset
Gate pipeline with reason codes, veto logging and per-filter switches
Independent long/short enable switches - operational only, fixed before testing
Closed-bar range breakout with buffer and entry window plus Range-width and compression gate - implemented for the research-only session strategy

modules.responsibility: Turns an intent into a quantity or a logged refusal. Size comes only from the money lost at the stop actually placed; margin and caps may only reduce it.
features: Loss-at-stop sizing via OrderCalcProfit - venue form: qty x contractSize x |entry - stop| plus both-side fees at the account's real rate plus slippage allowance; re-verified after rounding
Never-round-up lot normalisation (skip below minimum) - floor to the amount step; below min amount or min notional is a skip with a reason
Hard ceilings: max lot, max risk money, bounded risk percent - compiled 1.0% ceiling; MAX_RISK_MONEY is a required input with no default
Selectable risk base: fixed money, balance or equity; per-symbol virtual equity - default min(wallet balance, equity); fixed-money mode for comparable backtests; free balance is not offered
Margin affordability pre-check with free-margin buffer - plus an estimated-liquidation-distance check of at least 2x the stop distance
Aggregate exposure caps (total lots, positions, volume limit, pending reserve) - gold and silver in the same direction counted as one exposure
Lot cap from remaining daily loss budget

Pre-trade feasibility and net-RR gate with logged reject reasons and Cost-relative spread gate with hard cap, entry-only - merged into one cost gate: fees plus spread plus slippage as a fraction of the stop distance
Setup-geometry sanity band normalised by ATR and Broker stops-level and freeze-level floor applied before sizing - stop distance bounds checked before the quantity is computed
Init-time validation of the sizing configuration

modules.responsibility: Account-level limits that sit above both symbols, evaluated on a timer whatever the market is doing, persisted so a restart cannot grant a fresh budget.
features: Daily loss limit on equity (closed + floating) with configurable day boundary - boundary 17:00 New York
Day reference rebuilt from deal history (deposit-aware, scoped) - from the exchange income history: realised PnL, commission and funding count, transfers do not
Total drawdown limit: static floor or trailing equity high-water mark - trailing, persisted, permanent lock, manual reset only
Act-before-limit buffer on credit-free equity - entries blocked at 80% of each limit
Crash-proof persisted lock state machine - lock level, reason, until-timestamp, day base and equity peak in the durable store, escalate-only
Latched flatten with enforcement until flat
Trade-frequency caps: daily/session quota, entry cooldown, one-setup-per-day key - counted from confirmed fills, rebuilt from history
Exposure caps: positions, per-direction levels, single direction, entry spacing
Account precondition gates: live-arming guard, minimum capital, margin level - LIVE_ARMED plus expected account id; computed minimum viable equity printed at start
Early-warning alerts and visible block reasons

modules.responsibility: Single choke point for every order. Guarantees the invariant: no position older than 10 seconds without a confirmed exchange-side stop, otherwise it is closed.
features: Protected entry: stops anchored to the real fill, fail-safe close, slippage tolerance - market entry, stop computed from the actual fill, placed reduce-only on the exchange, read back; bounded retries then immediate close
Transaction-confirmed order state machine (in-flight guard + deferred deal queue) - websocket or polling as a hint, reconciliation by query as the truth, timeouts on every wait
Read-back confirmation of fills, modifies and closes - risk bookkeeping uses filled quantity
Duplicate-entry prevention and restart-safe ownership - deterministic clientOrderId from strategy, symbol, decision bar and side; order and fills queried before any resend
Decide once, deliver with a bounded retry window and failure circuit breaker - at most 2 attempts inside the 20:00-21:00 slot, drift guard re-checked, 5 consecutive failures pause entries

Single SL modification gateway: tighten-only, broker-valid, step-gated, throttled and Safe modify/close wrapper: freeze-level guard, no-change skip, minimum step, throttle - replace means place new, confirm, then cancel old, so cover never lapses

Composite minimum stop-distance engine (stops level, freeze level, spread fallback, correct quote side) - venue form: price filters and would-trigger-immediately rejections; a stop already through the market means close now
Emergency flatten routine (snapshot, pendings first, retry until flat)
OrderCheck preflight inside the send path - venue form: local validation of the full request against cached filters; never applied to reducing orders

modules.responsibility: Runs every cycle in a fixed order for each owned position: ensure a stop exists, apply forced exits, then compute the one tighten-only stop candidate.
features: Initial protective stop from structure or ATR, clamped and broker-valid - 3 x ATR20 from the fill
Staged exit pipeline with fixed precedence and profit-only trail activation - newSL = max(currentSL, candidate) for longs, mirrored for shorts; candidate ignored until it is at or beyond entry
Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop - recomputed once per closed session bar, best price since entry recomputed from bars so no extra state
Stop-loss watchdog for naked positions and Auto-attach missing protective stop (naked-position safety net) - attaches the stored intended stop, not a recomputed one; escalates to close
Idempotent SL/TP reconciliation and missing-stop repair
Signal-driven exits and verified close-then-reverse - only the verified close-then-open part: an opposite breakout closes first, a new entry needs confirmed flat

Time stop in traded bars, optionally conditional on progress - implemented and tested, default OFF for the trend engine (the trail is the exit; a bar-count stop would cut the few long winners); ON for the research session strategy
Restart-safe per-position exit state and strict ownership

modules.module: 9. state - persistence, ownership and the run cycle
modules.responsibility: Treats the exchange as the database and stores only what it cannot tell us. Owns the main loop.
features: Stateless restart recovery from broker state - positions, open orders and fills re-read at start and every cycle

Minimal durable store for non-derivable state - per-position initial stop and initial risk, day baseline, equity peak, locks, flatten latch, run mode; SQLite on a Railway volume, written on change in a transaction

Ownership by symbol + magic + position identifier - venue form: dedicated sub-account plus clientOrderId prefix; in one-way mode the bot must own the symbol, so a position it has no record of is never adopted or closed: entries are blocked with reason FOREIGN_POSITION and an alert is sent
Startup preflight: connection, permissions and account identity
Trading-day rollover: baseline rebuild and daily state reset
Unified tick-plus-timer cycle: re-entrancy guard, throttle, snapshot, idempotent actions - one position snapshot per cycle; abort all actions if it fails
Ordered pipeline: exits before entries, one entry gate that never blocks management
Single-instance lock with heartbeat - a second Railway replica refuses to trade
Persist operator control state across restarts

modules.module: 10. journal - decision log, trade log, cost telemetry
modules.responsibility: Makes every action and every non-action explainable and makes backtest and live comparable line by line. Same writer in both.
features: Decision journal with reason codes and a single order-send choke point - one line per evaluated bar per symbol: ENTER or SKIP with the measured value and its threshold; cannot be disabled
Position-level trade journal rebuilt from deals (net of all costs) - fees and every funding payment attributed to the position from the income history
R-multiple against the initial stop, plus MFE/MAE per trade - also PnL in basis points of price
Execution-cost telemetry: signed slippage, fill latency and spread and Execution-cost telemetry: stop slippage, fill slippage, real commission and swap - plus funding paid or received per position
Risk audit: sizing line, planned-versus-realised loss, never-widen-stop check - a widened stop counts as a test failure
Session, weekday, hour and exit-reason tags with bucket tables - tags only; no filter may be derived from them in-sample
Logging plumbing: levels, change-based throttling, durable append-only CSV - JSON lines to stdout for Railway logs plus journal tables in the store
Embedded trade-journal export at end of test and session

modules.responsibility: Event-driven replay that imports the live evaluator, sizer and exit pipeline unchanged; adds a cost model (fees, slippage, funding), benchmarks, a trial registry and the gate report.
features: Single evaluator for live and replay, with a filter-result bitmask as reason code
Cost-aware expectancy checks: breakeven win rate and pessimistic bar resolution - a bar containing both stop and target counts as a stop; costs charged both ways
Random-entry benchmark mode (null hypothesis) - seeded, same exits and costs, same entry frequency and long/short mix; refuses to run when LIVE_ARMED is set
OnTester criterion with hard gates and early/late consistency - Python form: the gate report with fixed windows and minimum trade counts
Built-in self-tests: known-answer checks and state round trip - pytest suite; any failure blocks deployment
Tester and optimiser hygiene: strict input validation, no UI in tester - invalid configurations fail at start; an append-only registry counts every run
Trade-list robustness analytics: bootstrap Monte Carlo, distribution metrics, per-pass frames - offline only, in R units, read as an optimistic lower bound and used to size risk, never to prove edge

modules.module: 12. ops - control, alerts and safety drills
modules.responsibility: Operator controls and supervision for a headless worker. Nothing here can widen risk.
features: Operating-mode switch (Normal / Monitor-only / Exit-only / Flatten-and-idle) - env var or small CLI; change is logged and persisted

Panic flatten button with retry-until-flat and result report and Two-step confirmation for destructive buttons - CLI command with a confirm token; latch persists across restarts and reports closed versus failed
Status dashboard with block reason and limit usage - headless form: one status line per minute (mode, block reason, limit usage, next boundary, funding accrued)
Once-per-event alerts and push notifications and Edge-triggered health monitoring, heartbeat and self-audit - one-way messages on state changes only; highest priority is 'position without stop'
Input validation and fail-fast init with a hard risk cap and Fail-fast input validation in OnInit
Demo acceptance harness: restart-survival test and demo-only build - scripted kill-and-restart drills; builds without LIVE_ARMED cannot send orders

strategies.name: TREND-D1: closed-session channel breakout with ATR chandelier exit (the only live candidate in v1)
strategies.logic:
Bars: session-day bars closing 17:00 America/New_York, Mon-Fri, built from 1h klines; Monday's bar starts Sunday 18:00; weekend prints excluded from indicators. All reads from closed bars. Let t be the bar that just closed.
Indicators: HH_N[t] = highest high of bars t-N..t-1; LL_N[t] = lowest low of the same bars; ATR20[t] = mean true range of the last 20 closed session bars.
Long signal: close[t] > HH_N[t] AND close[t-1] <= HH_N[t-1] (fresh break) AND no own position in the symbol. Short signal is the mirror with LL_N. Primary pre-registered parameters: N = 55, k = 3.0.
Gates (each a boolean with a logged reason, each switchable for ablation): data sanity; run mode and locks; week-edge guard; news CSV window; volatility shock (previous session true range > 3 x ATR20 blocks entries for 2 sessions); premium sanity (|mark - index| / index <= 0.5% gold, 1.0% silver); stop-distance band (k x ATR20 between 2% and 12% of price for gold, 4% and 25% for silver); cost gate (round-trip fees + spread + slippage allowance <= 5% of stop distance); exposure and daily-budget caps. Optional EMA200 side filter exists with default OFF.
Execution: the intent is stored at 17:00 New York and delivered once in the 20:00-21:00 New York slot of the same evening (a Friday signal executes Sunday 20:00). Drift guard: skip if |price - close[t]| > 1.0 x ATR20. Market order, quantity from loss-at-stop sizing. At most 2 send attempts; the intent expires at 21:00.
Initial stop: fill price -/+ k x ATR20, rounded away from price, placed immediately as a reduce-only exchange stop triggered on mark price, read back; if it cannot be confirmed within the retry budget the position is closed.
Trail: after each closed session bar, candidate = highest high since entry - k x ATR20 (shorts: lowest low + k x ATR20). The candidate is ignored until it is at or beyond the entry price; then newSL = max(currentSL, candidate) (min for shorts) through the tighten-only gateway.
Other exits: an opposite fresh breakout closes the position at the next execution slot (close verified before any new entry); daily-loss or drawdown lock flattens. No fixed take-profit and no time stop by default.
Pre-declared grid, same values for both metals: N in {20, 55, 120} x k in {2, 3, 4} = 9 cells. Pre-declared one-at-a-time ablations on the primary cell: EMA200 filter on; profit-only trail off; exit by fixed 2R target instead of trail; volatility-shock gate off; news gate off; next-session-open execution instead of the 20:00 slot.
strategies.timeframe: Signal on New-York-close daily session bars (Mon-Fri). Execution and stop resolution on 1h bars in research and live quotes in production. Expected holding period weeks to months; trade count to be measured (order of several per metal per year).
strategies.symbols: Binance USD-M XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT perpetuals, resolved by exchange id. One position per symbol. Identical parameters; silver at half the gold risk; same-direction gold plus silver treated as one exposure.
strategies.rationale:
Evidence: slow trend following is the only family in the research with long, multi-source evidence (confirmed), but on a single instrument it is not statistically established (very likely) and static rules were near zero in 2009-2022 in diversified portfolios. It is chosen because it is the least-bad evidence, not because it is proven.
Venue fit: with a stop of about 6.9% (gold) and 13.2% (silver) of price, the 10 bps taker round trip is about 1-2% of 1R, so the venue's main weakness is neutralised. The real drag is funding: a two-month long at 7-11% a year costs roughly 0.15-0.25R on gold (own arithmetic), which the cost model charges.
Catalog fit: 'Fresh closed-bar trend trigger: N-bar channel breakout or MA cross' in the form of quality-5 EA 77691, made symmetric because that EA's own header admits its long-only default was chosen after shorts lost in 2020-2026. 'Closed-bar ATR (chandelier) trailing stop' is the best-supported trail. Daily bars make results insensitive to tick modelling and let about 20 years of proxy history, including the 2011-2015 gold bear market, stand in for the 11-month perp history.
Discipline: 9 cells plus 6 ablations per run set keeps the trial count far below the 45-trial bound; no signal input is used that does not exist in the proxy history (perp volume, funding, premium and order book are safety vetoes and telemetry only).
Deviation from the requester's template, stated openly: no fixed 3 x ATR target (a fixed target cuts the right tail a trend system depends on; the 2R variant is tested as an ablation), risk 0.5% instead of 1%, and no EMA/RSI/MACD/volume stack (classic technical rules mostly fail once data snooping is controlled, silver worse than gold: confirmed).

strategies.name: SESSION-RB: pre-New-York range breakout on closed 15m bars (research harness only; not deployed in v1)
strategies.logic:
Range: high and low of 1m bars between 03:00 and 08:00 America/New_York, frozen at 08:00, rebuilt from history after a restart. Day is skipped if the range width is outside 0.15-0.70 of the daily ATR20, if the range has missing bars, or if a high-impact USD release falls between 08:00 and 11:00 (CSV).
Entry: first closed 15m bar between 08:00 and 11:00 New York that closes beyond the range by a buffer of 0.05 x daily ATR20; market order at the next bar open; one attempt per side per day, one position at a time.
Stop: opposite range edge plus the same buffer; skip if the stop distance exceeds 1.0 x daily ATR20. Target: 2R. Time exit: flat at 15:55 New York. Cost gate: round-trip fees + spread + slippage <= 10% of the stop distance.
No parameter search: these values are fixed a priori from the catalog sources (75586, 17465) and tested once, against the random-entry benchmark with the same exits.
strategies.timeframe: Range from 1m bars, trigger on closed 15m bars, intraday only, flat before 16:00 New York.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT first; XAGUSDT only as a robustness check with identical inputs.
strategies.rationale:
It is the family the better gold EAs actually implement (75586, 76153, 78688, 78259), so the requester will ask about it. It is in the harness to answer that question with numbers, not to be traded.
Pre-registered expectation: fail. A range of 0.15-0.70 x a 2.3% daily ATR gives stops of about 35-160 bps; at about 12 bps all-in cost the 10% cost gate needs a stop of at least 120 bps, so most days are infeasible before any signal is judged, and on the rest cost is 8-15% of 1R. The closest independent replication of an opening-range rule found a gross edge of about +0.13R that vanished net of costs (indices, not gold; partially supported). No peer-reviewed, cost-inclusive gold ORB test was found.
Platform consequence: if the requester still wants this family, that is trigger (c) for a raw-spread CFD venue, where the same trade costs about 1% of 1R. The module would move unchanged behind a broker adapter; the evidence problem would remain.

strategies.name: NULL: random-entry, buy-and-hold and always-in 12-month-sign benchmarks (not trading strategies)
strategies.logic: Random entry: at each decision bar where the real strategy is flat, enter with a probability that matches the real strategy's entry frequency; direction by seeded coin flip weighted to the real long/short mix; identical stop, trail, sizing, costs and funding; 1,000 seeds. Buy-and-hold: constant long, volatility-matched to the strategy, with funding charged. Always-in sign: long if the 252-session return is positive, short otherwise, same sizing unit. All three run in research only; the random mode refuses to start when LIVE_ARMED is set.
strategies.timeframe: Same bars and execution slot as TREND-D1.
strategies.symbols: XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT proxies and perps, same as the strategy under test.
strategies.rationale: Catalog core feature 'Random-entry benchmark mode (null hypothesis)'. Gold's long upward drift makes almost any long-biased rule with a trailing stop look profitable in 2015-2026 backtests (research: likely). The benchmarks separate signal from exit geometry and drift; without them a positive backtest is not evidence.

designs.risk_model:
UNIT. 1R = money lost if the initial stop is hit = quantity x contractSize x |fill - stop| + taker fees on entry and exit at the account's real rate + slippage allowance (2 bps of notional per side for gold, 5 bps for silver). Everything below is a default; all are inputs validated at start, none is optimised.

PER TRADE
- Gold 0.50% of min(wallet balance, equity); silver 0.25%. Compiled ceiling 1.00%. MAX_RISK_MONEY per trade is a required input with no default (start fails without it).
- Lower than the requester's 1% for three reasons: gold and silver are one correlated bet (0.83-0.88); stops do not bound loss in a gap (2026 worst single-day ranges 14% gold, 39% silver); the expected edge is small, so survival dominates.
- Quantity floored to the exchange step; below minimum amount or minimum notional the trade is skipped with a reason, never rounded up; loss re-verified after rounding.
- Stop distance 3.0 x ATR20 of session bars, measured from the real fill. Valid only between 2% and 12% of price (gold) or 4% and 25% (silver); outside, skip. At today's volatility that is about 6.9% for gold and 13.2% for silver.
- Cost gate: fees + spread + slippage allowance must be at most 5% of the stop distance (the trend engine sits near 1-2%).
- Resulting size, for orientation: gold notional about 7% of equity per position, silver about 2%. The bot prints the minimum viable equity at start (about $70 for gold and $265 for silver at default risk if the 5 USDT minimum notional is confirmed; about $350 and $1,320 at stage-1 risk).

EXPOSURE AND MARGIN
- One position per symbol, two in total. Same-direction gold + silver open risk capped at 0.75% of equity. Total notional capped at 0.5x equity.
- Isolated margin, exchange leverage 3x for gold and 2x for silver. Before each order: estimated liquidation distance at least 2x the stop distance, and free margin after the order at least 50% of equity. A change in leverage brackets or margin rate versus the previous day raises an alert.
- Dedicated sub-account, so these limits are not mixed with the crypto bot.

ACCOUNT LIMITS
- Daily loss: day boundary 17:00 New York; reference equity rebuilt from exchange income history (transfers excluded). At -1.6% new entries are blocked; at -2.0% own positions are flattened and entries locked until the next boundary. The next trade's size is also capped to 80% of the remaining daily budget, so one trade cannot breach the limit by itself. (The requester's 5% is cut to 2% to stay proportionate to 0.5% risk and two positions.)
- Total drawdown: -10% from the persisted equity high-water mark flattens and locks permanently; only an explicit operator reset with a new baseline clears it. Warning at -8%.
- Frequency: at most 1 entry per symbol per session day; at most 2 send attempts per decision; 5 consecutive order failures pause entries and alert.

TIME AND MARKET-STATE RULES
- No new entries from Friday 16:00 to Sunday 19:00 New York, or within 30 minutes of a high-impact USD release in the CSV.
- Open positions are held over weekends with the exchange stop live (trigger on mark price). The stop distance is far wider than the measured 2026 weekend gaps (gold 90th percentile 1.2%, silver 2.1%, worst about 2% and 4-5%), but a weekend stop can still fill badly on thin liquidity.
- Volatility shock: no new entries for 2 sessions after a session whose true range exceeds 3 x ATR20.
- Premium sanity: skip if |mark - index| / index exceeds 0.5% (gold) or 1.0% (silver). Quote older than 5 s: skip.
- Drift guard: skip if price has moved more than 1.0 x ATR20 from the signal close by execution time.

FUNDING
- Charged in every backtest and attributed per position live. Alert when the trailing 7-day funding against the position annualises above 25%. No automatic exit in v1.

HARD INVARIANTS (tested, not configurable)
- No position older than 10 seconds without a confirmed exchange-side stop; otherwise it is closed.
- A stop is never loosened.
- Margin and caps may only reduce a risk-sized quantity.
- Risk-reducing actions are never blocked by any gate, lock or limit.
- A position the bot has no record of is never adopted or closed; entries are blocked and the operator is alerted.

STAGING
- Stage 1: 0.10% gold / 0.05% silver. Stage 2: 0.25% / 0.125%. Stage 3: the defaults above. Stage rules are in the validation plan.
designs.validation_plan:
PRINCIPLES
- Thresholds are fixed here, before any result is seen, and are not relaxed afterwards. A new hypothesis is a new pre-registration.
- Every run is written to an append-only trial registry. Hard budget: 45 trials for the whole project (the published bound for a zero-skill in-sample Sharpe of 1 with 5 years of data; conservative here because the proxy sample is about 20 years).
- Parameters are identical for gold and silver. The verdict is read on the pre-registered primary cell (N=55, k=3) and on the median of the 9-cell grid, never on the best cell.
- [P] marks a threshold that traces to a primary source; [C] marks a convention.

G0 VENUE (Phase 0). PASS if all hold:
- Both markets resolve by exchange id; the account is eligible and the TradFi-Perps agreement is signed for the key in use; no HTTP 451/403 from the deployed region.
- Contract size, tick, step, minimum notional, leverage brackets, funding interval and the account's real maker/taker rates are read from the API and stored.
- One-way mode and isolated margin can be set and read back; creation and listing of a conditional stop order on the pinned ccxt version is demonstrated once (testnet if available, else one minimum-size order with the requester's consent).
FAIL: go to the fallback-venue phase; nothing else is built on Binance.

G1 DATA. PASS if all hold:
- Hourly spot proxy for both metals covers 2006-2026 with recorded provenance and checksums. If hourly depth is shorter, daily proxy bars with next-session-open execution are used and the downgrade is stated in the report.
- Session bars built from 1m and from 1h are identical; time-zone tests pass on the 2026 US and EU changeover dates.
- On the Jan-Nov 2026 overlap (December 2025 excluded as illiquid): at least 95% of session closes differ by no more than 0.30% (gold) and 0.80% (silver) between perp and proxy, and daily-return correlation is at least 0.98 [C].
- A second proxy feed gives the same sign of net expectancy and total R within 20% [C].

G2 HARNESS CORRECTNESS. PASS if: known-answer tests are green (sizing with step rounding, stop-first bar resolution, funding accrual, R-multiple, daily-baseline rebuild); a hand-computed 10-trade fixture is reproduced to the cent; two runs give an identical journal hash; the never-widen-stop audit finds zero violations.

G3 STRATEGY EVIDENCE. Proxy 2006-2026 with the perp cost overlay: taker fees both sides at the account's rate, slippage 2 bps gold / 5 bps silver per side, funding 7% a year charged to longs, nothing credited to shorts.
a) Primary cell and grid median: net expectancy above 0 R; at least 6 of 9 cells net positive [C].
b) Stress costs (fees x1.5, slippage x2, funding 11% a year): primary net expectancy at least 0.
c) Random-entry benchmark, 1,000 seeds: real pooled total R above the 95th percentile; each side (long, short) at or above the median of its own-side random distribution.
d) Four fixed windows (2006-10, 2011-15, 2016-20, 2021-26): net non-negative in at least 3.
e) Sample: at least 150 closed trades pooled across both metals [C]; fewer caps the verdict at tier B.
f) Statistics reported: t = annualised Sharpe x square root of years, and the Deflated Sharpe Ratio with the full trial count. PBO is not computed: its method needs many more than 10 trials and the grid is deliberately smaller.
Verdict:
- TIER A: a-e pass, t at least 3 and DSR at least 0.95 [P].
- TIER B: a-e pass, but t below 3 or DSR below 0.95. Weak evidence, not refuted.
- TIER C: any of a-d fails. This strategy is not traded live.

G4 RISK FROM RESAMPLING. Bootstrap of trade results in R (1,000 resamples; read as an optimistic lower bound because loss clustering is destroyed). The 95th-percentile maximum drawdown at the chosen risk per trade must be at most 8% of equity. If not, risk per trade is cut; the 10% kill level is not moved.

G5 STRESS REPLAY. Replay 30 January 2026 (silver about -26% to -31% close to close and 35-39% intraday; gold about -9% to -12%) and the worst 2026 weekend on Binance 1m bars, both metals long at default risk, stop fills taken at the worst price of the minute after trigger. PASS if account loss is at most 3x planned open risk, there is no liquidation at the configured leverage, and the daily-loss lock fires and survives a restart.

G6 EXECUTION PARITY (Phases 4-5). PASS if all hold:
- Fault-injection suite green: stop placement failing 3 times closes the position; a kill between fill and stop is repaired by the watchdog on restart; a replayed decision produces exactly one order; locks persist across restart; the flatten latch retries to flat; an auth or 451 error halts without a retry storm; a second instance refuses to trade.
- At least 30 calendar days in MONITOR mode with 100% agreement between live decisions and a replay over the archived bars.
- At least 20 scripted lifecycle drills at minimum notional, including at least 3 on a weekend, 3 across a funding timestamp and 10 forced restarts: zero duplicate orders, zero positions beyond 10 s without a confirmed stop, empty state diff after every restart.
- Journal fees and funding reconcile with exchange income history within 0.5% per day; median fill slippage is at or below the modelled value (if not, re-cost and re-run G3b).

G7 STAGED LIVE.
- Stage 1 (0.10% gold / 0.05% silver) for the longer of 10 closed trades or 3 months. Tier B never leaves stage 1. Tier A may move to stage 2 and then stage 3 after the same period at each.
- Halt-and-review rules, written now: drawdown beyond the bootstrap 95th percentile for the stage; any position without a stop for more than 60 s; median stop slippage above 2x the model; any decision mismatch against replay; 90-day funding drag above the stress assumption.
- A monthly report reconciles live trades against a replay of the same period trade by trade.

WHAT THE GATES CANNOT SHOW
- Passing lowers the chance of a false positive; it does not show profitability. In one large cohort, backtest Sharpe had almost no power to predict live results (R-squared below 0.025).
- Live trading at small size tests the implementation, not the edge: confirming even a Sharpe of 1.0 on daily returns needs about 2.7 years.
- The proxy is a different instrument from the perp; G1 bounds the difference for 2026 only.
- The session-breakout research strategy gets one run against the random-entry benchmark and the cost gate. It is reported, counted as a trial, and not promoted in v1 whatever the result.

build_phases.acceptance: The remaining G6 thresholds: 100% decision match on replay, zero duplicate orders, zero unprotected positions beyond 10 s, empty state diff after each of at least 10 forced restarts, fee and funding reconciliation within 0.5% per day.

build_phases.phase: Phase 6 - Staged live trading (tier A or B only; open-ended)
build_phases.deliverable: LIVE_ARMED set at stage-1 risk; monthly reconciliation report (live versus replay, planned versus realised loss, slippage and funding distributions); stage changes recorded with the evidence that justified them.
build_phases.acceptance: G7 rules applied as written. Any halt-and-review trigger stops new entries until a written review is done. Tier B never exceeds stage 1.

build_phases.phase: Phase 7 - Conditional second venue (only if a platform trigger fires: Phase 0 NO-GO, a regulated or prop account is required, or a deliberate move to an intraday family)
build_phases.deliverable: A second venue adapter, in order of preference OANDA v20, cTrader Open API, then an MQL5 EA written from this project's specification on a Windows VPS. Broker-specific symbol profile loader (contract size, digits, swap, sessions read live), spread recorder on the target account, and for MT5 a calendar CSV and explicit server-offset table for the tester.
build_phases.acceptance: G0 and G1 re-run for the new venue with its own cost model (spread, commission, swap including the triple-swap day). Minimum-lot feasibility shown for the requester's actual capital (a 3 x ATR daily stop needs about $54,000 at 0.5% risk on a 100-oz contract). G3b and G6 re-run before any live order.

main_risks: No edge. Single-instrument trend following is not statistically established, static trend rules were near zero in 2009-2022, and 74-89% of retail leveraged accounts lose. The most likely validation verdict is tier B or C.

Eligibility. Binance metals perps are jurisdiction-gated and need a signed agreement; the country list was not found. A NO-GO in Phase 0 forces the slower broker or MQL5 path and brings back the minimum-lot problem for small accounts.

Proxy mismatch. About 20 years of evidence would come from spot gold and silver, a different instrument from a USDT-settled perp with funding and weekend trading. Gate G1 bounds the difference only for 2026.

Short and shifting venue history. About 11 months of data, an illiquid first month, and two changes to off-hours index and mark mechanics in 2026; a third change could alter stop behaviour without notice.

Funding drag and spikes. Longs have paid roughly 6-11% a year recently, far more in early 2026, with prints up to +0.5% per 4 hours; on a multi-week long this is 10x the fee cost and can consume a small edge.

Gap and tail risk beyond the stop. On 30 January 2026 silver fell about 26-31% in a session and gold about 9-12%; weekend liquidity is 6-16% of weekday. A stop-market order fills at the next available price, so realised loss can be a multiple of planned risk.

Correlated book. Gold and silver correlate at 0.83-0.88 and silver behaves like roughly 2x gold; two positions are close to one larger bet, with almost none of the diversification that produces most published trend returns.

Counterparty and settlement. Profit and loss are in USDT on a crypto exchange; exchange failure, withdrawal limits, stablecoin de-peg or forced deleveraging are outside the bot's control and outside regulated retail CFD protections.

Operational platform risk. Railway restarts, an ephemeral filesystem if the volume is misconfigured, a region change that triggers HTTP 451, or an exchange API change (for example how conditional orders are created) can leave stops unmanaged; the exchange-side stop and the watchdog reduce but do not remove this.

Research overfitting by iteration. The temptation after a tier C verdict is to keep trying variants; each one spends trial budget and inflates the best result. The registry and the 45-trial cap are the only defence and depend on discipline.

Regime dependence. Gold is about 31% below its January 2026 record with daily ranges about twice 2024 levels and Fed-hike pricing; 2015-2026 backtests are dominated by one bull market, and parameters in ATR units still assume volatility estimates stay meaningful.

Carried-over assumptions about the current bot. Its '1% risk' and '5% daily stop' do not work as described; anyone comparing the new bot's results or sizing to the old one's should not treat the old figures as a baseline.

Scope not covered. Tax, legal eligibility for leveraged metals in the requester's country, and code-licence questions beyond 're-implement from a written specification' were not assessed and need the requester's own check.
designs.honest_expectation:
What can be promised is behaviour, not profit: every position carries an exchange-side stop; the loss at that stop is what the journal said before the order; a restart never duplicates or forgets a trade; every non-trade has a logged reason; live decisions replay exactly in the backtester; account limits fire and stay fired. Those properties are testable and the plan tests them.

What cannot be promised is an edge. The realistic picture, from the research:
- Published slow-trend results average a gross Sharpe near 0.4 per market over 136 years across 67 markets, and static trend rules earned close to nothing in 2009-2022 in diversified portfolios. Asset-by-asset tests find little statistically reliable momentum. A two-metal book has almost no diversification.
- With about 20 years of proxy data, t of 2 needs a net Sharpe of about 0.45 and t of 3 about 0.67. Clearing tier A is unlikely; tier B (weak evidence, not refuted) or tier C (fail) is the expected verdict. That is my judgement from the cited figures, not a measured probability.
- Costs on this venue: fees are about 1-2% of 1R per trade, but funding on a two-month gold long is roughly 0.15-0.25R. A small gross edge on the long side can be mostly eaten by funding.
- If the engine does trade: few trades (order of several per metal per year, to be measured), a win rate well under 50% as is normal for trend following (a general property of the family, to be measured in G3, not a sourced figure), flat or losing stretches of a year or more, and most of any gain from a handful of trades.
- The current regime is a high-volatility drawdown after a record run, and backtests covering 2015-2026 flatter anything long-biased. Results must beat random entries with the same exits and hold on the short side before they count.
- Running live at small size will not confirm an edge in any practical time; confirming even a Sharpe of 1.0 takes about 2.7 years of daily returns. Stage 1 is tuition for verifying execution, and a tier B strategy stays there.

The platform choice does not change these odds. It changes how quickly and cheaply they are found out: a go/no-go on the venue in a day or two, a full pre-registered test report in roughly two to three weeks of part-time work (rough estimate), in the language and on the deployment the requester already runs. If the verdict is tier C, the honest outcome is a tested execution and risk engine, a written reason not to trade this strategy, and repairs worth applying to the crypto bot that is live today.

The proxy is 'spot XAU and XAG daily histories', so the 20:00-22:00 delivery slot cannot be simulated in the 2010-2026 test. The test will fill at a daily open and call the difference 5 bps, when the 18:00-20:00 New York hourly range alone is roughly 23-33 bps.

'new stop confirmed before the old one is cancelled' assumes Binance accepts two reduce-only stops against one position on the conditional-order route. That check ('Conditional-order routing is verified with the pinned ccxt version') is in Phase 3, after the evidence run and verdict.

The 5-second invariant only binds while the process is alive. Fault injection 1 measures 'on restart the stop is attached within 5 s', so the naked time is the PaaS restart time, and the existing railway.json caps restarts at 10 retries, after which nothing runs.
V4 runs 'on testnet if the symbols exist there, otherwise at minimum order size' and requires no weekend or funding-timestamp drills. A testnet matching engine is not the production book.
Cross margin at 2x with no liquidation-distance check and no detection of leverage-bracket or margin changes; 'Liquidation is not a practical risk' is asserted, not monitored.
The funding gate 'limits new entries only'. A long already held through a January-2026-type funding month (4.35% of notional, about 0.6R on a 7% stop) has no rule.
No handling of US holiday sessions (Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year early closes) for the 'NY-day bars'; the 'complete count' check would retry or skip with undefined effect on signals.

strengths: Best spread-gate design of the four, matching what the market research asked for: 'skip when all-in round-trip cost exceeds 10% of the stop distance, or when spread exceeds 3 x its recorded same-hour median'.

Notional caps are derived from total stop failure, not from assumed stop fills: 'with every stop failing in a repeat of 30 Jan 2026 (gold -12%, silver -31%), loss = 2.4% + 2.5% = 4.9%', and carried notional is capped separately from intraday notional.
Shadow sleeves are scored under two cost models so the fee-versus-spread question is answered by data, and it says in advance that on Binance 'most setups will fail the 10% cost gate'.

Calendar hygiene is concrete: 'missing or expired file blocks intraday sleeves', 9-10 December 2026 flagged, OFF_HOURS gate 16:00-19:00 and Friday 16:00 to Sunday 19:00, and trend orders go out at 11:00 New York in the deepest hour.

Execution acceptance is numeric: 'fees and funding within 2% of the model, median entry slippage at or below the assumption', and a sleeve is suspended 'if realised costs exceed 1.5x the model over 20 trades'.
The CFD adapter is gated on measured broker reality: '8 weeks of recorded spreads on the actual account' and run-time checks '(silver 1,000 vs 5,000 oz, digits, stops level, swap, sessions)'.
Pre-2026 carry is modelled with rates ('longs pay T-bill + 3%') and every backtest is 're-run with costs doubled'.
flaws: Several sleeves share one exchange position: 'one-way (netting) mode' with 'clientOrderId prefixes as the ownership key'. The exchange holds one net XAUUSDT position, so per-sleeve reduce-only stops and 'limit take-profits' are bookkeeping that the venue does not enforce, and 'The venue is the database' is false for sleeve attribution. The design concedes 'Several sleeves on a netting account with per-sleeve stops, resizes and locks is far more code' and gives no mechanism.

The |S| resize ('1 -> 1/3 closes two thirds; 1/3 -> 1 adds back') needs a cancel-and-replace of the protective stop quantity at every step, multiplying unprotected windows. Adding back while price is below entry is adding to a loser, which contradicts 'The allocator forbids adding to a losing position in code'.

The trend sleeve has no drift or gap guard. The decision is at 17:00 and the order goes 'at the first H1 open at or after 11:00 New York on the next trading day', which is 18 hours later, or about 66 hours across a weekend. The other two Python designs skip beyond 1 ATR; this one enters regardless.
Stop trigger type unspecified; cross margin, 'exchange leverage 3x or lower', and carried notional up to 20% (gold) and 8% (silver) on a venue whose silver weekend range reached about 5%.

The CFD shadow cost model is the published floor: 'raw-spread CFD cost model (about 0.5-1.5 bps round trip)' applied to entries in 08:00-11:00 New York, the release hours. The research says those figures are minimums, raw accounts add commission, and no hour-by-hour table exists. A shadow 'pass under CFD costs' would be on perp or spot prices, not the broker's feed.
Resting 'reduce-only limit' targets imply a touch-fill assumption in M1/M15 replay; trade-through and the maker/taker fee mix are not addressed.
Data assumptions are unaudited: 'M1 bid/ask ... Assumed available from about 2016'.
Live differs from tested at small size by its own admission: 'Below roughly $2,000 the smaller silver positions are skipped, so the live portfolio differs from the tested one.'
It did not read the requester's existing execution code, so it misses that the current bot already uses the same ccxt conditional-order path it plans to depend on.

strengths: Only design that names the stop trigger and the venue's real rejection modes: 'reduce-only exchange stop triggered on mark price, read back', 'would-trigger-immediately rejections; a stop already through the market means close now', and it flags the conditional-order change itself: 'I recall Binance moving USD-M conditional orders to a separate algo-order endpoint around December 2025; not verified here'. Gate G0 demands 'creation and listing of a conditional stop order on the pinned ccxt version is demonstrated once' before anything else is built.

Venue-specific market-state checks no other design has: 'Premium sanity (|mark - index| / index <= 0.5% gold, 1.0% silver)', 'estimated-liquidation-distance check of at least 2x the stop distance', 'A change in leverage brackets or margin rate versus the previous day raises an alert', and isolated margin, which gives an exchange-enforced loss bound per position that does not depend on a stop fill.

Cost arithmetic is done per venue rather than asserted: 'about 10 bps or $3.90 per oz per round trip, versus about $0.19 per oz on a raw-spread CFD account', the 5m template 'pays about half of 1R in fees', and minimum-lot feasibility ($54,000 gold, $130,000 silver on CFD) against 0.001 oz steps.

The fallback venue phase lists real broker requirements: 'Broker-specific symbol profile loader (contract size, digits, swap, sessions read live), spread recorder on the target account, and for MT5 a calendar CSV and explicit server-offset table for the tester', and a cost model with 'swap including the triple-swap day'.

One-way-mode ownership is handled safely: a position the bot has no record of 'is never adopted or closed: entries are blocked with reason FOREIGN_POSITION'. Its six code-reading claims about the existing bot check out against the files in /home/user/Basel-Almubarak/pro-scalping-bot.zip.
flaws: Slippage model is thin: 'slippage 2 bps gold / 5 bps silver per side' is applied to stop exits too, the stress is only 'slippage x2', and G3 has no rule that a stop gapped through fills at the bar open (only 'a bar containing both stop and target counts as a stop').

January 2026 funding (+4.35% of notional in one month, about 0.6R on a 7% stop) would have been entered. A flat 'funding 7% a year charged to longs' ignores that funding spikes exactly when a trend follower is long.

The mark-price trigger is chosen, not tested. Off-hours mark derives from the order-book EWMA index and the +/-3% deviation cap is unverified. G5 replays on trade '1m bars', not mark-price klines, so the replay does not exercise the trigger the design specifies.

No absolute spread cap and no depth gate. The cost gate 'round-trip fees + spread + slippage allowance <= 5% of stop distance' on a roughly 690 bp stop tolerates about 20 bps of spread on gold, which is a visibly broken book for a one-tick market.

Holds over weekends with the stop live while the 2006-2026 proxy has 'weekend prints ... excluded from indicators' and no weekend bars at all; weekend stop-outs are absent from the evidence and covered by a single replayed weekend.
'No position older than 10 seconds without a confirmed exchange-side stop' holds only while the worker is alive; there is no independent watchdog and no bound on Railway restart time.
The recorder is only 'hourly spread and depth samples', too coarse to build a spread distribution for the 16:00-19:00 and weekend hours it later has to trust.
Hourly spot proxy back to 2006 is unverified; if it fails the design falls back to daily bars and inherits robust-minimal's execution-slot blind spot.
Drills 'live with explicit consent and a few USDT of notional' prove plumbing, not fill quality at real size or under stress.

Protection can travel with the order, which the Binance designs cannot do atomically: 'SL/TP sent with the order where accepted, otherwise attached at once; 3 attempts in 2 s, then immediate close'.

Tester gaps are named and partly plugged: DST rule engine with a live cross-check against server time, CSV news replay with 'a loud news filter inactive log line', real-tick-only final tests, 'fixed delay equal to measured ping, plus one Random Delay run', a Recorder 'to compare live spread by hour with tester spread', and a cross-feed re-test.

Margin-hike headroom is sized to the documented case: 'post-trade margin level at least 400%, so a 4x margin hike does not reach stop-out'. The 'Capital feasibility table at init' disables a module (INFEASIBLE_CAPITAL) instead of rounding up to minimum lot.
Rollover and session discipline: 'no entries 16:00-19:00 New York, none within 15 minutes of a session end', intraday modules 'flat at 15:45 New York', no DLL and no WebRequest.
It states the limit plainly: 'Market-order slippage and liquidity are not modelled ... Live results will be worse than the backtest by an amount only live trading can measure.'
flaws: The strategies most sensitive to execution (M15 and M30 intraday, stops of roughly $10-35) are validated in the tool least able to model it, and the cost stress is 'spread x1.5 and one extra tick of slippage each side'. One tick is $0.01 on gold, so the slippage stress is zero in practice, and it breaks the design's own rule of 'no pips or points anywhere'. A spread multiplier is also not a tester setting in real-tick mode; it needs a custom symbol with rewritten ticks, which is not specified.

The news gate is entry-only. S2 and S4 enter from 03:00 New York with stops as tight as '0.5 x ATR(14, M15)' and then sit through 08:30 releases whose hour range is about 1.5%. There is no flatten or widen before the window, and the tester will fill those stops at price.

'Notional cap 2x equity per position' on intraday gold in a 2.3% daily-ATR regime: a 1% slip through a stop is 2% of equity, about 4R and equal to the whole daily limit. The defence 'trade closed if realised risk exceeds 1.3x planned' is a code path that never executes in the tester, so its live behaviour is untested by construction.

No carry module although S3 holds overnight: long gold swap is 'roughly 5-8% a year', the triple-swap day is never mentioned, the tester 'appear[s] to use today's specification', and G3 has no swap stress.

The weekend rule is cosmetic: 'if it exceeds 2 x the planned 1R, close; otherwise hold'. With stops of 2 x ATR (about 1.9% on H4, 4.6% on D1) and an injected 2% gold gap, the loss is about 1R or less, so the rule never fires.
'Demo parity ... at least 90% of trades match on the bar' measures a demo server. Demo fills are not live fills; the first real execution data arrives only at G12 with money on.

The broker is unknown, so every execution property is hypothetical. The 'real-tick share at least 99%' gate may leave only 1-3 years of history at many brokers, which collides with G3's four calendar sub-periods covering both 2024 and 2026.

Margin hikes applied to open positions, close-only mode and suspended trading on silver are only 'classified' as retcodes; there is no rule for an open position when the broker cuts leverage before news or a weekend.

Platform cost and test surface: Windows host, new language, 13 modules, about 108 features and '60-80 inputs' across netting/hedging and brokers. The journal CSVs and approved_presets.csv it depends on are not retrievable from the MetaQuotes VPS it claims compatibility with.
