unresolved_concerns: Nobody has observed the order mechanics of the Binance metals contracts. exchangeInfo returned HTTP 451 to the researchers, so tick, quantity step, minimum notional, leverage brackets, the account's fee rate, available stop order types, trigger references and price bands (the +/-3% mark deviation cap) are all unverified. Three of the four execution layers are specifications against an API no one in this project has called.

None of the designs uses the cheapest live evidence available: the requester's current bot already sends ccxt create_order('STOP_MARKET', {stopPrice, reduceOnly}) in src/broker.py lines 79-82 and only logs 'SL failed' on error. Its production logs would show today whether the conditional-order route works through ccxt on this account after the reported December 2025 algo-order change, and whether live crypto positions are currently naked.

Stop trigger reference on weekends and off-hours is untested by all. One design picks mark price without evidence, two do not say. The off-hours index method changed on 2026-05-08 and 2026-09-15, so even venue-history replays before September describe a different stop behaviour from the one that would be traded.

Weekend and holiday exposure is absent from every evidence run. All long backtests use spot data with no Saturday or Sunday bars, while the perp trades and the stop is live. No design defines the session bar or the perp index behaviour on CME holidays and early closes (Thanksgiving on 26 November 2026, Christmas and New Year all fall inside any near-term pilot).

The naked-position window on process death is unbounded. Every 'no position without a confirmed stop for more than 5 or 10 seconds' invariant binds only while the worker is alive. There is no atomic bracket on the venue, no independent watchdog process, and the PaaS restart policy has capped retries.

Stop-market fill quality in a crash is assumed (2-10 bps), not measured. No design examines what the venue itself did on 30 January 2026: liquidation cascades, auto-deleveraging, halts or reduce-only states, and whether a silver perp listed three weeks earlier tracked spot. The one replay is at 1-minute resolution on trade bars.

Funding is modelled as a flat annual rate, but it is state-dependent: it spikes when price trends up, which is when a trend follower is long, and longs buy the perp at a premium that later decays. A spot-proxy backtest cannot reproduce this, and no design models funding conditional on trend state or premium at entry.

Eligibility decides everything and is unknown. If the account's jurisdiction is not served, the Python route ends and the CFD fallback brings back the minimum-lot barrier (about $54,000 for a gold slow-trend stop at 0.5% risk). With capital unknown, no design has a validated executable route for a small account outside Binance; the OKX fallback has about a tenth of the volume and equally unknown stop behaviour.

CFD broker reality is unmeasured in all four. No hour-by-hour spread table exists, published spreads are floors, demo fills are not live fills, and the MT5 tester does not model slippage, historical swaps or margin hikes applied to open positions (silver 5% to 20%, order size halved, possible suspension). No design says what to do with an open silver position when the broker goes close-only or raises margin mid-trade, beyond an alert.

Unscheduled shocks are not covered. The 30 January 2026 crash followed an unscheduled announcement; every news defence is calendar-driven and every volatility-shock gate reads closed bars, so it reacts after the move. Only small notional protects, and feature-max allows up to 2x equity per position.

Shared infrastructure limits are ignored. Binance REST weight limits and 429/418 bans are per IP; the new bot would share Railway egress with the 30-pair crypto bot polling every 60 seconds and with other tenants. An IP ban blocks stop maintenance and reconciliation. USDT/USD basis on a USDT-settled contract is also unaddressed.

Silver on the perp is assumed to behave like gold. The XAGUSDT quantity step and minimum notional are unverified, the 0.01 tick is about 2 bps, weekend depth was never measured, and the worst silver weekend range was 5.1%. Any sizing claim for silver is provisional until read from the venue.

Minimum-size drills prove plumbing, not fills. All parity tests run at a few USDT. If capital turns out to be large, market impact and weekend depth are untested; if it is small, step rounding distorts risk and trades are skipped, so the live system differs from the tested one either way.

strengths: Smallest pre-declared search of the four: "N in {20, 55, 120} x k in {2, 3, 4} = 9 cells" plus six one-at-a-time ablations, with the verdict "read on the pre-registered primary cell (N=55, k=3) and on the median of the 9-cell grid, never on the best cell".

Strictest null test on the path to real money: "real pooled total R above the 95th percentile; each side (long, short) at or above the median of its own-side random distribution". Nominal false-pass rate is 5%, against 10% for robust-minimal and portfolio.

Tightest link between evidence and capital: "Tier B never leaves stage 1" (0.10% gold / 0.05% silver), and anything larger needs "t at least 3 and DSR at least 0.95". Weak evidence can never buy more than token risk.
States its own power instead of hiding it: "t of 2 needs a net Sharpe of about 0.45 and t of 3 about 0.67. Clearing tier A is unlikely". I recomputed 0.45 and 0.67 for 20 years; both are right.

Refuses a statistic it cannot support: "PBO is not computed: its method needs many more than 10 trials and the grid is deliberately smaller." This matches the fact-check (N >> 10 required). Portfolio and feature-max both compute PBO on 6-9 configurations.

Cost stress, cross-feed and era checks are gates, not report lines: "fees x1.5, slippage x2, funding 11% a year: primary net expectancy at least 0"; second feed "same sign of net expectancy and total R within 20%"; four fixed windows including 2011-15.

The unsupported intraday idea has no route to capital: SESSION-RB is "not promoted in v1 whatever the result", with a pre-registered expectation of "fail" and the cost arithmetic shown. No forking path.

No signal input that lacks proxy history: "perp volume, funding, premium and order book are safety vetoes and telemetry only". Evidence run (Phase 3) comes before the execution engine (Phase 4), which limits sunk-cost pressure.
Bootstrap is labelled honestly ("read as an optimistic lower bound ... used to size risk, never to prove edge") and the plan has an explicit "What the gates cannot show" section.
flaws: Mis-states the trial bound: "Hard budget: 45 trials ... conservative here because the proxy sample is about 20 years". For the effect size being hunted it is the opposite. My calculation: the zero-skill expected best Sharpe on 20 years is 0.34 for 9 independent trials and 0.50 for 45, both at or above the 0.2-0.4 the literature offers. The budget only protects against a Sharpe-1 illusion.

Low power, so the test mostly cannot tell a small real edge from none. At a true Sharpe of 0.3 on 20 years the 95th-percentile gate alone passes about 38% of the time and t >= 3 about 5% (my calculation). The most likely verdict is Tier C whether or not an edge exists.

Tier B is a dead end with no exit rule. Stage 1 runs for "the longer of 10 closed trades or 3 months" at 0.10% risk, which the design itself calls "tuition"; nothing says what happens when a Tier B strategy is still unconfirmed after years.

Funding model is flat and too kind: "funding 7% a year charged to longs", stress "11% a year". The fact-check puts May-October 2026 at 7-11% a year and January 2026 alone at 4.35% of notional. Funding peaks in rallies, exactly when a trend rule is long, so a constant rate understates it. "No automatic exit in v1".

Drawdown sizing uses an i.i.d. bootstrap ("1,000 resamples ... loss clustering is destroyed") and then feeds it into the risk-per-trade decision and the live halt rule. The design admits the bias but keeps the method.

Proxy gate checks price basis only: "at least 95% of session closes differ by no more than 0.30% (gold) and 0.80% (silver)". 0.80% is about a fifth of silver's daily ATR, there is no agreement test on breakout days, and the overlap is 10 months spanning two index-method changes.

Two gates add little: "at least 6 of 9 cells net positive" counts cells that are the same signal at overlapping lookbacks, and "net non-negative in at least 3" of 4 windows passes 31% of the time for coin flips.

"at least 150 closed trades pooled across both metals" treats trades in two 0.83-0.88 correlated metals as independent. If random entries are drawn independently per metal the null is too narrow: my simulation gives a standard-deviation ratio of 1.29, turning a nominal 5% test into about 10%.

The rule is a channel breakout with a chandelier stop ("candidate ignored until it is at or beyond the entry price"), not the vol-scaled always-in momentum the literature tested. Buy-and-hold and the always-in 12-month sign are computed but no gate uses them.

Live vetoes cannot be validated on the proxy: premium sanity, the stop-distance band ("between 2% and 12% of price for gold") and the spread/cost gate were set knowing the 2026 regime and change the live trade list in ways the 2006-2025 test does not see.

strengths: One live hypothesis with a fixed primary cell ("Primary cell: 63 / 3 / off"), "There is no optimiser", and the grid is "a sensitivity report read by its median, not a search for the best cell".
Mechanical four-way verdict with a real kill outcome: "REFUTED ends the trading project here", and the verdict "follows mechanically from the V2 and V3 rules".
The sharpest single bull-market test in any design: REFUTED if "the result with 2019-01 to 2026-01 removed is negative".
Null benchmark keeps drift exposure constant: "1,000 seeded random-entry runs with the same exits, frequency and long/short mix".
Block bootstrap done properly: "blocks of 5 consecutive trades, 5,000 resamples ... Independent resampling is not used because it removes loss clustering."
Most conservative funding assumption of the three perp designs: "funding of 10% a year charged to longs and nothing credited to shorts; a second run at 25% a year".

Risk above 0.50% / 0.25% is tied to sourced hurdles ("DSR >= 0.95 with the honest trial count" and "pooled t ... >= 3.0"), and the prior is stated: "NOT REFUTED or INCONCLUSIVE is the best realistic outcome".

Evidence run (Phase 2) precedes the shell (Phase 3), and the pre-registration commit must precede "the first full backtest in the repository history". Admits "Live trading tests implementation and cost parity, not edge."
flaws: The bar for live money is p of about 0.10: NOT REFUTED only requires the primary cell to reach "the 90th percentile of the random-entry distribution". Risk then doubles to 0.50% / 0.25% after "at least 6 months and at least 8 closed trades" of execution checks, with no new statistical evidence. Nominal false pass is 10%, about 16% if the null is not synchronised across metals (my simulation).

24 cells plus RANGE-NY is 25 trials. Zero-skill best-of-24 on 16-21 years is a Sharpe of 0.43-0.49 (my calculation), above the 0.2-0.4 prior. "Lifetime trial budget: 45 (MinBTL logic, confirmed)" imports the 5-year, Sharpe-1 bound unchanged.
"fewer than 18 of 24 cells positive" adds almost no falsification power: the cells are one trend signal at overlapping lookbacks, so if the primary is positive most neighbours are.

"fewer than 150 pooled trades" is filed under REFUTED. Too little data is not refutation, and 150 trades in two 0.83-0.88 correlated metals is far fewer independent bets. With "at least 2010-2026" and "8-14 trades a year across both metals" the count is 128-224, so data length may decide the verdict.

The proxy gate is close to vacuous: "identical channel and ATR signals on >= 95% of days". A 63-day breakout fires on a few percent of days, so two feeds that disagree on every trigger still pass. It should measure agreement on trigger days.
Cost stress and side checks are not gates: the 25% funding case is only "a second run", and long and short are "reported" separately with no pass rule. Only one era test binds.

RANGE-NY's promotion gate cannot be met as written: "At least 150 shadow signals" against "One attempt per symbol per day", "XAUUSDT first" and "deleted after 6 months" (about 126 sessions before width and news filters). If met by pooling silver it is still one 6-month regime.

Live gates are untestable on the proxy: the funding gate ("exceeds 0.25R"), depth gate ("<= 1% of resting depth") and spread gate cannot be evaluated on 2005-2025 spot data, so the tested trade list is not the live one.
Post-hoc selection not counted as a trial: "A metal with at least 60 trades and expectancy <= 0 on its own is dropped."
The SUPPORTED tier is decorative: t >= 3 has roughly 4-5% power at a true Sharpe of 0.3, and DSR on 24 highly correlated cells has small cross-trial variance, so it barely deflates.

strengths: The trend signal is the object the literature actually tested: "for L in {21, 63, 252} trading days, m_L = sign(C_t - C_(t-L))", matching the research's 1-, 3- and 12-month blend, with "Fitted parameters: none".
States the inference limit outright: "Expected t is about 0.3 x sqrt(21 years) = 1.4, so the sleeve cannot be significant on its own data. It rests on the multi-market literature prior."

Candidate gates for the intraday sleeves are hard and falsifiable: "t-statistic of mean R >= 3.0", "Deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 using the full ledger count", "at or above the 95th percentile of 1,000 random-entry seeds", positive in high- and low-volatility samples, "a final 12-month holdout opened once".

Bear-market and beta gates on the trend sleeve: "net P&L >= 0 in the 2011-2015 gold bear market", "If shorts lose more than half of what longs earn, the sleeve is classed as long beta and capped at PILOT", and "lower maximum drawdown than exposure-matched buy-and-hold".

Gets the trial bound right where the winner gets it wrong: "The bound is tighter for lower Sharpe targets, so anything below Sharpe 1 is treated as unproven." Its figure of an expected zero-skill maximum of about 1.0 for 30 trials at dispersion 0.5 checks out.

Pre-registration is "hashed and committed before any metal data is pulled"; live falsification rules carry numbers ("rolling 24-month net R falls below the bootstrap 5th percentile"); a null result is accepted in advance.
flaws: Capital escalates on evidence the design says cannot be significant. The sleeve goes to "LIVE-1 (g = 0.5)" after a 12-week pilot and to "LIVE-2 (g = 1.0) only after at least 12 months live with no invariant violation, drawdown inside the bootstrap 75th percentile". That is 1.00% gold risk and a 15% drawdown kill, ten times the winner's Tier B exposure on the same class of evidence, and scaling up after a good year is outcome-conditioned.

The gates are loosest where the money goes. "net Sharpe >= 0.20 over 2005-2026" passes 18% of the time under zero skill (my calculation) and is contaminated by gold's drift; T5 only asks for "the 90th percentile". The t >= 3 gates guard sleeves the author already expects to fail ("well under one in four").

The ledger does not close. "capped at 30 runs: TREND 1 + 6 neighbours, SRB 6, SWEEP 6, ablations 10, reserve 1" already sums to 30, yet BENCH adds a Donchian-20 H4 run and the 5m port, "Each is one ledger entry". Over budget before the first run.

Uncounted second chances: shadow trades are scored "under two cost models", "If it passes only under CFD costs" a CFD adapter is built, and Phase 6 has "Candidate gates are re-run with the measured spread table". Each is another evaluation the DSR count ignores.
PBO is a gate marked [P] on six configurations: "The matrix barely meets the 'many more than 10 trials' requirement". Six is not more than ten; the number is noise.

The only capital-bearing sleeve carries many untested fixed constants the literature does not: the |S| resize rule, the re-entry latch, "improves by at least 0.25 x ATR(D1,20)", "ATR(D1,20) / ATR(D1,250) >= 1.5 halves new-entry risk", the 15% carry veto. The published prior covers none of them, and only 6 neighbours are tested.

Internal contradiction: intraday sleeves trade "only in the direction of sign(S) from TREND-D1", but P1 requires daily-return correlation with the live portfolio "within +/-0.30". The lock builds in the correlation the gate forbids; the design admits "the direction lock makes all sleeves long or short together".

Intraday data is assumed, not confirmed: "M1 bid/ask ... Assumed available from about 2016", while C1 needs "at least 300 trades" and C7 needs 2017-19. SWEEP, at one trade a day after a direction lock, may fail on sample size, not on edge.
Selection and discretion remain: "ablations 10" with "Ablations may only remove a component" leaves open adopting an ablated variant, and promotion needs "a recorded operator sign-off".
Build order invites sunk-cost bias: allocator and execution engine (Phase 2) are built before the trend sleeve is validated (Phase 3).

strengths: Trial counting is automated, not left to discipline: "every tester run appends config hash, dates and results to a common-folder CSV", and live trading needs "the hash listed in approved_presets.csv".

G3 contains a real significance requirement per module: "Bootstrap 5th percentile of mean R above 0 at base cost", "at or above the 95th percentile of 200 random-entry seeds", and "Long-only and short-only mean R each at least -0.05R".
"Complete grid search only, no genetic runs" is the form the PBO paper's method assumes, and the DSR script must reproduce the paper's worked example ("0.9004 at N = 100, 0.9505 at N = 46").
Honest about the ceiling: "most modules will end UNPROVEN at best", and "If no module passes G3, the EA ships as a framework in MONITOR mode" is accepted.

The 45-trial bound is at least applied to the setting it was derived for (about 5 years of data, Sharpe-1 target), and there is a live disable rule with a sample size: "mean R after 50 trades below the 5th percentile of the backtest bootstrap".
flaws: Most hypotheses against the least data: four signal modules plus presets on about 5 years of broker real ticks of unknown depth. t = 3 on 5 years needs a Sharpe of 1.34 (my calculation), so SUPPORTED is unreachable by construction; the design concedes "t of 3 needs about 9 years".

Family-wise error is uncontrolled on the path that reaches real money. UNPROVEN "may trade only at minimum size" after G3 and G4, and S1 (two presets), S2, S3 (two presets) and S4 are tested separately at about 5% each. That is a 19-34% chance (4-8 tests) that at least one zero-edge module trades live. The DSR correction only guards a label nobody will reach.

Parameters are chosen in-sample: "the chosen cell is the centre of the plateau" is picked after viewing a 3x3 grid, where the other three designs fix the primary cell beforehand. Then "A final 6-month holdout is opened once" has no numeric pass criterion.

The plan's own required runs exhaust the budget. S1 has 9 cells and "One alternative preset is declared in advance", S2 has 9, S3 has 2, S4 has 1-3, and G7 runs "Each Tier B filter ... on and off" per module. "at most 9 configurations per module and 45 across the whole project" cannot hold through one honest pass.

The only evidence-backed family cannot be tested or afforded here: T-slow is "reported as not testable on broker history", and S3 "needs an account of roughly $15,000-36,000". The testable preset is "H4, entry channel N = 20", about 3.3 days, not the 1-12 month horizon the literature covers, so citing "Slow trend is the only family with long, multi-source evidence" for it is a misattribution.
Three of four modules are unsupported by the design's own words: S1 "edge itself is unproven", S2 "No published evidence supports it", S4 "The evidence is against it".

The tool of record cannot falsify costs: "swaps appear to use today's specification, and market-order slippage is not modelled", and the stress is "spread x1.5 and one extra tick of slippage each side", a convention. Net-of-cost claims for intraday modules with a few-basis-point gross edge cannot be settled in the tester.
200 random seeds give a 95th-percentile estimate with a rank error of about 1.5 points, so the real test size is anywhere from 2% to 8%. The other designs use 1,000.

The window is one regime pair (a record bull run, then a crash with volatility tripled). "Mean R positive in at least 3 of 4 calendar sub-periods" inside 5 years is not regime evidence, and there is no 2011-2015 bear market in the sample.
G6 is convention on thin data: "efficiency at least 50% and at least 4 of 6 out-of-sample windows profitable" on roughly 6-month windows of a few dozen trades.

Maximum sunk cost before any test: signals arrive in P6 after roughly 11 weeks of plumbing (P1-P5). Tier C unlocks, 60-80 inputs and per-symbol enables (silver "stays disabled unless it passes on its own") are further forking paths.

grafts: From robust-minimal: add the bull-run exclusion as a hard gate, REFUTED if "the result with 2019-01 to 2026-01 removed is negative". The winner's 3-of-4 windows rule lets the result lean entirely on the 2019-2026 run.

From robust-minimal: replace the i.i.d. bootstrap in G4 with the block version, "blocks of 5 consecutive trades, 5,000 resamples", with trades ordered in time across both metals so cross-metal loss clusters are kept.

From robust-minimal and portfolio: harden the funding model. Use 10% a year as base and 25% as a gated stress case, and use "actual funding for 2026" on the overlap instead of a flat 7% / 11%. Make funding state-dependent (higher when the rule is long in a rally).

From portfolio: turn the benchmarks the winner already computes into gates: "lower maximum drawdown than exposure-matched buy-and-hold", and "net P&L >= 0 in the 2011-2015 gold bear market" as an explicit requirement.

From portfolio: add the literature-form signal (sign of 21/63/252-day returns, blended) as a pre-registered comparator, counted as one trial. If the channel rule does not at least match it, the literature prior does not cover what is being traded.

From portfolio: correct the trial-budget statement with "The bound is tighter for lower Sharpe targets" and print the computed zero-skill expected maximum Sharpe for the actual trial count and sample length in the report (0.34 for 9 trials, 0.50 for 45, on 20 years).

From portfolio: strengthen pre-registration to "hashed and committed before any metal data is pulled", and check proxy fidelity on signal state ("sign agreement between spot and perp on at least 98% of days") plus agreement on breakout days, not only price basis.

From portfolio and feature-max: add live falsification rules on performance, not only execution: "rolling 24-month net R falls below the bootstrap 5th percentile", "realised costs exceed 1.5x the model over 20 trades", and "mean R after 50 trades below the 5th percentile of the backtest bootstrap". Add a wind-down date for a strategy that stays Tier B.

From feature-max: bind live to tested with a config hash on every journal row and an approved-preset list, have every run append to the trial ledger automatically, and make the DSR script reproduce the paper's worked example (0.9004 at N = 100, 0.9505 at N = 46) as a self-test.
From robust-minimal: keep the explicit terminal outcome "REFUTED ends the trading project here", and report results per metal as well as pooled, without the post-hoc rule that drops a losing metal.
unresolved_concerns: No design can detect the edge it hopes for. At the literature's Sharpe of 0.2-0.4 on 16-21 years the expected t is 0.8-1.8. My calculation: power is 20-57% at the 95th-percentile gate, 32-71% at the 90th, and 1-12% at t >= 3. All three perp designs therefore put money on 'not refuted', and feature-max has even less data.

The literature prior does not transfer. It is for diversified books of 43-67 markets, vol-scaled and always-in, gross of costs, and it fell to a Sharpe of 0.06 in 2009-2022, which is most of every design's test window. A stop-managed rule on two 0.85-correlated metals is not that object, so the prior for the tested window is close to zero.

Effective sample is a handful of macro regimes (2005-11 bull, 2011-15 bear, 2019-26 bull, 2026 crash), on one price path. Trade-count thresholds such as 150 pooled trades and the bootstraps treat correlated gold and silver trades as independent bets.

Random-entry null construction is unspecified. If entries are drawn independently per metal while the real rule enters both together, the null is too narrow: my simulation gives a standard-deviation ratio of 1.29, so a nominal 5% test runs at about 10% and a 10% test at about 16%. No design says the null preserves cross-metal synchronisation.

Nothing is truly out of sample. Every 'a priori' constant (ATR 20, k = 3, N = 55 or 63, drift guards, shock thresholds, execution slots, stop-distance bands) is being fixed in November 2026 by authors who have seen the full history, and the research itself ran statistics on 2024-2026. Pre-registration stops later tuning; it does not undo that. Only forward data is clean, and at about 10 trades a year it accrues too slowly to matter.

Strategy choice is itself selected on the same history: the channel-breakout form was picked because it is the best-coded published gold EA, and published EAs survive because they backtested well on gold. That selection is not in any trial count.

Spot-proxy to perpetual transfer is unvalidated beyond 10-11 months that include an illiquid launch and two index-method changes. Funding, premium, depth and spread vetoes cannot be backtested before 2026, so the live system differs from the tested one in ways no gate measures.

Funding is treated as a flat annual rate everywhere except the 2026 overlap. It is state-dependent and highest when a trend rule is long (4.35% in January 2026 alone), so every long-side net result is biased upward by an unknown amount.

Tail sizing rests on one observation. The 30 January 2026 session is a single event, bootstrap drawdown percentiles from the trade list cannot represent a tail seen once, and stop fills in that session are assumed, not measured.

Trial budgets are borrowed from a 5-year, Sharpe-1 case and count only formal runs. Informal looks (which N, which k, which window) and re-runs after cost re-measurement are not bounded, and 'at least X of Y cells positive' rules count highly correlated cells as corroboration.

No design defines when to stop for lack of evidence. A trend rule can sit at 'not refuted' or Tier B indefinitely, and decisions to continue or scale will be made on noise because the minimum track record at these Sharpe levels is years to decades.

Key cost inputs are still unverified (the account's real taker fee, minimum notional, step sizes; the exchange API returned HTTP 451 to the researchers), so every cost-gate threshold in the perp designs is computed on assumed values until Phase 0 reads them.

strengths: Fastest first verifiable result of the four: Phase 0 is a 'read-only probe run from the Railway service' taking a 'rough estimate 1-2 days', ending in 'a recorded GO (continue) or NO-GO (jump to Phase 7). This is the first verifiable result.'

The only design with an effort estimate on every build phase (P1 3-5 days, P2 5-7, P3 2-3, P4 7-10, P5 at least 30 calendar days), so the owner can budget and notice slippage. Strategy verdict is claimed in 'roughly two to three weeks of part-time work'.
Evidence is bought before the expensive part: the verdict (Phase 3) precedes the execution engine (Phase 4), and 'The requester decides, with the verdict in hand, whether Phases 4-6 proceed'.
One code path to maintain: the backtester 'imports the same evaluator, sizer and exit pipeline the live loop will use', in the language and deployment the owner already runs.

Phase acceptance is mostly machine-checkable by an AI assistant in CI: 'a hand-computed 10-trade fixture is reproduced to the cent; two runs give an identical journal hash', seven named fault-injection scenarios against 'a simulated exchange', and 'at least 20 scripted lifecycle drills at minimum notional ... 10 forced restarts'.

Its inventory of the current bot is accurate. I checked the archive at /home/user/Basel-Almubarak/pro-scalping-bot.zip: risk.py lines 61-78 compute sl_dist and never use it, record_trade is never called from bot.py, broker.py lines 77-84 only log a failed stop, strategy.py line 56 reads df.iloc[-1], and requirements.txt has ccxt>=4.4.0. The kept/not-kept list is therefore a real scope statement, not decoration.

Avoids building statistics that cannot mean anything ('PBO is not computed: its method needs many more than 10 trials') and does not mislabel a short sample as a refutation ('fewer caps the verdict at tier B').
Cheap operational safety defaults: 'Default run mode MONITOR; live orders require an explicit LIVE_ARMED flag plus the expected account id' and 'MAX_RISK_MONEY is a required input with no default'.
flaws: Estimates are optimistic and self-labelled 'rough'. Phase 4 puts 'Venue adapter, order state machine with protected entry, stop gateway, watchdog, reconciliation loop, daily and drawdown locks, latched flatten, durable store, run modes, single-instance lock, status line and alerts; a simulated exchange for fault injection' into '7-10 days'. The current bot is about 800 lines with no tests, and the simulated exchange must imitate a conditional-order path the design admits is 'not verified here'.

Two gate/phase sequencing errors. G1 is a Phase 1 acceptance item but requires 'A second proxy feed gives the same sign of net expectancy and total R within 20%', which needs the Phase 2 harness and a strategy run (and it is unclear whether that run spends a trial). G5 is evaluated in Phase 3 but requires 'the daily-loss lock fires and survives a restart', and the guard and durable store are Phase 4.

Code built that v1 never uses: 'Session/opening range builder from M1 bars - built and tested, used only by the research strategy'; 'Time stop ... implemented and tested, default OFF'; an EMA200 filter 'default OFF'; a news CSV gate that 'rarely binds ... it ships because the journal tags and any later intraday module need it'. Each is extra test surface and, for the CSV, a recurring manual upkeep task.

SESSION-RB is cost with no decision value: 'Pre-registered expectation: fail' and 'not promoted in v1 whatever the result'. Its data window and minimum sample are not stated; on 11 months of venue data it is inconclusive by construction.

Speculative generality: a venue interface 'so ... a second adapter (OANDA v20, cTrader) can be added later', and a Phase 7 with no effort estimate that brings back the design's own 'about $54,000' minimum-lot problem.

Minimum-equity figures ignore its own floor-to-step rule: 'gold is tradable at 0.5% risk from about $70 of equity and at the 0.10% staging risk from about $350'. With a 0.001 oz step and a 5 USDT minimum notional the smallest legal order is 0.002 oz, about $0.54 at the stop, so by my arithmetic about $108 and $540. Stage 1 silver needs '$1,320', so a small account runs a gold-only book.

Shadow parity verifies little: 'At least 30 calendar days in MONITOR mode with 100% agreement' for an engine trading 'order of several per metal per year' is almost entirely SKIP lines. The entry path is exercised only by drills, and 'at least 3 on a weekend' contradicts 'No new entries from Friday 16:00 to Sunday 19:00', so drills need an unspecified bypass that makes the drilled path differ from the live one.

Long, thin live phase: stage 1 runs 'for the longer of 10 closed trades or 3 months', which at the stated trade rate is one to two years of monthly reconciliation reports at 0.10% risk. The operator control path ('env var or small CLI') is never exercised in an acceptance test.

strengths: Smallest live strategy surface: 'one slow, symmetric, three-parameter trend rule with no optimiser', one venue, 'no MQL5 in v1', no venue abstraction and no second venue.
Evidence before shell, with a hard exit: 'REFUTED ends the trading project here; the shell is then built only if the requester wants it for the existing crypto bot.'

Verdict is mechanical and auditable: 'The verdict follows mechanically from the V2 and V3 rules, and the trial ledger count matches the runs performed', with 'The pre-registration file's commit precedes the first full backtest in the repository history'.

Shell acceptance is concrete: ten named fault injections 'all passing twice', 'The backtest is bit-reproducible', an 'Invariant scan over every simulated trade', and 'A code grep confirms a single order-send function and no path that adds to an open position.'
Operator path is actually tested: V5 requires that 'the operator has exercised EXIT_ONLY and a confirmed flatten'.

Its list of defects in the current bot is accurate (I confirmed all six against the archive, including that close_all() loops over every account position with no retry), and it is the only design that schedules a back-port of the fixes.

Handles the likeliest PaaS failure explicitly: 'If the store is missing while the exchange shows our positions, state is rebuilt, the baseline is flagged as estimated, and entries wait for operator acknowledgement.'
flaws: No effort estimate for Phases 1 to 5. Only Phase 0 has a duration ('about 2 weeks, mostly waiting on the recorder'); everything else is waiting periods (4 weeks shadow, 6 months probe). The owner cannot budget the build.

Slow first result. Phase 0 acceptance is 'No HTTP 451 or 403 from the worker for 14 days. The recorder covers two weekends', and 'If any assumption A1-A6 fails ... no strategy code is written'. A go/no-go read of the venue takes a day; two weeks pass here before the first line of strategy code. A6 is also listed as 'checked in Phase 0' but its test (V0 overlap gate) is in Phase 1.

RANGE-NY cannot pass its own gate in its own lifetime: it needs 'At least 150 shadow signals' but is 'deleted after 6 months', with 'One attempt per symbol per day' on 'XAUUSDT first'. That is at most about 126 trading days before the width, event and trigger filters. The module, its M1 range builder and its calendar CSV are built to be deleted.

A sample-size artefact can end the project: 'REFUTED if ... fewer than 150 pooled trades', while the design expects 'roughly 8-14 trades a year across both metals' on 'at least 2010-2026'. The low end is about 135 trades, which returns REFUTED ('no live trading') without saying anything about edge.

Capital floor contradicts the sizing rule: the bot 'refuses to arm below 500 USDT', but L1 silver risk of '0.125%' is 0.625 USDT at a 13-14% stop, about 4.6 USDT of notional, under the assumed 'min notional 5 USDT'. At the floor, silver is skipped for the whole probe of 'at least 6 months', so the live book is not the tested book.

Fault-injection mechanism is undefined. V4 runs 'on testnet if the symbols exist there, otherwise at minimum order size', and the deliverable is just 'plus the fault-injection scripts'. A live venue cannot be made to reject a stop three times on demand; without a simulator or an injecting wrapper, injections 2, 5 and 7 cannot be run.

Evidence data is unsourced behind a hard gate: 'Candidates: Dukascopy export, OANDA v20 candles; coverage to be confirmed', with 'Median absolute close difference between sources <= 0.05%, no missing weeks'. If it fails, 'the long backtest is not accepted as evidence' and no fallback is given.

The 'minimal' label oversells the shell: 12 modules carrying about 100 relabelled MT5 catalog features, a 24-cell grid, DSR, a PBO it calls 'flagged as noisy at 24 trials', a block bootstrap, and live gates needing order-book depth and funding history.
Operator control is 'changed only by a CLI command on the host' on a PaaS, and storage is still undecided ('SQLite on a Railway volume, or Postgres').

Shadow and probe gates are weak for a ten-trades-a-year engine: '0 unexplained differences between live decisions and next-day replay' over 4 weeks is nearly all SKIPs, and 'at least 6 months and at least 8 closed trades' is realistically about a year.

strengths: The most concrete per-phase acceptance tests of any design: 'A 10,000-case property test shows sizing never rounds up and the verified loss never exceeds budget', 'reproduces a hand-computed 20-trade ledger to the cent, including fees and funding', 'Reruns are deterministic (identical journal hash)', and a fault list that includes 'expired calendar file'.
Pre-registration is ordered before data: the file is 'hashed and committed before any metal data is pulled'.
A null outcome is accepted in advance ('risk engine built, no sleeve cleared for capital'), so the plan does not depend on a pass.
Fails closed on a stale calendar: 'missing or expired file blocks intraday sleeves'.
Honest about time: 'Reaching first pilot capital takes about five to six months of build, validation and paper trading.'
flaws: Execution is built before evidence. Phase 2 (3-4 weeks: allocator, gate pipeline, account guard, execution engine, exit manager, state_ops, status page) comes before Phase 3 TREND validation, so 7 to 9 weeks pass before the first strategy verdict, and 'If any gate fails, the trend sleeve is not traded and the project continues only as research'. Six conjunctive gates (T1-T6) sit on a signal whose 'Expected t is about ... 1.4'.

It schedules weeks of work it expects to discard: 'I expect both to fail on Binance' and the chance of either passing 'is well under one in four', yet Phase 5 is '4-6 weeks build' for SRB, SWEEP, RV-DIAG and two cost models.

Multi-sleeve bookkeeping conflicts with its own recovery model. It runs 'one-way (netting) mode' with 'Each sleeve has its own ownership prefix', per-sleeve stops and targets, and TREND resizes by |S|. On one netted position, per-sleeve quantity cannot be rebuilt from the venue, which breaks 'The venue is the database'. The design concedes this is 'far more code than the requester's current bot'.

Heaviest and least certain data dependency: 'M1 bid/ask with at least 99% coverage inside session windows. Assumed available from about 2016; audited in Phase 1', plus 'two independent feeds, 2005-2026; closes within 0.3% on at least 99% of days'. No source is named.

Trial bookkeeping does not add up. The ledger is 'capped at 30 runs: TREND 1 + 6 neighbours, SRB 6, SWEEP 6, ablations 10, reserve 1', which leaves no room for the four BENCH comparators ('Each is one ledger entry') or the runs 're-run with costs doubled'.
C5 applies PBO to six-run grids and says the matrix 'barely meets the "many more than 10 trials" requirement'. Six is below ten; the gate is computed but meaningless.

Shadow results under the CFD cost model cannot be verified when produced: the spread table comes only in Phase 6 ('8 weeks of recorded spreads on the actual account'). A CFD-only pass then triggers a second adapter and venue.

The |S| resize ('1/3 -> 1 adds back') creates partial positions that fall under minimum size on small accounts; the design admits that below about $2,000 'the live portfolio differs from the tested one'.

Highest ongoing burden: a 'small CLI/HTTP status page' to secure, weekly reconciliation, a 'Monthly scorecard per sleeve', 'quarterly re-validation', an 'annual review of policy constants', and 'LIVE-2 ... only after at least 12 months'.

strengths: The MT5 tester is a ready-made execution simulator, which gives a strong shell test without building an exchange mock: 'At least 10,000 random-entry trades on real ticks across 2024-2026 satisfy every G2 invariant.'
Shell is built and tested before any signal, driven by the S0 random signal.

Known-answer acceptance for the statistics code: 'The Python DSR script reproduces the paper's worked example (0.9004 at N = 100, 0.9505 at N = 46)', and self-tests for '100 oz, 5,000 oz and 1,000 oz contracts, 2- and 3-digit gold'.

P0 produces 'a list of questions for the requester (broker and legal entity, account type and netting/hedging, capital, swap-free or prop account, negative-balance protection)', which no other design asks for.
Says the quiet part itself: 'A single-strategy bot on the same safety core would be cheaper to build and easier to validate.'
flaws: Discards the owner's whole stack: 'The requester's Python/ccxt/Linux PaaS stack does not carry over', the EA 'needs a Windows VPS or the MetaQuotes VPS', the broker is unknown, and Python is still needed offline. That is two languages, two toolchains and a new host.

An AI coding assistant cannot close the loop. Compiling and Strategy Tester runs happen only in a Windows terminal, so every acceptance test in P1 to P8 is executed by hand by the owner, and 'restart tests are run by hand in v1'. There is no CI path.
Slowest by a wide margin: the phases sum to 18-20 weeks plus 'at least 8 weeks of demo', and the first signal-module verdict comes only after about 12 weeks of plumbing (P0-P5).

Scope is not realistic for one person: 'The catalog's 108 "core"-verdict features are always on', 13 modules, 'about 60-80 inputs', four signal modules, Tier C features and a prop-firm profile 'compiled but locked off'. Its own risk list says 'More code means more failure paths and a test matrix of module x account mode x broker.'

It is expensive validation with a foregone result: 'At a Sharpe of 1, t of 3 needs about 9 years, so most modules will end UNPROVEN at best', and T-slow is 'reported as not testable on broker history'. G1 depends on an unknown broker's real-tick depth.

Every tester gap needs custom tooling to maintain: a DST rule engine, a 'CSV news replay', a calendar exporter script, a Recorder EA and cost-stress runs, because the tester has no calendar, 'TimeGMT() equals server time in it', and 'market-order slippage is not modelled'.

Trial budget is incoherent: 'At most 9 configurations per module and 45 across the whole project' cannot hold four modules at 9 cells plus presets, G7 on/off ablations, stress and Random Delay runs. 'every tester run appends' a ledger row, including '200 seeds per comparison'.

The Governor's barrier is a file the operator edits ('the hash listed in approved_presets.csv'), and the design admits 'The approved-preset hash is the only barrier between the tested system and an untested one.'
Capital may make the result a log of skips: 'accounts under about $3,000 will see most signals skipped', and S3 needs 'roughly $15,000-36,000'. Capital is unknown.
Build order starts with S4, a benchmark of which it says 'The evidence is against it'.

The defects are confirmed in the archive, the codebase is about 800 lines, and the bot is live today; this is the cheapest verifiable result available and a rehearsal for the shell. Also check whether its STOP_MARKET orders still succeed on the unpinned ccxt, since the winner itself recalls an unverified move of conditional orders to a separate endpoint.

From robust-minimal: make pre-registration an artefact with an ordering check ('The pre-registration file's commit precedes the first full backtest in the repository history'); from portfolio, hash it before any metal data is pulled. The winner only says thresholds are 'fixed here'.

From robust-minimal: add the three fault injections missing from the winner's seven ('Failed or partial kline fetch: the bar is retried, not skipped', 'A deposit or withdrawal does not move the day's P/L', 'Size below minimum: skipped with a reason') and require every scenario to pass twice in a row.
From robust-minimal: the CI-checkable structural test 'A code grep confirms a single order-send function and no path that adds to an open position.'

From robust-minimal: the lost-store rule ('If the store is missing while the exchange shows our positions, state is rebuilt, the baseline is flagged as estimated, and entries wait for operator acknowledgement'), since a misattached Railway volume is the likeliest PaaS failure.
From robust-minimal: add an operator drill to Phase 5 acceptance ('the operator has exercised EXIT_ONLY and a confirmed flatten'), run from whatever device the owner will really use.

From robust-minimal: replace the winner's iid trade bootstrap in G4 (which it admits destroys loss clustering) with the block bootstrap ('blocks of 5 consecutive trades, 5,000 resamples'); same code size, less optimistic drawdown.
From robust-minimal: treat the side research module the way Keel treats RANGE-NY in the build order ('built last'), or drop SESSION-RB from Phase 3 entirely, so it cannot delay the TREND verdict.

From portfolio: the sizing property test ('A 10,000-case property test shows sizing never rounds up and the verified loss never exceeds budget'). It would also have caught the winner's own minimum-equity arithmetic slip.

From portfolio: if the news CSV gate stays, make it fail closed with an expiry date ('missing or expired file blocks') and add 'expired calendar file' to the fault suite; otherwise remove the gate from the daily engine.
From portfolio: automatic degrade on invariant breaches ('Three invariant violations put the bot in EXIT_ONLY') instead of relying on the owner to read an alert.
From feature-max: a known-answer test for the statistics code ('The Python DSR script reproduces the paper's worked example (0.9004 at N = 100, 0.9505 at N = 46)').

From feature-max: an invariant soak through the execution engine. Drive the simulated exchange with the random-entry mode for 'At least 10,000 random-entry trades' and require zero invariant violations, in addition to the seven scripted faults.

From feature-max and portfolio: stamp the config hash and code commit on every journal row and every trial-registry row ('Config hash of all inputs plus build number stamped on every journal row'), used for traceability of live-versus-replay parity, not as a lock.

From feature-max: put the owner questionnaire in Phase 0 ('a list of questions for the requester'): capital, country of residence, whether sub-accounts are available, and whether the current bot is trading real money.
unresolved_concerns: Nobody checks the checker. In every design the tests, the simulated exchange and the fault injections are written by the same AI assistant that writes the engine. The only human-anchored checks are hand-computed fixtures (10 or 20 trades), and no design says how many owner hours review, drills and reports will take, or what happens if the owner cannot review the code.

Fault-injection fidelity. Whether the Binance testnet lists XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT is unknown, a home-made simulator encodes the author's assumptions about conditional-order behaviour, and live minimum-size drills cannot provoke venue-side rejections. No design defines how the simulator is validated against recorded real responses, so 'no naked position' is proven against a model, not the venue.

The spot proxy history has no confirmed source. 16 to 20 years of New-York-close daily bars (or hourly, or M1 bid/ask) from two independent feeds is assumed by all three Python designs ('coverage to be confirmed', 'Assumed available from about 2016'). The evidence phase's duration, and the fallback if only one feed is obtainable, are not costed.

The first strategy result is inconclusive by construction. Every design expects 'NOT REFUTED', 'tier B' or 'UNPROVEN', so what is actually verifiable is the shell. No design sets a cost-benefit stop rule or a minimum capital below which a 12-module system producing about ten trades a year at 0.1-0.5% risk is not worth building and operating for years.

No cheap first-pass falsification. All four build a custom harness before seeing any number, although a one-day run of the pre-registered daily channel rule on an off-the-shelf backtester could show the order of magnitude (at the price of one trial).

The whole Python plan hangs on one unverified fact: eligibility for Binance TradFi perps in the owner's jurisdiction. The fallback paths (OKX at about a tenth of the volume, or a CFD or MT5 route with the roughly $54,000 minimum-lot problem) have no time or cost estimate in any design.

Dead-bot detection. All alerts and heartbeats are emitted by the bot itself; no design specifies an external dead-man monitor or even the alert channel. The current railway.json has restartPolicyMaxRetries 10, so a service can stay down silently while the trailing stop stops updating.

PaaS assumptions are untested: volume attachment for SQLite, single-replica behaviour during redeploy, region pinning, and how the owner issues EXIT_ONLY or a two-step flatten from a phone at night ('CLI command on the host', 'env var or small CLI').
Event calendar upkeep. Three designs depend on a hand-maintained UTC CSV of NFP, CPI, PCE and FOMC dates; none names the source, the person who updates it or the update schedule.

Dependency upgrades. A pinned ccxt will break when Binance changes an endpoint and an unpinned one changes behaviour silently. No design defines an upgrade procedure, such as re-running the venue probe and the fault suite on every version bump.
Trial-budget discipline is self-policed by the person with the incentive to break it. No design makes the harness refuse to run past the cap or prevents runs outside the harness.

The current live bot stays broken while the new project runs. Its sizing ignores the stop, its daily-loss halt can never fire and a failed stop is only logged. Only one design mentions a back-port, as an optional last phase, and none confirms that a dedicated sub-account is available to keep the two bots' limits apart.

strengths: Smallest exposure of the four, and the stress arithmetic checks out. "Combined open risk at the stops for gold plus silver <= 0.75% at L2" and "Notional caps: 15% of equity per symbol, 25% combined. Expected use is about 7% (gold) and 2% (silver)". I recomputed the 30 January 2026 case: 7.1% x 12% + 1.85% x 31% = about 1.4% of equity, matching its "about 1.5% in total".
Gold and silver are treated as one bet in the limits, not only in prose: "They count as one bet: correlation 0.83-0.88, silver beta about 2", with one position per symbol and silver at half risk.

No averaging path, and the claim is checkable. "a trigger while a position is open is logged SKIP(position_open) and never reverses"; Phase 3 acceptance is "A code grep confirms a single order-send function and no path that adds to an open position". Risk base is "min(wallet balance, equity)", so size shrinks in drawdown.

Best restart-safety specification. "day reference rebuilt from the exchange income history so deposits, withdrawals and restarts cannot reset it"; locks "only escalate, and survive restarts"; "A hard lock latches a flatten that retries until flat"; "A database lock prevents two replicas trading during a Railway redeploy"; and if the store is missing, "entries wait for operator acknowledgement".
Enforceability is gated before live money: ten fault injections "all passing twice", including a kill between fill and stop, a daily lock across restart, and a deposit not moving the day's P/L.

Loss is bounded by frequency as well as size: "at most 1 entry per symbol per NY-day, 2 per day in total, 6 per symbol per rolling 30 days". That caps the monthly loss at stops at about 4.5% (6 x 0.50% + 6 x 0.25%).

Risk is sized from a pessimistic drawdown estimate: block bootstrap with "blocks of 5 consecutive trades" because "Independent resampling is not used because it removes loss clustering". A REFUTED verdict means "no live trading".

Dedicated sub-account, so the worst case is the sub-account balance. It also found that the existing bot's close_all() "closes every position on the account", which I confirmed in src/broker.py lines 122-126.
Funding gate on new entries ("skip if the trailing-30-day funding ... exceeds 0.25R") and a depth gate ("Order notional <= 1% of resting depth within 0.2% of mid").
flaws: The headline invariant cannot be enforced when it matters. "no position without a confirmed server-side stop for more than 5 seconds" holds only while the process is alive; its own test says "on restart the stop is attached within 5 s". The daily lock, the -10% halt and the flatten latch are also in-process. During a Railway outage or an HTTP 451 block, only the resting stop protects the position.

The stop trigger type is never specified (mark or last price), yet positions are "held over weekends and releases by design" on a book with 6-16% of weekday volume and index rules that changed twice in 2026. Weekend safety is argued from bar ranges ("about 0.14% + 0.08%"), not from observed stop fills.

"cross margin inside the sub-account; exchange leverage set to 2x as a hard order-size ceiling" is not a hard ceiling. 2x equity is 8 times the stated 25% notional cap; a sizing bug at that ceiling in a 30 January silver session would lose about 62% of the sub-account. Cross margin leaves the whole sub-account as collateral with no exchange-enforced per-position cap.

Risk doubles on no evidence. "Step-up to L2 only if none fired" after "at least 6 months and at least 8 closed trades", and the NOT REFUTED verdict already allows it. Eight trades show nothing about edge; this is a 0.25% to 0.50% increase on an unproven strategy.

The daily limits cannot bind at this sizing. At about 9% combined notional, the -2.0% hard lock needs a gold-equivalent move of roughly 22% in a day. The limits that can fire are per-trade risk, the frequency cap and the -10% halt. There is no weekly or monthly loss limit.

Funding is an uncapped loss while in a position: "the gate limits new entries only". At January 2026 levels (4.35% of notional in a month) a held gold long loses about 0.6R a month and no limit reacts.

The "permanent halt at -10% (... manual re-arm only ...)" has no cap on re-arms and no cooling-off period. If the store is lost, "the baseline is flagged as estimated", so the high-water mark can be reset downward; it is not rebuilt from income history.

All sizing evidence (V2, V3) comes from spot daily bars and modelled fills: "The overlap gate checks signals, not costs in past regimes". "Loss per event <= 2% of equity" is therefore a model output, not a measured venue result.

API key permissions and IP restrictions are not mentioned. At the 500 USDT floor in the probe stage, the silver order (about $4.6 notional by my arithmetic) falls under the reported 5 USDT minimum, so the probe tests gold only.

strengths: The only design with a loss cap that survives a dead process and an unfilled stop. "Isolated margin, exchange leverage 3x for gold and 2x for silver. Before each order: estimated liquidation distance at least 2x the stop distance, and free margin after the order at least 50% of equity". At default sizing the exchange limits loss to roughly 2.4% (gold) plus 0.95% (silver) of equity (my arithmetic: notional divided by leverage).

Stop mechanics are specified: "reduce-only exchange stop triggered on mark price", a premium sanity gate ("|mark - index| / index <= 0.5% gold, 1.0% silver"), and "A stop already through the market means close now".
Most conservative link between evidence and risk: "Stage 1: 0.10% gold / 0.05% silver" and "Tier B never leaves stage 1". An unproven edge never exceeds 0.10% per trade.

Hard money ceiling outside the percent logic: "MAX_RISK_MONEY per trade is a required input with no default (start fails without it)". Correlated book capped: "Same-direction gold + silver open risk capped at 0.75% of equity".
Blast radius limited: "separate Binance sub-account with its own trade-only API key". It also raises "an alert" on "A change in leverage brackets or margin rate versus the previous day".

Stress and restart tests use venue data and real orders: replay "on Binance 1m bars ... stop fills taken at the worst price of the minute after trigger", and "at least 20 scripted lifecycle drills at minimum notional, including at least 3 on a weekend, 3 across a funding timestamp and 10 forced restarts".
No averaging: "the exposure cap is one position per symbol and adds are not implemented"; "Risk-reducing actions are never blocked by any gate, lock or limit".

Its reading of the existing bot is accurate. I confirmed in the archive that position_size() ignores the stop distance (src/risk.py lines 61-78), record_trade is never called (src/bot.py line 175) and a failed stop-loss is only logged (src/broker.py lines 77-84).
flaws: "Total notional capped at 0.5x equity" is twice the robust-minimal cap and too loose as a bug backstop. At that cap a 30 January silver session costs about 15% of equity, more than its own "-10% from the persisted equity high-water mark" kill, in one session.

No funding protection, not even on entry: "Alert when the trailing 7-day funding against the position annualises above 25%. No automatic exit in v1." Its own text says funding "is 10x the fee cost and can consume a small edge".

Risk is knowingly sized from an optimistic drawdown estimate: "Bootstrap of trade results in R (1,000 resamples; read as an optimistic lower bound because loss clustering is destroyed)", then used as the 8% gate.

Orphan handling leaves a real position unmanaged: "a position the bot has no record of is never adopted or closed". In a dedicated sub-account, a no-record position after store loss is the bot's own. It gets no trail and no watchdog close, and the text does not say the latched flatten covers it.

The G5 pass condition contradicts itself. It requires "account loss is at most 3x planned open risk" (at most 2.25%) and that "the daily-loss lock fires" (which needs -1.6% to -2.0%). At the design's own sizing the replay loses about 1.4%, so the lock cannot fire; the gate either fails a safe result or gets waived.

Looser naked-position tolerance than robust-minimal: "No position older than 10 seconds without a confirmed exchange-side stop", with halt-and-review only at "more than 60 s". Like the others it is in-process only.
No weekly loss limit and no rolling entry cap beyond "at most 1 entry per symbol per session day". A whipsaw month is bounded only by the -10% kill.

Close-then-reverse on an "opposite fresh breakout" doubles order traffic at turning points, when books are worst. The close is verified, so it is not averaging, but it is one more failure path that robust-minimal avoids.

strengths: The right principle is stated and used: "the notional caps are the only defence that does not depend on a fill". Caps are derived from total stop failure: "XAU <= 20% of equity, XAG <= 8% ... loss = 2.4% + 2.5% = 4.9%".
Explicit correlated-exposure limit: "XAU and XAG are one bucket: |N_XAU + 2 x N_XAG| <= 40% of equity".
Staged capital with automatic demotion: "SHADOW 0, PILOT 0.25, LIVE-1 0.5, LIVE-2 1.0", "Demotion is automatic", and "At 60% of the kill level the stage is halved".
Has a weekly loss limit ("2% / 3% / 4%") beside the daily one, plus a portfolio gate that the "probability of reaching the drawdown kill within 3 years <= 10%".
Regime logic only reduces: "It never routes between strategies and never scales size up."
flaws: Hidden averaging, contradicting its own claim. "When |S| changes without a sign flip the position is resized: 1 -> 1/3 closes two thirds; 1/3 -> 1 adds back". That re-adds to an open campaign that can be under water, after realising a loss on the cut. There is no cumulative loss cap per campaign, so repeated 21-day flips can lose more than one risk unit. The same document says "The allocator forbids adding to a losing position in code".

Permanently exposed. S only takes "-1, -1/3, +1/3, +1", never zero, so the trend sleeve is always in the market (about 14.5% gold and 3.8% silver notional at full stage). It always carries gap and funding risk.

Stacking by construction: "Intraday sleeves trade only in the direction of sign(S) from TREND", with "Intraday notional ... XAU <= 30% of equity" on top of the carried position. At its own bucket cap (24% gold plus 8% silver) the 30 January scenario costs about 5.4% by my arithmetic. That breaches its own P3 gate, "loss <= 5% of equity with total stop failure".

No account isolation. Settings are "one-way (netting) mode, cross margin ... clientOrderId prefixes as the ownership key", with no sub-account. The existing crypto bot shares that wallet, and its close_all() closes every position on the account (confirmed). Equity-based daily, weekly and drawdown limits would be driven by crypto P/L, and metals collateral sits behind crypto liquidations.

Loosest limits of the four: "Total open risk at stops: 2.0% of equity" (2.7 times robust-minimal) and a drawdown kill of "4% / 8% / 15%". Full stage rests on tests it calls "non-contradiction, not proof".

Restart safety is asserted, not specified. State is "written atomically" but no durable medium is named and no Phase 0 storage check exists. On a PaaS with an ephemeral disk the "persisted lock" and high-water mark vanish on redeploy.

Several sleeves with separate reduce-only stops and targets on one netted position create orphan-order risk (a leftover intraday stop cutting the trend position). The design admits "Bugs in sizing, duplicate entries or lost state are the realistic way to lose money quickly".
Tolerates repeat failures: "Three invariant violations put the bot in EXIT_ONLY", so two naked-position events pass without action.
Intraday stops of 40-70 bps at 0.25% risk imply 36-62% of equity in notional before the 30% cap. A 2% slip through the stop at the cap costs about 0.6%, more than twice the planned loss.

strengths: Broker-side stop attached to the position: "SL/TP sent with the order where accepted, otherwise attached at once; 3 attempts in 2 s, then immediate close; trade closed if realised risk exceeds 1.3x planned". On MT5 the stop belongs to the position, so there is no separate stop order to orphan.
The only design that budgets for broker margin hikes: "post-trade margin level at least 400%, so a 4x margin hike does not reach stop-out".

Limits are coherent with each other: "At most 2 entries per symbol and 3 in total per day" keeps the day's loss at stops under the 1.6% trigger. It has a weekly limit ("4.0%: EXIT_ONLY") and a 10% total lock triggering at 9%.
Good persistence detail: locks "mirrored to a file because terminal globals expire after about four weeks", and "a restart cannot grant a fresh loss budget".
Explicit weekend rule for held positions: "compute the loss from a 2% (gold) or 4% (silver) adverse gap with OrderCalcProfit; if it exceeds 2 x the planned 1R, close".
One position per symbol and no signal blending: "Adding to a loser and multiplying lots after a loss are impossible in this code".
flaws: Gap sensitivity is 15 to 25 times the Binance designs. "Notional at most 2x equity per position", and with its own "gold intraday stops are about $10-35 per ounce", 0.5% risk means 0.55 to 1.9 times equity in gold. A 2% slip costs about 4% of equity. A stop not honoured in a 12% session costs about 23% on one position. The 1.6% daily trigger cannot stop a single-trade gap.

The only design where loss can exceed the deposit: "whether the account has negative-balance protection is unknown", and broker, account type and capital are all unknown. At 2x notional and 5% margin, a 50% stop-out fires only after about 95% of equity is gone (my arithmetic). Offshore leverage of 1:1000-1:2000 would not stop a sizing bug.

Risk-increasing paths are compiled in behind flags. "Tier C, locked off: 'Guarded minimum-lot fallback with a second risk cap' (1.5x base, every use counted)" is a round-up-to-minimum-lot path. It contradicts "never rounded up" and its own G2 gate "Minimum-lot round-ups: 0". Small accounts where "most signals are skipped by design" are where that switch gets flipped.
Duplicate-instance protection is off by default: "Tier C, locked off: 'Single-instance lock with heartbeat'".

Capital protection cannot be validated with the chosen tool. The design admits "market-order slippage is not modelled" and "swaps appear to use today's specification". G10 ("Replay 30 January 2026 ... Pass: no stop-out") therefore runs in a tester that fills stops at the tick price, and proves nothing about gaps.
Unproven modules still trade real money: "UNPROVEN (may trade only at minimum size)" means live at 0.25% risk, and it expects "most modules will end UNPROVEN at best".

Largest failure surface: 13 modules, about 108 features and "60-80 inputs", where "The approved-preset hash is the only barrier between the tested system and an untested one". All account locks run inside one terminal on one Windows host.

Aggregate notional across both metals has no numeric cap (only "Combined open risk ... at most 1.0%" at stops). The slow trend signal is delivered "at the first tick after 19:00 New York", straight after the thinnest hours.

grafts: From platform-pragmatic: isolated margin per position (gold 3x, silver 2x, auto-add-margin off) with its check "estimated liquidation distance at least 2x the stop distance". This replaces cross margin and gives an exchange-enforced cap of roughly notional divided by leverage (about 2.4% plus 0.95% of equity) that holds with the process dead and the stop unfilled.

From platform-pragmatic: state the stop as "reduce-only exchange stop triggered on mark price" and add the premium gate "|mark - index| / index <= 0.5% gold, 1.0% silver". Add "A stop already through the market means close now".

From platform-pragmatic: tie risk to evidence. Use "Stage 1: 0.10% gold / 0.05% silver" and "Tier B never leaves stage 1" in place of the step-up to 0.50% / 0.25% after 8 trades on a NOT REFUTED verdict.

From platform-pragmatic: "MAX_RISK_MONEY per trade is a required input with no default", a "trade-only API key" for the sub-account, and the alert on a "change in leverage brackets or margin rate versus the previous day".

From platform-pragmatic: replay 30 January 2026 and the worst weekend "on Binance 1m bars ... stop fills taken at the worst price of the minute after trigger". Add the lifecycle drills "at least 3 on a weekend, 3 across a funding timestamp and 10 forced restarts" and the daily fee and funding reconciliation "within 0.5% per day".
From platform-pragmatic: the stop-distance band (skip when 3 x ATR is under 2% of price for gold or 4% for silver), so a quiet regime cannot inflate notional just before a shock.

From portfolio: a weekly loss limit and graduated de-risking, "At 60% of the kill level the stage is halved; restoring it needs operator action". Robust-minimal currently has nothing that can fire between the per-trade stop and the -10% halt.

unresolved_concerns: No independent dead-man's switch. In all four designs the daily and weekly locks, the drawdown kill, the flatten latch and the naked-stop watchdog run inside the one bot process. During a host outage, an HTTP 451 region block, an API ban or a key revocation, nothing can flatten and only the resting stop protects. The Binance designs alert on state changes and heartbeat daily; none pages the operator within minutes or runs a second watchdog on another host with its own key.

A stop-market order is not a loss limit, and none of the designs has evidence of how these venues fill stops in a gap. Nobody measures how conditional stops on XAUUSDT and XAGUSDT triggered and filled on 30 January 2026 or on thin weekends under the order-book index introduced on 2026-05-08 and changed on 2026-09-15. The mark-price deviation cap is unverified. Every stress figure is arithmetic on bar ranges or modelled fills.

Venue and counterparty loss is unbounded by any rule. All of the bot's equity sits in USDT on one 11-month-old product, exposed to insolvency, withdrawal freezes, a stablecoin de-peg, auto-deleveraging, or forced settlement after a delisting or eligibility change. None of the designs caps the share of the requester's total capital on the venue or sweeps unused collateral off it, although positions use under a quarter of equity. Feature-max has the same gap with an unknown broker and unknown negative-balance protection.

No lifetime loss budget. Capital, account type and jurisdiction are unknown, so percent-of-equity limits bound a sub-account, not the person. Every "permanent" drawdown lock is cleared by the operator with no cap on re-arms, no cooling-off period and no rule against topping up after a kill. Ruin by repeated 10% or 15% instalments is not addressed.

The largest live risk to the requester's capital today is the existing crypto bot, and none of the designs makes fixing or pausing it a precondition. I confirmed in /home/user/Basel-Almubarak/pro-scalping-bot.zip that sizing ignores the stop (src/risk.py lines 61-78: notional = balance x 1% x leverage 10 per trade, max_positions 5), that record_trade is never called so the 5% daily stop cannot fire (src/bot.py line 175), that a failed stop-loss is only logged (src/broker.py lines 77-84), and that positions live only in memory while railway.json restarts on failure up to 10 times. After each restart the already-in-position check and the max-positions count reset, which is an accidental stacking path. Robust-minimal and platform-pragmatic call the fix optional; portfolio and feature-max ignore it. None models the joint drawdown of the crypto and metals books in a dollar-liquidity shock.

Funding is an uncapped slow loss while a position is open. Robust-minimal and portfolio gate new entries only, platform-pragmatic only alerts, and feature-max pays swap with no rule. At January 2026 levels (4.35% of notional in a month, prints of 0.5% per 4 hours) a held long loses about 0.6R a month without tripping any daily limit. None of the designs caps cumulative loss per position across price, funding and fees.

Silver's tail is under-modelled. All designs size silver at half risk on a beta of about 2 and cap combined risk at the stops. On 30 January 2026 silver moved about 2.6 to 3 times gold, and the short side faces squeezes like October 2025 and the January 2026 run. Margin changes applied to open positions (CME 9% to 18%, one broker 5% to 20%) can force a cut at the worst moment; only feature-max budgets headroom and only platform-pragmatic alerts.

API key compromise is not treated as a capital risk. Keys sit in PaaS environment variables, usually without a static IP for whitelisting. Only platform-pragmatic specifies a trade-only key. A leaked trade-only key can still drain an account through trades in illiquid contracts, and none of the designs addresses that.

The lock-state store is a single point of failure in every design. Losing it estimates or resets the high-water mark and day baseline (robust-minimal: "flagged as estimated"; platform-pragmatic: the position becomes FOREIGN; portfolio: medium unspecified; feature-max: a file and terminal globals on one host). None rebuilds the high-water mark from exchange income history or keeps an off-box copy, and only robust-minimal fails closed when the store is missing.
